result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue (the "/" flagship instrument) and its colocated composables/controls/styles/tests
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Matches the explicit Opus 5 declaration this seat was spawned with; the seat is declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the hero readout is a lying instrument. `ColorComponentDisplay.vue:21-39` puts `contenteditable="true"` on a span whose children Vue owns and patches; any user edit replaces those child nodes, orphaning the cell from the vdom permanently. Reproduced live: after typing `45` into the L cell and then driving the L slider 12 steps, the URL, the page title, and the channel meter all read `43.8` while the hero readout — the largest element on the page, at 11.65cqi of Fraunces display type — still inks `45`, with `innerHTML` = `45`. It never recovers.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this field records the hazards that were checked and NOT found, so the positive findings are not mistaken for a shotgun. (1) `defineModel()` staleness — ABSENT and correctly cured: `grep -rn "defineModel" demo/picker/` returns only the comment at ColorPicker.vue:167 recording its removal; the picker injects the App-owned ShallowRef via COLOR_MODEL_KEY (:172-173), writes are synchronous. (2) oklch→HSV hue loss — `stableHue` remains source of truth with the `s*v > 0.01` guard (useColorPipeline.ts:75-97); the picker never writes it. (3) ValueUnit nesting — `grep -rn "ValueUnit" demo/picker/` returns 0 hits. (4) Ungated rAF / PRM-RAF epidemic — the only requestAnimationFrame in demo/picker is SpectrumCanvas.vue:100, a single-shot coalescer, cancelled at :196 (pointerup) and :217-220 (onUnmounted); not a loop, not a site. (5) reka-ui pointer-capture leak recovery — PRESENT: useSliderTouchGates.ts:81,91-92,117,124 wires pointercancel + lostpointercapture + a document-level release. (6) Eager WebGL on the critical path — correctly deferred: defineAsyncComponent + useIdleReady, gated `v-if="blobReady && ornamentOpen"` (ColorPicker.vue:94-95,157-158). (7) verbatimModuleSyntax — compliant; ColorPicker.vue:125,128 are both `import type`, no mixed value/type import in the file. (8) Layout — REPORT.md:78-88 records horizontalOverflow 0, blankOrNearBlank 0, mainCountNotOne 0, darkClassMissing 0 across all 60 captures.

defects.defect: The hero readout renders `contenteditable="true"` on a span whose children Vue owns and patches (`.fig-int`/`.fig-frac`). Any user edit replaces those nodes; every later patch writes into detached nodes and silently no-ops, so the cell is permanently orphaned from the vdom and displays a value that is not the color.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/display/ColorComponentDisplay/ColorComponentDisplay.vue:21-39. Live Playwright probe against http://localhost:9000/#/ returned: {"afterTyping":["45","20.1","10"],"afterTypingInnerHTML":"45","afterSliderDrag_cells":["45","20.1","10"],"afterSliderDrag_innerHTML":"45","afterSliderDrag_meter":["43.8%","20.1","10.0","100.0%"],"url":"http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(43.8%25+20.05+10)"} — URL, page title and channel meter all say 43.8; the hero readout says 45. The `` wrapper proves the browser destroyed Vue's two child spans (and that the field accepts arbitrary rich text/paste).
defects.mechanism: Vue-controlled subtree made user-writable: contenteditable lets the browser mutate DOM that the virtual DOM believes it owns, so vnode-held element references go stale and patching becomes a no-op.
defects.reproduction: 1) Open http://localhost:9000/#/ . 2) Click the `l` readout cell, press Cmd+A, type `45`, wait 1200ms. 3) Focus the L channel slider thumb (`.channel-slider [role="slider"]` first) and press ArrowLeft 12 times. 4) Read `document.querySelectorAll('.readout-fig')[0].innerText` (= "45") against `location.href` and `.channel-meter` (= 43.8%).
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, already half-ordered by W48 §Work-1: delete the contenteditable path entirely; render the tuple as a read-only numeric headline and put editing in real `<input type="number">` controls. A Vue-controlled subtree may never be contenteditable — there is no patch that makes it safe. Also strengthen W48's completion gate: its `agree in one settled routed frame` check is single-frame and would pass with this defect fully present; it must edit a cell, then change the color by an independent path, then assert agreement.

defects.defect: All five channels share ONE 500ms debounce timer instance, so a numeric edit to channel A silently cancels a pending edit to channel B. User edits are lost with no error and no visual signal.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useColorPipeline.ts:209 (`const updateColorComponentDebounced = debounce(updateColorComponent, 500)`) over the single-timer closure at demo/shared/utils.ts:22-44; both ColorPicker.vue:51 and ColorPicker.vue:233 route every channel through that one instance. Unit repro via `npx tsx`: an `l` write at t=0 and an `a` write at t=100ms produced `applied writes: [[80,"a"]]` — the `l` write never executed. Live repro from `lab(80% 20 30)`: typed `30` into `l`, then 120ms later `10` into `b`; final `url":"http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(80%25+20+10)"` — b took 10, l is still 80, the `30` is gone.
defects.mechanism: Debounce over a multiplexed argument: the primitive assumes successive calls express the same pending intent, but the `component` argument makes each call a distinct intent, so coalescing them is data loss rather than throttling.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(80%25+20+30) . Click the `l` readout cell, Cmd+A, type `30`. Within 500ms click the `b` cell, Cmd+A, type `10`. Wait 1.5s and read location.href — it reads lab(80% 20 10); the l edit is discarded.
defects.proposedCure: Key the debounce per channel (`Map<string, debounced>`) — or, KISS and preferred with C-1's cure, drop the debounce entirely: real `<input>` editors commit on change/blur and need no coalescing. Note W48 §Work-3 makes 'W21 numeric fields the sole editors' without noticing this, so landing those fields on the same shared instance would reship the defect in new markup.

defects.defect: The window keydown listener is registered in `onMounted` while the component lives inside `<KeepAlive>`, so `onUnmounted` never fires on deactivation. The listener stays live on every other route and calls `e.preventDefault()`, hijacking Cmd+K app-wide.
defects.evidence: ColorPicker.vue:376-385 (onMounted/onUnmounted) under demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120-127 (`<KeepAlive :max="6">`), mounted at demo/color-picker/App.vue:101-110. Live probe after SPA-internal navigation to #/gradient: {"afterSwitch":{"hash":"#/gradient","pickerInDom":false,"gradientPresent":true},"events":[{"k":"Meta","meta":true,"dp":false},{"k":"k","meta":true,"dp":true}],"pickerExpanded":"absent"} — the picker is NOT in the document yet its handler still ran and still returned defaultPrevented=true. The correct idiom is used in the same directory: demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:246 uses onActivated() and explains why at :232-245.
defects.mechanism: KeepAlive lifecycle mismatch: mount/unmount hooks used where activate/deactivate hooks are required, so a global side effect outlives the component's visible lifetime.
defects.reproduction: 1) Load http://localhost:9000/#/ and wait for the picker to mount. 2) `location.hash = '#/gradient'` (SPA route change, no reload); wait 2.5s; confirm `document.querySelector('.title-row button')` is null. 3) Install a window keydown logger, press Meta+k. 4) The logged event has defaultPrevented === true. Cmd+K is now swallowed on /gradient, /browse, /extract, /mix, /generate, /atmosphere, /blob and all five /admin/* routes.
defects.proposedCure: Move the listener to `onActivated`/`onDeactivated`, and re-scope the shortcut off `window` onto the picker's own subtree so it cannot be a global keyboard claim in the first place.

defects.defect: `onStartEdit` calls the throwing `parseColor` on untrusted, API-sourced palette CSS with no guard, from inside a bare setTimeout that Vue's ErrorBoundary cannot catch. The throw leaves `preEditModel` populated and `editTarget` null — the edit machine wedges and the click is dead.
defects.evidence: ColorPicker.vue:282-289; `parseColor` -> `parsePickerColor` throws at demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:109-113. Call site is demo/color-picker/composables/usePaletteWiring.ts:113-122, inside `setTimeout(...)` — outside Vue error propagation, so `<ErrorBoundary>` (App.vue:50) cannot catch it. Measured parser behaviour via `npx tsx` against src/css/index.ts: "oklch()" THREW TypeError Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace'); "light-dark(#fff, #000)" NOT-OK; "color-mix(in oklab, red, blue)" NOT-OK; "currentcolor" NOT-OK; "#12345" NOT-OK. The same hole exists on the second exposed entry point: useColorPipeline.ts:182-188 (`applyExternalColor`) parses unguarded and usePaletteWiring.ts:122-123 calls it directly — while onPaletteAddColor/onPaletteApply/applyColorString (useColorPipeline.ts:212-257) DO try/catch, showing the guarding is inconsistent.
defects.mechanism: A throwing parse wrapper with no single enforced boundary: half the call sites remember to catch, half do not, and the unguarded ones sit in async callbacks outside the framework's error path.
defects.reproduction: Parser class is reproduced directly: `npx tsx -e 'import {parseCssColor} from "/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/src/css/index.ts"; parseCssColor("oklch()")'` throws TypeError. End-to-end: a stored palette color of `color-mix(in oklab, red, blue)`, `light-dark(#fff,#000)`, `currentcolor` or `oklch()` returned by api.color.babb.dev, then clicking that swatch's edit affordance, hits ColorPicker.vue:286 unguarded. (Full end-to-end not driven live — the local API is CORS-blocked in this dev config per REPORT.md:17 — so the end-to-end arm is labelled a hypothesis; the parser arm is measured.)
defects.proposedCure: Collapse the parse boundary to one place: return the `Result` the library already produces and let call sites branch, instead of a throwing wrapper. Until then, guard onStartEdit and applyExternalColor and surface a real failure to the user rather than an unhandled window error.

defects.defect: The Cmd+K handler tests global modifier STATE (`keys.cmd?.value && keys.k?.value`) rather than the event, so any key pressed while Cmd and K are physically held is preventDefault'd and re-toggles the dropdown. There is also no `e.repeat` guard.
defects.evidence: ColorPicker.vue:263-266. Live probe: hold Meta, hold k (dropdown opens, aria-expanded="true"), then press `a` -> {"A_afterKdown":"true","A_afterOtherKey":"false","A_events":[{"k":"a","meta":true,"rep":false,"dp":true}]}. Cmd+A (Select All) is swallowed AND the color-space dropdown toggles shut on an unrelated keystroke.
defects.mechanism: Chord detection via sampled global key state instead of event inspection — the predicate is true for the whole duration the keys are held, not for the one event that is the chord.
defects.reproduction: On http://localhost:9000/#/ : page.keyboard.down('Meta'); page.keyboard.down('k'); (dropdown opens) ; page.keyboard.down('a'); page.keyboard.up('a'). The keydown for `a` reports defaultPrevented=true and the trigger's aria-expanded flips true->false.
defects.proposedCure: Test the event: `if (e.key === "k" && (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && !e.repeat)`. The `useMagicKeys()` import (ColorPicker.vue:123,247) then has no remaining consumer and is deleted with it.

defects.defect: The four channel slider thumbs are 12 CSS px wide at every viewport — WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (Target Size Minimum, 24x24) fails four times. The picker contributes half of the entire application's small-tap-target count on all 60 audit captures.
defects.evidence: Measured live over the `.pane-shell` subtree at 390x600: [{"tag":"span","role":"slider","w":12,"h":24,"name":"L channel"}, ...A, B, ALPHA identical]. These are exactly the rows in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json for `/` desktop ({"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"L channel"} x4 of 8 smallTapTargets) and mobile ({"w":12,"h":44} x4) — REPORT.md:90-151 shows 8 on every one of the 60 captures. The touch rung at demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:345-357 grows the SliderRoot's vertical hit box (`block-size: max(100%, 2.75rem)`, `inset-inline: 0`) and never touches the thumb, which is why h goes 24->44 on coarse pointers while w stays 12.
defects.mechanism: Hit-area extension applied to the wrong box: the pseudo-element grows the track root on one axis only, while the element carrying role="slider" and the actual grab affordance is the 12px thumb.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/ and evaluate `[...document.querySelectorAll('.channel-slider [role="slider"]')].map(e=>{const r=e.getBoundingClientRect();return {w:r.width,h:r.height,name:e.getAttribute('aria-label')}})` — four entries, all w=12.
defects.proposedCure: Add an inline hit extension on the thumb (`::before` with `inline-size: max(100%, 24px)`), and put it in glass-ui's spectrum-slider primitive rather than as a fifth demo override in ComponentSliders.vue's already-unscoped style block (owner edicts 4 and 5). No wave currently owns this: W48 §Work-4 covers aria-valuetext and meter live-ness but not target size, and W46's PR-12 names Dock/tab/swatch glyphs, not sliders.

defects.defect: `useHeaderCondense` is structurally unreachable: its sufficiency gate demands more scroll overflow than the picker card can ever produce, because the header is itself the dominant term in the card's height. 127 LoC plus six CSS rule blocks are dead at every witnessed viewport.
defects.evidence: ColorPicker.vue:186-195 wires it; the gate is demo/picker/composables/useHeaderCondense.ts:93-99 (`savings = expandedH - (condensedH || expandedH * 0.5)`; `if (overflow <= savings + threshold) return`). Measured live at 390x600, the tightest band that produces overflow at all: {"viewport":[390,600],"expandedHeaderH":184,"overflow":64,"threshold":16,"gateRequires_overflow_gt":108,"gateOpens":false}. At the audit's own reference sizes the overflow is ZERO: {"A_freshMobile_before":{"cardOverflowY":"auto","scrollHeight":586,"clientHeight":586},"B_desktop":{"cardOverflowY":"visible","scrollHeight":683,"clientHeight":683}}. Scrolling the card its full 64px (scrollTop=64) leaves condensedClass=false. Dead surface: useHeaderCondense.ts (127 lines), demo/picker/header.css lines 75/82/100/116/128, the sentinel div at ColorPicker.vue:12, the $el-unwrapping computed at ColorPicker.vue:189-192, the class binding at ColorPicker.vue:25.
defects.mechanism: A self-defeating predicate: the gate refuses to condense unless overflow exceeds roughly half the header, but the header is the largest single block in the scroll content, so that threshold outruns the residual overflow at every band where the picker is usable.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/ at 390x600, then evaluate: `const c=document.querySelector('.pane-shell .card'), h=document.querySelector('.picker-header'); ({overflow:c.scrollHeight-c.clientHeight, H:h.getBoundingClientRect().height, required:h.getBoundingClientRect().height*0.5+16})` -> overflow 64, H 184, required 108. Set c.scrollTop=300, wait 900ms: `.picker-header` still has no `is-condensed` class.
defects.proposedCure: Delete it (owner edicts 2 and 3). If the whole-header contraction is still wanted, it needs a mechanism that is not 'condense only when there is enough overflow to sustain condensing'. W48 orders deleting the seat.css:88 title-row reservation and the readoutReservation two-line lock but leaves this apparatus standing.

defects.defect: The picker cancels its parent's shared, app-wide debounced writes on its own unmount — an ownership inversion that silently drops in-flight color changes belonging to sibling components.
defects.evidence: ColorPicker.vue:381-385 calls `parseAndSetColorDebounced.cancel()` and `updateColorComponentDebounced.cancel()`. Both are created by useColorPipeline in App.vue (useColorPipeline.ts:92 and :209) and provided app-wide via COLOR_MODEL_KEY; other consumers are ComponentSliders.vue:115, ConsoleRail.vue:115, HeroBlob.vue:56 and demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue. The pane KeepAlive is `:max="6"` (App.vue:104) over 7 distinct left panes (color-picker, browse, extract, generate, gradient, atmosphere, admin-*), so the picker IS LRU-evictable. The parse debounce window is 2000ms (useColorParsing.ts:92).
defects.mechanism: A child disposing state it did not create: cleanup responsibility placed on the consumer instead of the owning composable's own scope.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis on the observable drop. The ownership violation itself is direct from the cited lines; the concrete drop requires evicting the picker from the 6-slot LRU while a 2000ms parse debounce is pending, which I did not drive.
defects.proposedCure: The pipeline owns its own lifetime: move both cancels into an `onScopeDispose` inside useColorPipeline. The picker should cancel nothing it did not create — and should instead be clearing the two timers it DOES own (see C-14), which it does not.

defects.defect: Vacuous test gate: the only test in the repository that references ColorPicker.vue does not mount it — it readFileSyncs the file and asserts two regexes over its text. No test anywhere drives the readout edit path, the keyboard shortcut, the edit state machine or the numeric commit path.
defects.evidence: test/picker-blob-config.test.ts:12 reads the file; its only two assertions about it are line 44 `expect(picker).not.toMatch(/<HeroBlob[^>]*@click=/)` and line 49 `expect(picker.match(/writeClipboard\(/g)).toHaveLength(1)`. Run: `npx vitest run test/picker-blob-config.test.ts --reporter=basic` -> ` ✓ test/picker-blob-config.test.ts (3 tests) 2ms / Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 3 passed (3)`. Grepping test/ and e2e/ for `readout-fig`, `contenteditable` or a Cmd+K chord returns only e2e/smoke/flows/color-propose.spec.ts, whose own comments (lines 17-22) scope it to the dock's propose-mode span. e2e/smoke/oracles/readout-seam.spec.ts measures box geometry only (boxTop/boxBottom/minHeightPx) and would pass unchanged with C-1 present.
defects.mechanism: Grep-over-source-text standing in for behavioural coverage — the retired `proof:*` idiom the owner deleted as 'overfit junk' (memory: feedback-proof-idiom-retired.md), reappearing under a different filename.
defects.reproduction: Exact mutations that keep the suite green: (a) delete `handleKeydown` and both window.addEventListener/removeEventListener lines; (b) delete the entire `onComponentInput` hex branch (ColorPicker.vue:225-229); (c) replace `parseAndSetColor(newVal)` in the inputColor watcher (ColorPicker.vue:360) with a no-op; (d) delete both onUnmounted debounce cancels; (e) invert `isEditing` (ColorPicker.vue:273). Each passes, because the two assertions look only for `<HeroBlob @click=` and count `writeClipboard(`.
defects.proposedCure: Mount the component (@vue/test-utils with a provided COLOR_MODEL_KEY stub) and assert behaviour: readout-model agreement after a manual edit followed by an independent color change; cross-channel commit independence; listener removal on deactivate; a throwing `originalCss` leaving the edit machine consistent. Delete the two regex assertions.

defects.defect: `@update` on ColorComponentDisplay is a dead binding: the child declares the event and never emits it, while the parent binds a live handler to it.
defects.evidence: ColorPicker.vue:51 binds `@update="(v, c) => updateColorComponentDebounced(v, c)"`. ColorComponentDisplay.vue:92-95 declares `update: [value: number, component: string]`. `grep -n "emit(" demo/picker/display/ColorComponentDisplay/ColorComponentDisplay.vue` returns exactly one line: `33: emit('input', text, component);`.
defects.mechanism: Declared-but-unemitted event surviving a refactor, with its consumer binding left in place.
defects.reproduction: grep as above — the child has exactly one emit call site and it is `input`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `update` emit declaration and the parent's `@update` binding (owner edict 2 — no dead paths).

defects.defect: `isTransitioning` is dead exposed state — declared, published on the public defineExpose surface, never written and never read.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "isTransitioning" demo/ test/ e2e/ src/` returns exactly two hits, both in the same file: demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:330 (`const isTransitioning = ref(false)`) and :333 (the defineExpose entry).
defects.mechanism: Vestigial public API from a removed feature.
defects.reproduction: The grep above.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both lines.

defects.defect: The hex guard admits invalid CSS hex lengths (5 and 7 digits), so the guard that exists to prevent a parse failure is exactly what causes a spurious 2-second error flash.
defects.evidence: ColorPicker.vue:227 `/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}$/` — valid CSS hex is 3, 4, 6 or 8 digits. Measured: `"#12345" NOT-OK(result)` and `"#1234567" NOT-OK(result)`. Both reach parseAndSetColor, fail, and trip flashParseError() (useColorParsing.ts:54-57, :84-86).
defects.mechanism: A validating regex whose accepted language is wider than the grammar it guards.
defects.reproduction: npx tsx against src/css/index.ts: parseCssColor('#12345') returns a non-ok Result; the ColorPicker regex accepts it, so it is forwarded and flashes an error.

defects.defect: Parse errors raised by the picker's own input path surface on a different component in a different region (the dock's color input), and never to assistive tech — there is no error affordance and no aria-live region anywhere in demo/picker/.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "parseError" demo/ | grep -v useColorParsing.ts | grep -v useColorPipeline.ts` returns only demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:19, :87, :153, :163. `grep -rn "aria-live|role=\"status\"|role=\"alert\"" demo/picker/` returns one hit: ComponentSliders.vue:84, deliberately `aria-live="off"`.
defects.mechanism: Error state raised in one component and rendered in an unrelated sibling, with no local or AT-visible channel.
defects.reproduction: Type an invalid value into a picker readout cell; the red error badge appears on the dock's ColorInput, not on the field that was edited. A screen-reader user gets silence.
defects.proposedCure: Surface the parse verdict on the control that produced it, in a `role="status"` live region local to the picker.

defects.defect: Two timers escape their scope: the 120ms edit-target timer and the 850ms plateOpening timer both discard their ids and are never cleared, while onUnmounted clears only the two FOREIGN debounces it should not touch.
defects.evidence: ColorPicker.vue:288 `setTimeout(() => setEditTarget(target), 120)` — id discarded. ColorPicker.vue:378 `window.setTimeout(() => { plateOpening.value = false; }, 850)` — id discarded. ColorPicker.vue:381-385 (onUnmounted) clears neither, and instead cancels parseAndSetColorDebounced and updateColorComponentDebounced (see C-8) — exactly inverted ownership.
defects.mechanism: Fire-and-forget timers in a component whose lifetime is shorter than the timer (KeepAlive eviction), combined with cleanup pointed at the wrong resources.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the observable fault — hypothesis. The escape is direct from the cited lines: on eviction within 120ms the callback writes a ref on a dead scope and drives `watch(editTarget, ...) -> emit("update:editTarget")` (ColorPicker.vue:276) from an unmounted instance.
defects.proposedCure: Capture both ids and clear them in onUnmounted/onScopeDispose; remove the two foreign debounce cancels (C-8).

defects.defect: `paletteManager` is injected without `!` and without a default, and commitEdit early-returns on it WITHOUT clearing editTarget — a masking fallback that would wedge the app permanently in edit mode. The port is in fact always provided, so the guard is dead defensive code that would hide a genuine wiring break.
defects.evidence: ColorPicker.vue:198 `const paletteManager = inject(COLOR_TARGET_PORT_KEY);` — no `!`, unlike its siblings COLOR_MODEL_KEY! (:172) and VIEW_MANAGER_KEY! (:197). ColorPicker.vue:292 `if (!editTarget.value || !paletteManager) return;` leaves editTarget set. The port is always available: App.vue:351 -> usePaletteWiring.ts:60 -> usePalettePorts.ts:246 `provide(COLOR_TARGET_PORT_KEY, colorTargetPort)`, called from App setup.
defects.mechanism: Defensive optionality on a dependency that is structurally guaranteed, with a silent early-return that converts a wiring bug into a stuck UI state instead of a loud failure.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis (the port cannot currently be absent). The inconsistency and the non-clearing early-return are direct from the cited lines.
defects.proposedCure: `inject(COLOR_TARGET_PORT_KEY)!` to match every sibling injection in the file; delete the fallback branch (owner edict 2 — no masking fallbacks).

defects.defect: The route's only heading is an `<h3>` whose accessible text is a number tuple and which contains three `role="textbox"` contenteditable descendants — a heading that is also a form-control cluster. There is no h1 and no h2 on the flagship route.
defects.evidence: Measured live: {"headings":["H3: 50.0 % , 20.2 , 30.0"]} — the only heading in the whole document. Confirms REPORT.json `"h1": 0` on all 60 captures. CardTitle renders the h3 at ColorComponentDisplay.vue:13, with the contenteditable textboxes at :21-39 inside it. Full picker-subtree interactive inventory at 390x600: 1 combobox 70x52.5, 3 textboxes 88.6x46.9, 4 tabs 31.7x44, 4 sliders 12x24 — with no role="tabpanel"/aria-controls partner for the tablist (ConsoleRail.vue:13, V-A138 still open) and SpectrumCanvas.vue:8 still role="img" with no keyboard path (V-A137 still open).
defects.mechanism: Display typography chosen as semantic structure: `CardTitle` is used for a numeric readout, so heading semantics follow the visual weight rather than the document outline.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/ and evaluate `[...document.querySelectorAll('h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6')].map(h=>h.tagName+': '+h.innerText)` — a single H3 containing the number tuple.
defects.proposedCure: Land W47 §Work-3's 'one stable shell <main>+H1' and demote the readout to a non-heading element; the contenteditable roles die with C-1's cure.

defects.defect: `any` in the template erases the only place `selectedColorSpace` could be checked against `DisplayColorSpace`, under an otherwise strict config.
defects.evidence: ColorPicker.vue:43 `@update:model-value="(colorSpace: any) => updateModel({ selectedColorSpace: colorSpace })"`.
defects.mechanism: Type hole opened at a component boundary where the child already knows its own value type.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis (no runtime fault observed); the annotation is direct from the cited line.
defects.proposedCure: Type the parameter `DisplayColorSpace` (or let ColorSpaceSelector's emit type flow through by using v-model).

defects.defect: The pointer-debug surface is statically imported into the picker's eager chunk in production, unlike the blob graph which was deliberately split out for exactly this reason.
defects.evidence: ColorPicker.vue:133 and :141 statically import usePointerDebug and PointerDebugOverlay (which pulls DebugEventLog.vue and ~155 lines of overlay CSS). usePointerDebug() constructs a reactive state object on every mount (usePointerDebug.ts:44-50). Render is correctly gated (PointerDebugOverlay.vue:4 `v-if="debug.state.enabled"`) and global listeners are correctly gated on ?debug=1 (usePointerDebug.ts:154), so this is bundle weight, not runtime cost. Contrast ColorPicker.vue:148-158, where the blob graph is deliberately deferred with defineAsyncComponent + useIdleReady and the rationale is written out.
defects.mechanism: Debug tooling co-located with production code without the async boundary the same file applies to its other heavy dependency.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis on the bundle delta; the static imports are direct from the cited lines.
defects.proposedCure: `defineAsyncComponent` the overlay behind the same `debug=1` predicate, matching the blob precedent in the same file.

defects.defect: The '/' route — the picker's, and the only route mounting an eager WebGL surface — is the sole capture in the entire 60-capture matrix that both lost its GL context and blew the 30s navigation budget.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json, safari-desktop-light `/`: "navError":"TimeoutError: page.goto: Timeout 30000ms exceeded ... waiting until \"networkidle\"", "settleMs":38454, consoleErrors including "WebGL: context lost." and "[vite] TypeError: Importing a module script failed.". Median settle across the other 59 captures is 3490-3715ms (REPORT.md:190-249). ColorPicker.vue:94-98 is the sole mount site of HeroBlob -> glass-ui Blob. glass-ui 7.0.0 DOES ship a webglcontextlost handler (grep -rl webglcontextlost node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/ hits), so no missing-recovery defect is claimed.
defects.mechanism: Unknown — the capture conflates GL context loss with a concurrent Vite HMR module failure in the same console list, so the causal direction is not established.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is explicitly a HYPOTHESIS. It needs a repeat capture with HMR quiesced to separate GL loss from the [vite] module failure.
defects.proposedCure: Re-capture the '/' route on a production build (no HMR) x2 matrices before attributing anything to the blob; if GL loss persists, escalate to the glass-ui producer with the trace rather than patching the demo.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion & seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]; the explicitly declared spawn tier, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-01 — the contenteditable headline is an unguarded write path with no commit/cancel/clamp/error semantics. One keystroke into the `a` cell of lab(50% 20 30) sets the model to 20.05 while the readout and aria-valuetext both say 20.1 and the URL + document title carry 20.05: the instrument cannot round-trip its own display and the share link encodes a value the user was never shown. Ten keystrokes reflow the "locked" chassis by +61.2px (readout) / +8.4px (card) with 8px of inner horizontal overflow mid-typing, falsifying readoutReservation.ts's own "TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION" card-lock premise. The register knows the contenteditable must die; it does not know it corrupts the model, the URL and the title, nor that it breaks the card-lock.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded soundness, so the next seat does not re-litigate: reduced motion is genuinely correct — `--stagger-base` is consumed only inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` at animations.css:43-54, and header.css:136-143 collapses condense transitions to 0.01ms while keeping the layout state; HeroBlob.vue:10 is aria-hidden + pointer-events-none so the inert-specimen leaf really landed; `main` count = 1; specimen Copy count = 0 inside the picker card; PointerDebugOverlay.vue:4 is v-if-gated and paints 0 nodes; verbatimModuleSyntax satisfied at ColorPicker.vue:125,128; Vue 3.5 idioms present — useTemplateRef ×2 at 186,189 and shallowRef at 272, with the defineModel round-trip deliberately avoided via the injected App-owned ShallowRef; scrollWidth − clientWidth = 0 at both 1440 and 390.)

defects.defect: The `contenteditable` numeric headline is an unguarded write path with no commit, cancel, clamp, or error semantics. Display, AT announcement, URL and document title disagree after a single keystroke, and the card-lock the whole reservation system exists to hold breaks mid-typing.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/display/ColorComponentDisplay/ColorComponentDisplay.vue:22-23 (contenteditable="true" role="textbox"); demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:223-235 (onComponentInput → parseFloat → updateColorComponentDebounced). Live Playwright transcript at 1440x900, route #/?space=lab&color=lab(50% 20 30): t0 cells ["50.0 % ,","20.0 ,","30.0"] sliders "a axis 20.0" title "lab(50% 20 30)"; t1 cells [...,"20.05 ,",...] ; t2(+900ms) cells [...,"20.1 ,",...] sliders "a axis 20.1" title "lab(50% 20.05 30)" url #/?space=lab&color=lab(50%25+20.05+30). Second run, insertText('9999999999'): before readout 441.8x122.4 card h 684.8 scrollW 442 = clientW 442; during readout 469.0x183.6 (+61.2px = one 1.12em line) card h 693.2 (+8.4px) scrollW 477 > clientW 469 (8px inner overflow); settled back to 122.4/684.8 with title "lab(50% 20.19999999999 30)".
defects.mechanism: Editing job fused into the display job: one DOM node is simultaneously the reactive render target and the user's text-entry surface, and the model clamp/format lives at the pipeline seam, downstream of the paint. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 ("read-only contiguous numeric readout"), §4 ("editing occurs only in W21's semantic numeric fields"), PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.10 ("no duplicate contenteditable path").
defects.reproduction: Serve the demo (http://localhost:9000/), open #/?space=lab&color=lab(50%25%2020%2030) at 1440x900, wait for settle, focus the second [contenteditable="true"][role="textbox"] cell, collapse the selection to the end of its contents, document.execCommand('insertText', false, '5'), wait 900ms, then read the cell text, every [role=slider] aria-valuetext, location.hash and document.title. Repeat with '9999999999' while sampling .readout and the picker card getBoundingClientRect before / during / after.
defects.proposedCure: Transposition, not validation. Split the headline's three fused jobs: the route <h1> is owned by the shell, the readout becomes a pure projection (<output>, no contenteditable, no role=textbox, no tab stop), and editing moves whole into the domain-neutral axis composition over BI Slider that W48 already specifies — which owns commit/cancel/error and formats through the same cell the headline projects. One writer, one formatter, one truth. Do not add validation to the contenteditable; delete the writer.

defects.defect: PR-01's label→headline void is live and the register's cure is mis-apportioned: 69.93px of dead vertical air at 1440 against a 14.87px canon ceiling, of which the Blob-derived .title-row minimum contributes exactly 0px.
defects.evidence: Live at 1440x900: trigger text-box bottom 240.91, readout first ink line top 310.84 → gap 69.93px. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.2 / PROPORTION-AUDIT §2.2 bind I_after ≤ min(φG, I_before − G) with G ≈ 9.2px → φG ≈ 14.87px; measured 69.93 = 4.70× the ceiling (25.4px = 1.71× at 390). Apportionment: readout reserved-minus-painted = 122.40 − 67.50 = +54.90px with align-content:flex-end (ColorComponentDisplay.vue:151,166); .picker-header row-gap = 7.168px (header.css:25); label leading ≈13.3px; .title-row min-height computes 73.12px against a content height of 84.98px → NON-binding, 0px. `--instrument-title-gap` computes to the empty string on the live page (P122 token undefined/unconsumed). Same measurement at 390: readoutReservedVsPainted = −4.2px (the lock is honest there).
defects.mechanism: A display surface was made to reserve an editing worst-case: readoutReservation.ts derives lab's line count as 2 from a static worst-case ch table and `.readout` bottom-anchors a one-line value inside that two-line box, so the unused legal-width line renders as blank air above the numbers. readoutReservation.ts:138-147 models only the "cqi band (pane 400–512)" and the "390 phone" and claims the capacity is "a structural guarantee across the whole band"; at 1440 the pane IS 512 (in-band) and lab renders one line while the table derives two — the guarantee fails inside its own modelled band.
defects.reproduction: At 1440x900 on the settled / route, take Range.getClientRects() over .space-trigger and over .readout; gap = min(readout rect tops) − max(trigger rect bottoms) = 69.93. Then compare .readout getBoundingClientRect().height (122.40) against the painted ink extent (max bottom − min top = 67.50) → 54.90px reserved-not-painted, and read getComputedStyle('.title-row').minHeight (73.12px) against its rendered height (84.98px). Repeat at 390x844 for the −4.2px arm.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `--readout-lines`, `align-content: flex-end` and the static line table outright (ColorComponentDisplay.vue:151,166 + readoutReservation.ts:122-208). One line always; a genuinely wrapped tuple grows BELOW into feature-local flow, which VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.2 already sanctions. The card-lock goal is then met by tabular figures + the fixed per-space least count alone — mechanism (i) that readoutReservation.ts:14-18 already names. W48 must reorder: at 1440 deleting the Blob reservation first moves the frame 0px.

defects.defect: The picker's primary spatial control — the 2D saturation×lightness spectrum field — is not in the tab order at all; the flagship instrument is mouse-only.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/controls/SpectrumCanvas/SpectrumCanvas.vue:8-9 — role="img" on a pointer-only div, no tabindex, no role="slider", no named numeric axes. Live enumeration of focusables inside the picker Card at 1440x900 (offsetParent !== null), in order: combobox "Select color space"; textbox "l/a/b component value" ×3; tab "l/a/b/alpha channel" ×4; slider "L/A/B/ALPHA channel" ×4. Twelve stops, none of them the spectrum. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 "every spatial action has a keyboard/numeric equivalent"; §5.2 "Spectrum coordinates: expose two named numeric axes … pointer canvas is not the sole keyboard control". This is V-A137, confirmed still born-RED on disk at c654824e.
defects.mechanism: A canvas-shaped control was given a presentational role instead of a control role, so its two coordinate axes were never modelled as named numeric quantities; the composition has no shared axis primitive to fall back on.
defects.reproduction: At 1440x900 on the settled / route, enumerate [...card.querySelectorAll('a[href],button,input,select,textarea,[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"]),[contenteditable="true"]')].filter(e => e.offsetParent !== null) where card = document.querySelector('.pane-shell [data-slot=card]'); the .spectrum-picker element is absent from the result.
defects.proposedCure: Build the shared domain-neutral axis composition over BI Slider (already W48 Work step 3) and give SpectrumCanvas two named numeric S/V axes sharing one coordinate model with the canvas, per §5.2's Home/End and arrow law. The pointer canvas becomes an alternate view of the same two controls, not the only view.

defects.defect: The route protagonist holds exactly 50.00% of the two-pane stage — 11.8 percentage points below the canon floor — with a character-identical drop shadow to its companion, so the composition has no protagonist at all.
defects.evidence: Live at 1440x900: .pane-container.pane-container--dual is display:grid with grid-template-columns "512px 512px", gap 18px; panes [left x199 w512 h774] [right x729 w512 h774] → leftShare 50.00% / rightShare 50.00%. box-shadow on BOTH plates: "color(srgb 0.11 0.098 0.09 / 0.5) 8px 8px 0px 0px" (picker card 512x684.8, About card 512x774). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 1: exactly golden 61.8033989%/38.1966011% or preview-dominant 66.6666667%/33.3333333%, protagonist law 61.8–66.7%. §3 law 8: "Supporting fixtures do not compete with it through equal size or equal shadow." §3.1 line 58: "About is a quiet trailing destination rather than Picker's companion." PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-04 disposes "Empty/equal companion Cards" as REMOVE. Visible directly in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png.
defects.mechanism: An equal-column grid was used where a golden instrument/inspector ratio is bound, and the companion was given the same material tier and the same shadow token as the protagonist, so neither size nor depth nor material distinguishes figure from ground.
defects.reproduction: At 1440x900 on /, read getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.pane-container')).gridTemplateColumns → "512px 512px", and getComputedStyle(el).boxShadow for both [data-slot=card] elements wider than 300px → identical strings.
defects.proposedCure: Retire About as Picker's companion per §3.1 (it is a trailing route, not an inspector) and transpose the picker to the producer InstrumentChassis with its exact golden stage/inspector ratio. If an inspector is genuinely absent, §3.1 is explicit that it "leaves no filler" — the stage takes the full width rather than being halved by a peer document. D-11 (the duplicated ColorSpaceSelector) dies with this.

defects.defect: The P019 identity/specimen type pair is at the required 1/√φ only at the phone floor; it drifts to near-parity at 1440, so at desktop the label and the numeric specimen are optically the same size.
defects.evidence: Measured label font-size / headline font-size: 390x844 → 32.928 / 41.888 = 0.7861 (required 1/√φ = 0.78615, correct); 1440x900 → 53.280 / 54.644 = 0.9750. Drift +24.0% across the band. Sources: label = --type-display-2 = clamp(2.058rem, 1.5rem + 2.2vw, 3.33rem) at ColorSpaceSelector.vue:209 (ceiling-bound at 1440); headline = calc(min(var(--type-display-4), max(11.65cqi, 2.618rem)) * var(--readout-fit,1)) at ColorComponentDisplay.vue:137-140 (floor-bound at 390, 11.65cqi-bound at 1440 — --type-display-4 resolves to 86.11px and never binds). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.2: "BI P019 supplies one paired proportional clamp; both sizes resolve from that one clamp … rather than only at endpoints" and "independently clamped display-2/display-3 tokens and a local approximation are forbidden."
defects.mechanism: Two independently clamped sources with different binding arms cannot hold a constant ratio. The register (V-A140) describes this as a fixed two-rung skip; the rendered truth is a ratio that is exactly right at one end of the band and collapses at the other — worse than documented.
defects.reproduction: On the settled / route read parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.space-trigger')).fontSize) / parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.readout')).fontSize) at 390x844 (0.7861) and at 1440x900 (0.9750).
defects.proposedCure: One shared P019 paired clamp: derive both arms from a single fluid quantity so label = headline / √φ identically through floor, fluid and ceiling. Delete the local 11.65cqi mint and the independent --type-display-2 claim; the pair becomes one token consumption, not two.

defects.defect: The numeric headline renders in Fraunces, not Fira Code, so the identity arm and the specimen arm share a family — which is why D-05's near-parity reads as a collision rather than a contrast.
defects.evidence: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.readout')).fontFamily = 'Fraunces, "Fraunces Fallback", serif' at both 1440 and 390. The .fira-code class is applied only when formatted[component]?.monospace (ColorComponentDisplay.vue:28), which is false for every numeric channel. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.2: "the read-only Fira Code numeric readout is the headline and the Fraunces selected-space identity is exactly one adjacent golden rung smaller"; §4: "value applies Fraunces to its identity arm and Fira Code to its headline arm at exact 1/√φ"; §7 Picker repeats it.
defects.mechanism: The family split that carries the identity/value distinction was never applied to the headline; the whole readout inherits font-display (Fraunces) from ColorComponentDisplay.vue:14.
defects.reproduction: On the settled / route, read getComputedStyle('.readout').fontFamily; confirm no .fira-code class on any .readout-fig by inspecting the rendered innerHTML of a .readout-cell.
defects.proposedCure: Apply Fira Code to the headline arm unconditionally as §4's sole paired-scale exception specifies, landing atomically with the D-05 paired clamp — family and ratio are one design decision, not two.

defects.defect: The flagship route has zero <h1>, and the first heading in the document is an <h3> whose text is a number tuple and whose children are three interactive textboxes.
defects.evidence: Live at 1440x900: h1count = 0; headings[0] = { tag: "H3", data-slot: "card-title", text: "64.8%,18.0,42.0" }; contenteditable count = 3, all role="textbox", all inside that H3; main count = 1 (this half is correct). ColorComponentDisplay.vue:13 renders the readout as glass-ui <CardTitle>, which emits <h3>. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: "Each route has one H1 and exactly one stable main landmark"; §5.1: "the single visible H1 exist[s] before app-ready". PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.11: "A display-sized readout is not therefore a document heading or live status … route H1 owns heading hierarchy."
defects.mechanism: A display-sized readout was expressed with a heading primitive because CardTitle was the nearest available typographic slot; the route's actual identity heading was never authored.
defects.reproduction: On the settled / route: document.querySelectorAll('h1').length → 0; [...document.querySelectorAll('h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6')][0] → H3[data-slot=card-title] with numeric text; document.querySelectorAll('[contenteditable="true"]').length → 3, all descendants of that H3.
defects.proposedCure: Shell owns one route <h1> per §5.1's focus/announcement table; the readout becomes <output> (non-heading, non-live, labelled) per §5.11's "one labeled non-live domain output". Lands with D-01 as one atomic change — the heading role and the editor role are the same fusion.

defects.defect: Card is used as the route chassis where the canon binds InstrumentChassis (which glass-ui 7.0.0 ships), and a second Card is nested inside it — falsifying the premise PROPORTION-AUDIT §2 ruling 2 is conditioned on.
defects.evidence: Live: the picker plate is <div data-slot="card" class="glass-resting card rounded-card …">, composed at ColorPicker.vue:6,21,64 from Card + CardHeader + CardContent. `node -p "Object.keys(require('@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json').exports)" | grep chassis` → ./instrument-chassis; `grep -rl InstrumentChassis node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` → dist/instrument-chassis.js, dist/components/instrument-chassis/InstrumentChassis.vue.d.ts. Nested Card: ComponentSliders.vue:25 renders <Card surface="veil">, measured live as a glass-quiet card at 469 x 190.4 inside the glass-resting card. `--instrument-title-gap` computes to "" on the live page. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1 binds Picker's outer housing to InstrumentChassis and states Card "is never the default page primitive"; §2 "One surface has one tier. An inner card is not automatically another pane of glass." PROPORTION-AUDIT §2 ruling 2 opens: "Because Picker no longer nests a Card, BI P122 exposes --instrument-title-gap …" — false at HEAD.
defects.mechanism: The producer chassis was never consumed, so every quantity it would supply (title gap, stage/inspector ratio, boundary set, reserve) is re-minted locally — which is the upstream cause of D-02's undefined token, D-04's equal grid and D-05's independent clamps. Owner edict 4: glass-ui is the design system; do not hand-roll what it provides.
defects.reproduction: On the settled / route: getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--instrument-title-gap') → ""; document.querySelectorAll('.pane-shell [data-slot=card]').length → 2 (glass-resting outer, glass-quiet inner at 469x190.4). In the tree: grep -n 'Card' demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue → line 25 <Card surface="veil">.
defects.proposedCure: Transpose the picker to the producer InstrumentChassis (stage / inspector / action regions, P122 boundary set [] and reserve none per OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS §5) and collapse the inner veil Card to a plain material region — §2's "one surface has one tier". The proportion, title-gap and pair rows then close by token consumption instead of five separate local cures. PROPORTION-AUDIT §2 ruling 2 must be re-premised before it is executed.

defects.defect: The "ONE rhythm law" token introduced to cure a 6× title→readout gap divergence did not cure it — it inverted the sign and left a 2.75× divergence, now worst at desktop.
defects.evidence: header.css:18-23 states the token replaces "the fixed gap-y-1 (4px) that … read as a 6× divergent gap (4.0px@1440 vs 24.6px@390)" so that "1440 and 390 share ONE rhythm SOURCE". Measured label→headline separation after the cure: 1440 → 69.93px, 390 → 25.40px, ratio 2.75× with the loose arm now at desktop (previously 6.15× with the loose arm at mobile). The row-gap token itself is well-behaved: getComputedStyle('.picker-header').rowGap = 7.168px at 1440.
defects.mechanism: A token was introduced against a symptom whose cause lives in a different file: the seam is governed by the readout's two-line reservation (D-02), not by the header row-gap. Curing the wrong quantity leaves the divergence intact and changes only which arm is worse.
defects.reproduction: Measure the label→headline ink separation (Range.getClientRects over .space-trigger and .readout) at 1440x900 (69.93px) and 390x844 (25.40px); separately read getComputedStyle('.picker-header').rowGap (7.168px at 1440) to show the token is not the governing quantity.
defects.proposedCure: Retire --picker-header-rhythm in favour of the producer P122 --instrument-title-gap once the chassis lands (D-08), and delete the readout reservation (D-02). The seam then has exactly one owner and the two arms converge by construction.

defects.defect: The only keyboard-operable channel control is a 12x24 CSS px target at every viewport — half the WCAG 2.2 minimum on the inline axis, with no touch accommodation.
defects.evidence: Live measurement of focusables inside the picker Card: 1440x900 → L/A/B/ALPHA channel sliders 12.0 x 24 CSS px; 390x844 → 12.1 x 24 CSS px. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (Target Size, Minimum, AA) floors at 24 x 24 CSS px. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.7: "Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities. Accessibility floors do not require bloated visible chrome"; PR-12 disposes this family as TIGHTEN with "invisible/seat geometry preserves target floor while optics follow rung".
defects.mechanism: The visible thumb glyph IS the hit target — the three quantities §5.7 separates were collapsed into one, so the only way to meet the floor would be to fatten the optic, and neither was done.
defects.reproduction: At 390x844 and 1440x900 on the settled / route, map every focusable inside document.querySelector('.pane-shell [data-slot=card]') to its getBoundingClientRect() and filter width < 24 || height < 24 → four [role=slider] thumbs at 12.0–12.1 x 24 in both matrices.
defects.proposedCure: Give the producer Slider thumb an invisible seat (pseudo-element or padded hit box) at ≥24x24 while the painted glyph keeps its 12px optical rung — exactly PR-12's disposition. Root-level, in glass-ui's Slider, not per-instance in demo/picker (owner edict 5).

defects.defect: Two instances of the same control, bound to the same state, are visible simultaneously on the desktop route at two different sizes with no indication they are one control.
defects.evidence: Live at 1440x900: .space-trigger count = 2 — [0] x220.5 y161.0 111.5x85.0 font 53.280px Fraunces "Lab" (picker header); [1] x894.4 y164.0 88.6x48.0 font 41.888px Fraunces "Lab" (About heading, inline variant). Both are ColorSpaceSelector driving model.selectedColorSpace. Visible in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png as "Lab ⌄" appearing twice. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-06/PR-07 family: "One action/selection owner"; §5.6 "Subtraction precedes explanation."
defects.mechanism: The About pane was made Picker's desktop companion (D-04) and independently embeds the same selector in its heading sentence, so one piece of state acquired two peer controls with two type treatments.
defects.reproduction: On the settled / route at 1440x900: [...document.querySelectorAll('.space-trigger')].map(e => ({rect: e.getBoundingClientRect(), fs: getComputedStyle(e).fontSize, text: e.innerText.trim()})) → two entries, 53.280px and 41.888px, both "Lab".
defects.proposedCure: Dies with D-04: once About is a trailing route rather than Picker's companion, the picker header owns the sole selector. If About must name the active space it renders it as text, not as a second operable control.

defects.defect: An undiscoverable global Cmd+K shortcut is bound on `window` with no target guard and no affordance anywhere in the UI.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:247 (const keys = useMagicKeys()), :263-266 (if (keys.cmd?.value && keys.k?.value) { e.preventDefault(); selectedColorSpaceOpen.value = !selectedColorSpaceOpen.value; }), registered at :377 (window.addEventListener("keydown", handleKeydown)). No tooltip, menu item, hint or label names it anywhere in demo/picker/. PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-07 ("Hover-only/unlabeled controls") and §5.6 ("Subtraction precedes explanation"); VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 interaction grammar select → tune → commit.
defects.mechanism: Three defects in one binding: undiscoverable (no affordance), unscoped (a bare window listener fires while focus is in any editable surface, including this component's own contenteditable cells and the dock colour input), and a toggle on a held-key predicate (useMagicKeys reports cmd and k as held, so any subsequent keydown while both remain down re-toggles the popover).
defects.reproduction: Read demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:247,263-266,377 — the handler has no event.target / activeElement check and no document-scope guard. Reproduction of the re-toggle: hold Cmd+K and press any third key; the predicate is still true and the popover toggles again.
defects.proposedCure: Either give the shortcut a named, visible home (a labelled affordance on the selector trigger, or a command palette that owns the binding) and scope the listener to the instrument root with an editable-target guard, or delete it. Subtraction precedes explanation: an undiscoverable command is not part of the grammar.

defects.defect: The mobile headline wraps to a 27%-filled orphan line — a three-term tuple broken 2+1, the worst available break.
defects.evidence: Measured at 390x844: last painted line of .readout carries 88.7px of ink in a 327.7px box = 27.1% filled, 72.9% void. Visible in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-mobile-light/picker.png as "20.0" stranded alone beneath "92.0%, 88.8,". PROPORTION-AUDIT §2.5 permits a second line only for "a tuple whose rendered legal width actually wraps" but is silent on where the break falls.
defects.mechanism: flex-wrap with atomic nowrap cells and no break policy: the line simply fills greedily, so a 3-tuple breaks 2+1 whenever the third cell does not fit.
defects.reproduction: At 390x844 on the settled / route, take Range.getClientRects() over .readout, group by rounded top, sum the widths of the rects on the last line (88.7px) and compare with .readout getBoundingClientRect().width (327.7px).
defects.proposedCure: Give the tuple an explicit break policy in the composition — all-on-one-line (via the paired clamp of D-05 sized to the guaranteed capacity) or an even 1+1+1 stack — rather than greedy fill. The break is a design decision and must be authored, not inherited from flex-wrap.

defects.defect: `isTransitioning` is declared, exposed on the public component surface, never written and never read anywhere in the repository.
defects.evidence: $ grep -rn "isTransitioning" demo/ src/ → demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:330 (const isTransitioning = ref(false);) and demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:333 (inside defineExpose). Zero other hits repo-wide.
defects.mechanism: Dead reactive state kept alive by an imperative defineExpose surface that no type-checker or grep can prove unused from the consumer side.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "isTransitioning" demo/ src/ — two hits, both the declaration and its own re-export.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both lines. Owner edict 2 (no legacy code, no dead paths); folds into D-16's reduction of the exposed surface.

defects.defect: `.pane-shell` declares a transform transition for a property nothing in the tree ever sets — dead residue of a deleted margin morph.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:399 — transition: transform var(--spring-smooth-duration) var(--transition-liquid-spatial); resolving live to "transform 0.35s linear(0 0%, 0.00287 2.041%, …)". $ grep -rn "pane-shell" demo/ → ColorPicker.vue:5 (the root), seat.css:42, overture.css:126 (which targets .pane-shell > :first-child, i.e. the Card, not the shell) plus comments. No rule applies a transform to .pane-shell. The comment at ColorPicker.vue:392-398 records the deleted margin morph this replaced.
defects.mechanism: A transition survived the deletion of the property it was written for; nothing fails, so nothing surfaced it.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "pane-shell" demo/ and inspect each hit — no transform declaration or class toggle targets the element; getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.pane-shell')).transform is "none" in every state sampled.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the declaration. Owner edict 2.

defects.defect: A 12-member imperative defineExpose surface, with the dock's action-bar contract handed to a sibling through a parent-held template ref.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:315-344 exposes isEditing, isTransitioning, editTarget, commitEdit, cancelEdit, onPaletteApply, onPaletteAddColor, parseColor, setCurrentColor, applyExternalColor, onStartEdit, actionBarContext. The comment at :311 states the mechanism plainly: "Action bar context for TopDock (exposed, not provided — TopDock is a sibling)".
defects.mechanism: Cross-sibling coupling routed through an imperative ref: every consumer is invisible to the type system and to grep, which is exactly how D-14's dead member survived. Owner edict 1 (no god modules; focused modules with real encapsulation).
defects.reproduction: Read demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:311-344; the twelve members and the sibling-wiring comment are literal.
defects.proposedCure: Move the action-bar contract into the injected COLOR_MODEL_KEY pipeline that both dock and picker already consume, so the contract is a typed provide/inject rather than a ref-reach. The exposed surface shrinks to whatever the parent genuinely orchestrates.

defects.defect: Two untokenized magic timings couple the edit state machine and the boot state flag to motion durations re-derived by hand in JavaScript.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:288 — setTimeout(() => setEditTarget(target), 120) inside onStartEdit. demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:378 — window.setTimeout(() => { plateOpening.value = false; }, 850), whose comment at :365-371 derives 850 from "440ms plate-land → field paint-in → +220ms stagger … 90ms slack". Both are literals over token-owned quantities (--overture-plate-land, --stagger-base, --spring-smooth-duration).
defects.mechanism: A consumer of a motion's END re-derives that end arithmetically instead of observing it, so retuning any motion token silently desynchronises state from paint. The same file already does this correctly elsewhere: ColorPicker.vue:97 uses @vue:mounted / animationend for the HeroBlob emerge beat.
defects.reproduction: Read demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:288 and :365-378; both timings are literals with no token reference. Changing --overture-plate-land in overture.css does not change either number.
defects.proposedCure: Listen for animationend (the idiom this file already uses at :97) or read the token via getComputedStyle, rather than re-deriving durations as literals. The 120ms edit delay should be replaced by the transition's own completion signal or deleted.

defects.defect: Dark mode was inherited, not designed: the ambient field is identical in both schemes, so the plate inverts against a bright ground, the cartoon shadow disappears, and the inert Blob becomes the highest-luminance object on the page.
defects.evidence: Compare docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png with safari-desktop-dark/picker.png: the atmosphere gradient behind the plates is the same bright pink→peach field in both; only the cards change, to a desaturated brown-maroon. The 8px 8px 0 0 shadow at 50% alpha of near-black is legible in light and effectively invisible in dark. In safari-mobile-dark/picker.png the Blob renders as a pure-white blot — the brightest element on the page by a wide margin, beside a specimen readout several stops darker. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.9: "Picker Blob is inert presentation"; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7: "Blob is a noninteractive center-ward specimen"; §2: "Dark chrome uses the restrained neutral pole" — the measured dark plate is a seed-tinted brown, not neutral.
defects.mechanism: Figure/ground inversion: dark surfaces were applied to the chrome without a corresponding treatment of the ambient field or of the ornament's luminance, so the scheme's hierarchy is the light scheme's hierarchy with the two brightest layers swapped.
defects.reproduction: View the four committed picker screenshots side by side (safari-{desktop,mobile}-{light,dark}/picker.png); the background gradient is pixel-comparable between the light and dark members of each pair while the card surfaces invert.
defects.proposedCure: Author the dark scheme as its own composition: restrained-neutral chrome per §2, an ambient field that darkens with the scheme, and a Blob luminance ceiling bound to the specimen's — an inert ornament may never be the brightest object in the frame.

defects.defect: Alpha is structurally excluded from the headline while the channel rail displays it, so the flagship readout describes a colour the instrument is not holding; and the reservation table budgets an alpha cell that is never rendered.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useColorPipeline.ts:117-123 builds colorComponents from PICKER_CHANNELS[space] only — alpha is never a headline cell. In docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png the rail reads "α 82.7%" while the headline reads "92.0% 88.8, 20.0". W48's own completion evidence expects four cells: "reads 92.0% | 88.8 | 20.0 | 82.70%". VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4: "Alpha appears only when semantically relevant" — 82.7% alpha is the definition of relevant. Mirror-image dead code: readoutReservation.ts:96 injects an `alpha` entry into READOUT_CH for every space, but readoutLineCount/readoutFit are only ever called with colorComponents.map(([c]) => c), which excludes alpha.
defects.mechanism: The headline's cell set and the reservation table's cell set were derived from different sources and never reconciled: one under-reports the colour, the other over-reserves for a cell that cannot appear.
defects.reproduction: Read demo/color-session/useColorPipeline.ts:117-123 (no alpha in colorComponents) alongside demo/picker/display/ColorComponentDisplay/readoutReservation.ts:94-97 (alpha injected into READOUT_CH); then view safari-desktop-light/picker.png where the rail shows α 82.7% and the headline shows three cells.
defects.proposedCure: One source of truth for the shown-channel set: the headline projects exactly the channels the rail exposes, with alpha present iff it is not 1 (per §4). Delete the unreachable alpha entry from READOUT_CH — or, better, delete the whole table with D-02.

waveSpec.title: Picker instrument transposition — supersedes V.W48 in place (same row, same discharges, re-premised)
waveSpec.scope:
THREE ORDERED STAGES, ONE ATOMIC CLOSE. No intermediate state is mergeable; B and C delete code that only compiles once A's symbols exist.

ROW IDENTITY: this IS W48. It keeps W48's dependency edges (W46 chrome law, W47 shell/scene), its Absorbs (W20+W21+W29's Picker paint slice) and its ENTIRE discharge list — RF-28 F2 phantom-gate heal, PR-01/02/03/13/15-seed/23, V-A137/A138/A140/A167/A120, archaeology T-2/4/5/7/16/17/28/33/34/35/40/44/50/51/59 and U-F9/F16/F25/F26/F27/F57. RE-PREMISED: three of W48's stated premises are false at HEAD c654824e — (i) PROPORTION-AUDIT §2 ruling 2's 'Because Picker no longer nests a Card' (it nests one at ComponentSliders.vue:25; --instrument-title-gap resolves to ""); (ii) Work-2's seat.css:88 anchor is the HORIZONTAL padding-right, the vertical reservation is :89, and at 1440 neither binds — the readout reservation does, at 55.41px of a 70.42px seam; (iii) the completion clause 'agree in one settled routed frame' is single-frame and passes with the readout/model desync fully present.

STAGE A — THE LIBRARY BOUNDARY (additive minor 4.1.0; 4.0.0 is immutable, no existing export changes shape). Create src/color/space-schema.ts holding CHANNEL_DOMAIN: Record<SpaceId, readonly {key,min,max,unit,hue?}[]> — the node ARCHITECTURE.md:71 declares and the tree lacks; the library is already the authority (it clamps kelvin 1000–40000 at model.ts:91 and gamut-maps against these bounds). Re-export SPACE_SCHEMA, SPACE_IDS, makeColor, isAnyColor, CHANNEL_DOMAIN and the four operations through BOTH src/color/index.ts and src/subpaths/color.ts. Rebuild dist/ (demo Vite aliases are generated from package.json#exports and resolve to dist/ — the rebuild is part of the wave, not an assumption). Then DELETE the demo's shadow library and rewrite picker-color.ts to a Result-returning adapter with NO throwing wrapper. Rewrite the two docstrings citing dead APIs to name the real published symbols.

STAGE B — OWNERSHIP. useColorEditSession + useActionBarContext land in demo/color-session/, provided by App beside COLOR_MODEL_KEY; the Dock injects. defineExpose → 0; colorPickerRef deleted; usePaletteWiring loses its picker parameter, whenColorPickerReady and BOTH fallback arms. applyExternalColor/applyColorString reconcile to one applyCssColor(css): Result. demo/shell/useKeyboardMap.ts becomes the ONE window keydown owner, registered once at the root and dispatching by active route; the picker keeps no global listener. usePaneRouter.componentFor() becomes exhaustive over LeftPane and THROWS on unknown. demo/color-picker/ → demo/app/ (the declared name). demo/ui/ DELETED, 90 import sites rewritten to @mkbabb/glass-ui[/subpath]. Pointer-debug moves to demo/platform/debug/ behind import.meta.env.DEV + dynamic import; ComponentSliders' dead injection deleted; SpectrumCanvas takes inject(POINTER_DEBUG_KEY, null) with optional calls.

STAGE C — THE INSTRUMENT. InstrumentChassis (stage/inspector/action, proportion golden, boundaries [], reserve none) replaces Card+CardHeader+CardContent; the inner veil Card collapses to a plain material region. ColorReadout.vue — an <output>, labelled, non-live, non-heading, no contenteditable, no role=textbox, one line always, a true wrap growing BELOW into feature-local flow — replaces ColorComponentDisplay; readoutReservation.ts, --readout-lines and align-content:flex-end deleted. ONE shared P019 paired clamp with the Fira Code headline arm and the Fraunces identity arm at exact 1/√φ. ChannelAxis.vue (glass-ui Slider for pointer/keyboard/Home/End + NumberField for commit/cancel/clamp/invalid/format) becomes the SOLE editor, consumed by ComponentSliders and by SpectrumCanvas's two named S/V axes sharing one coordinate model with the canvas — A137 and A138 die, and SpectrumCanvas's role="img" rationale COMMENT is deleted with the attribute. channelSet.ts becomes the single shown-channel derivation over the published CHANNEL_DOMAIN, alpha present iff alpha !== 1, with headline/rail/reservation reading the SAME array identity. displaySpace.ts becomes the one DisplayColorSpace home, collapsing 11 `=== "hex"` sites to 1. useHeaderCondense deleted (the contraction is W47's shell obligation). The producer Slider thumb gains a ≥24px invisible seat IN GLASS-UI with a BH/BI relay.

result.addendumClause:
**MT-A-PICKER-1 (architecture · isomorphism).** `demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue` is adjudicated **APOTHEOSIS_REQUIRED** on the architecture axis: twenty-one merged defects, four of them BLOCKER, all four reproduced at HEAD `c654824e`. The mechanism is singular and it is not local to the component — **five concepts are implemented one level below the level that owns them, because the owning level withheld them**: the colour-space schema and generic constructor (`src/color/model.ts` implements `SPACE_SCHEMA`/`SPACE_IDS`/`makeColor`/`isAnyColor`; `src/color/index.ts` re-exports none, so `dist/subpaths/color.js` publishes 23 symbols and none of these four, and `demo/color-session/picker-color.ts` hosts a shadow library — a 17-space channel table, a byte-identical copy of `src/css/grammar.ts:160-164`, and a 17-case `buildColor` that is `makeColor` with type safety stripped, in the slider hot path); the edit session and action-bar contract (whose *type* already lives at `demo/color-session/keys.ts:17`, whose *assembly* sits in a KeepAlive'd route leaf behind a 12-member `defineExpose` reached by a template ref captured on the desktop mount path only — measured: six action-bar controls present at 1440×900 and absent at 390×844 with the picker mounted in both); the application keyboard map (a `window` keydown listener registered in `onMounted` under `<KeepAlive>` — measured on `#/gradient` with the picker absent from the DOM, a real ⌘K arrives `defaultPrevented: true`); numeric editing, the instrument chassis and the axis primitive (all three shipped by `@mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0` as `./number-field`, `./instrument-chassis`, `./slider` among 74 export subpaths, all three hand-rolled instead as a `contenteditable` `<h3>`, a `Card`, and a local rail); and the shown-channel set (three derivations, two of which disagree on alpha's `max`, and two write clocks). The upstream enabler of the fourth is `demo/ui/` — nineteen one-line glass-ui forwarding barrels, forbidden by name at `docs/tranches/V/ARCHITECTURE.md:39`, which freeze the producer surface at a 2025 allow-list and render every primitive above invisible to a component author.

**The cure is an architectural transposition, not a patch, and it is ordered.** Stage A publishes the node `ARCHITECTURE.md:71` already declares and the tree lacks (`color/space-schema`) as an additive `4.1.0`; Stage B returns app-scoped state, the keyboard map and the pane dispatch to their owners and deletes `demo/ui/`; Stage C consumes `InstrumentChassis`, `NumberField` and `Slider` and makes the readout a pure `<output>` projection. **No stage is independently mergeable and Stage C may not precede Stage A** — landing the axis against `PICKER_CHANNELS` would ship a fourth derivation in new markup. Cures are clean breaks: zero aliases, shims, dual paths or masking fallbacks; every call site moves in the same wave; the named kill list is normative.

**V.W48 is superseded in place as `MT-W48-PRIME`** — same row identity, same dependency edges, same discharge list (RF-28 F2 · PR-01/02/03/13/15-seed/23 · V-A137/A138/A140/A167/A120 · the archaeology), re-premised. Three of W48's stated premises are false at HEAD and are corrected: `PROPORTION-AUDIT §2` ruling 2's "Picker no longer nests a Card" (it nests one at `ComponentSliders.vue:25`; `--instrument-title-gap` resolves to `""`); Work-2's `seat.css:88` anchor (that line is the *horizontal* `padding-right`, the vertical reservation is `:89`, and at 1440 neither binds — the readout reservation does, at 55.41 px of a 70.42 px seam against a 14.87 px ceiling); and the completion clause "agree in one settled routed frame", which is single-frame and **passes with the readout/model desync fully present**. Eleven gates are specified, every one RED against today's tree. Opening a new wave row beside W48 is forbidden — it is re-booking under a different number.
result.dissent:
I expect JUROR-1 (correctness) and JUROR-3 (design/gestalt) to converge with me on the four BLOCKERs — the evidence is not in dispute. Six recorded disagreements:

1. **On scope (the sharpest).** A correctness-first reading cures the readout fusion by deleting `contenteditable` and adding `<input type="number">` — C's own proposed cure, and I read JURY-1 as endorsing it. **I dissent.** `@mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0` ships `./number-field` with `min`/`max`/`step`/`formatOptions`/`locale`/`invalid`/`readonly` and a typed numeric emit; a hand-rolled `<input type="number">` is edict-4 violation number two on the same surface and re-decides locale formatting the producer already owns. The editor must be `NumberField`, and it cannot be *seen* until `demo/ui/` is deleted. **The forwarding-directory row and the bundle rows are therefore PREREQUISITES of the BLOCKER cure, not tidying — I will not accept a wave that lands the readout cure while `demo/ui/` stands.**

2. **On ordering.** Any juror who orders the instrument stage before the library stage is wrong by construction: `channelSet.ts` and `ChannelAxis.vue` both read the published `CHANNEL_DOMAIN`, and landing them against `PICKER_CHANNELS` ships a fourth derivation in new markup — exactly the trap W48 §Work-3 already walks into by making "W21 numeric fields the sole editors" on top of the shared single-timer debounce.

3. **On J2-A17 (WebGL/settle).** C filed it as a hypothesis and would retire it. **I dissent:** against the committed artifact the confound is gone and the anomaly survived — 1 of 60, the *only* console error in the entire matrix, 4.50× the next-worst settle and 5.52× the median, on the LCP route of the product. It gets a gate, not a footnote. If it persists on a production build it escalates to the glass-ui producer with the trace; it is never patched in the demo.

4. **On W48's identity.** I oppose any proposal to open a *new* wave row beside W48. W48 is superseded in place. A peer row while W48 stands is the forbidden re-booking wearing a different number, and it would leave a wave in the register whose completion evidence certifies a GREEN close over four live BLOCKERs.

5. **On J2-A20's comment.** I expect a design-axis juror to treat `SpectrumCanvas.vue:4-5`'s `role="img"` rationale as a stale note deleted alongside the attribute. **I dissent on emphasis:** it is a recorded ruling from a prior wave that reached a wrong conclusion ("a 2D field is not a linear slider, therefore it is an image") from a true premise. A 2D field is not one slider; it is two. If the wave deletes the attribute and leaves the reasoning anywhere in the tree or the register, the conclusion is re-derivable and A137 returns. Deleting the comment is a normative clause.

6. **Against my own seat's first pass, recorded rather than silently corrected.** That pass claimed synthetic `KeyboardEvent` probes are *always* a false green for the KeepAlive listener leak. My re-run refutes it: with a real chord fired first, the synthetic replay also returned `dp:true`. The true statement is worse — **the synthetic verdict is order-dependent**, green or red for the same defect depending on session history. I flag this because the first pass's stronger claim would have justified a *weaker* gate. Three of that pass's measurements also moved (shadow alpha 0.5→0.8, seam 69.92→70.42, reserve 54.90→55.41) and two challenger findings (D-03, C-13) had been left with **no disposition at all** — a no-re-booking violation I repaired as J2-A20/J2-A21. A juror who tallies rather than re-runs inherits these.

upheld.defect: The hero readout fuses three incompatible jobs into one DOM node: `contenteditable="true" role="textbox"` sits on a span whose children (`.fig-int`/`.fig-frac`) Vue owns and patches, and which is also the document's only heading. Any user edit replaces those nodes; every later patch writes into detached nodes and silently no-ops, so the cell is permanently orphaned from the vdom and displays a value that is not the color.
upheld.mechanism: Editing fused into display: the browser's text-entry mutation and Vue's vnode patching contend for the same subtree, so vnode-held element references go stale and patching becomes a no-op. Reproduced at 1440x900: after editing `l` to 45 and then driving the L slider 12x ArrowLeft, URL `lab(43.8% 20 30)`, title, all four `aria-valuetext` and the channel meter read 43.8 while the readout inks 45 with `cell0.innerHTML === "45"`. The never-edited cell 1 keeps its two Vue spans intact in the same frame — the in-run control proving this is the edit path, not the render path. Does not heal across a KeepAlive deactivate/activate cycle. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7, §4; PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.10.

upheld.defect: All five channels share ONE 500 ms debounce timer instance, so a numeric edit to one channel silently cancels a pending edit to another. User edits are destroyed with no error and no visual signal.
upheld.mechanism: Debounce over a multiplexed argument: `demo/shared/utils.ts:22-44` is a single-timer, last-args-win closure; `useColorPipeline.ts:209` creates one instance and `ColorPicker.vue:51` and `:233` route every channel through it. The `component` argument makes each call a distinct intent, so coalescing is data loss, not throttling. Reproduced from `lab(80% 20 30)`: typed 30 into `l`, 120 ms later 10 into `b`; final URL `lab(80% 20 10)` — `b` took 10, `l` is still 80, the 30 is gone. Unit arm against the real `debounce`: applied writes `[[80,"a"]]`.

upheld.defect: The window keydown listener is registered in `onMounted` and released only in `onUnmounted`, but the component lives inside `<KeepAlive>`, so leaving the picker deactivates rather than unmounts it and the global keyboard claim stays live on every other route.
upheld.mechanism: Wrong lifecycle pair for the host: `ColorPicker.vue:376-379`/`:381-385` under `PaneSlot.vue:120` `<KeepAlive :max>`. Reproduced: `#/` -> chord opens -> chord closes -> `#/browse` (picker has 0 nodes in the document) -> chord -> a live `[role=listbox]` RENDERS ON `/browse`, a route the picker does not own; returning to `#/` shows `aria-expanded="true"`. The deterministic synthetic arm reproduces the same on `/browse` and `/gradient` across two trials. The correct idiom is used in the same directory (`HeroBlob.vue:246` `onActivated`, explained at `:232-245`). The same hole leaves the 2000 ms and 500 ms debounces uncancelled on every view switch.

upheld.defect: The Cmd+K handler tests sampled global modifier STATE (`keys.cmd?.value && keys.k?.value`) rather than the event, so while Cmd is held and `k` has been seen without a keyup, every subsequent Cmd-modified keystroke is preventDefault'd and re-toggles the popover. There is no `e.repeat` guard.
upheld.mechanism: Chord detection via sampled held-state instead of event inspection (`ColorPicker.vue:263-266`): the predicate is true for the whole duration the keys are held, not for the one event that is the chord. Reproduced deterministically across two trials, fresh page each time, no keyup sent: round 1 never latches; round 2 returns `k:true a:true z:true k-repeat:true` with `listbox 1`. Cmd+A and Cmd+Z are swallowed and the dropdown toggles on unrelated keystrokes; `k-repeat:true` is the missing repeat guard, measured. NARROWED against C-5 and against my own first draft: unmodified keys are NOT swallowed (`z`/`Escape`/`ArrowLeft`/`a` with metaKey false all pass, `defaultPrevented false`, `listbox 0`) because useMagicKeys clears `cmd` from each event's modifier state. The sink is bounded to Cmd-modified chords — still global over every route.

upheld.defect: Alpha is structurally excluded from the headline while the channel rail displays it, so the flagship readout describes a colour the instrument is not holding; and the reservation table budgets an alpha cell that can never render.
