waveSpec.title: Picker Instrument, re-premised — the flagship transposition (supersedes W48)
waveSpec.scope: demo/picker/** · demo/color-session/** · demo/color-picker/App.vue (mount + provide wiring) · demo/shell/{PaneSlot.vue,usePaneRouter.ts,dock/**} · demo/ui/** (deletion) · src/color/{index.ts,model.ts} + src/subpaths/color.ts · test/** + e2e/** · one glass-ui producer relay (Slider thumb seat; InstrumentChassis consumption). Preconditions before any Work step: (1) re-premise PROPORTION-AUDIT §2 ruling 2, whose opening premise "Because Picker no longer nests a Card…" is false at HEAD; (2) re-resolve every W48 source anchor against HEAD (seat.css:88 is padding-right; the reservation PR-01 names is :89); (3) do not re-mint the Blob b₀ reconstruction — the phantom-gate HEAL packet and the pinned v-blob-b0-26-ref-w40 tag are IMMUTABLE under the epoch rule and carry forward unchanged. Work in transposition order, each step a clean break with no alias, shim, dual path or masking fallback: 1) split the fused headline into three owners — shell owns one route <h1>, the readout becomes a labelled non-live <output> with no contenteditable/role=textbox/tab stop, editing moves whole into the shared domain-neutral axis composition over BI Slider which owns commit/cancel/clamp/error; 2) move the edit session and action-bar contract into color-session, provided by App beside COLOR_MODEL_KEY, Dock injects — defineExpose to 0, colorPickerRef and whenColorPickerReady and both fallback arms deleted, applyExternalColor/applyColorString reconciled into one operation; 3) kill the global keyboard claim — a shell-owned keyboard map registered once at the composition root testing the EVENT (e.key === "k" && (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && !e.repeat), useMagicKeys deleted, any KeepAlive'd-leaf listener uses onActivated/onDeactivated; 4) invert timer ownership — onScopeDispose inside useColorPipeline owns the debounces, the picker cancels nothing it did not create and clears the two ids it owns, the 120 ms and 850 ms literals become animationend or token reads; 5) publish SPACE_SCHEMA/SPACE_IDS/makeColor/isAnyColor through src/color/index.ts to src/subpaths/color.ts, extend SPACE_SCHEMA.channels to {key,min,max,unit,hue}, promote withChannel/withAlpha/channelAt/clampToDomain, then delete buildColor, CSS_PICKER_SPACES, the channel-name/hue columns of PICKER_CHANNELS and valueDomain.ts; 6) collapse the parse boundary — parseColor returns the library's Result, call sites branch, the hex regex is deleted, one color-session displaySpace module owns {resolve,format,parse,channels} collapsing 11 === "hex" sites to 1, and the verdict surfaces in a picker-local role="status"; 7) transpose to the producer InstrumentChassis with its stage/inspector/action regions, collapse the inner veil Card to a plain material region, retire About as Picker's companion, picker header owns the sole selector; 8) close the seam and the pair by token consumption — delete --readout-lines, align-content:flex-end and the static line table, consume P122 --instrument-title-gap as G, one shared P019 paired clamp with Fira Code on the headline arm unconditionally, author the tuple break policy explicitly; 9) producer relay: invisible ≥24x24 seat on the glass-ui Slider thumb with the painted glyph unchanged at its 12 px rung, relayed to the standing glass-ui BH inbox; 10) author the dark scheme — restrained-neutral chrome, an ambient field that darkens with the scheme, a Blob luminance ceiling bound to the specimen's; 11) excise the dead surface including useHeaderCondense whole, and make componentFor() exhaustive over LeftPane and throw on an unknown name; 12) delete demo/ui/ — all 19 directories, all 90 import sites rewritten to @mkbabb/glass-ui and its declared subpaths; 13) replace the vacuous test gate with the behavioural suite the gates require.

result.addendumClause:
V·addendum — Picker instrument (`demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue`), re-premised.

W48 as written is RETIRED and superseded by W48′, which carries W48's entire visual mandate forward unchanged — V-A137, V-A138, PR-01..03, `hide-indicator`, and the pinned Blob b₀ reconstruction (`v-blob-b0-26-ref-w40`, IMMUTABLE under the epoch rule) — and adds the five BLOCKER mechanisms no wave in the arc owns. W48 could not have closed: no clause of it touches `defineExpose`, the `colorPickerRef` service-locator, the picker's four illegal import edges, the mobile action-bar loss, the shared debounce instance, or the `onMounted`/`onUnmounted` pair under `<KeepAlive>`; and its completion check is single-frame, which cannot see the readout↔model divergence at all, because that divergence only appears on the SECOND mutation.

Two register premises are corrected as a precondition of execution, not as work inside it. (a) `PROPORTION-AUDIT §2` ruling 2 opens "Because Picker no longer nests a Card, BI P122 exposes `--instrument-title-gap`…". That premise is false at `c654824e`: the picker plate is a `Card`, it nests a second `Card` (`glass-quiet`, 469.1 × 190.3, from `ComponentSliders.vue:25`), and `--instrument-title-gap` computes to the empty string. The clause is RETIRED as premised and re-authored only against a tree where the producer `InstrumentChassis` has landed. (b) W48 §Work-2's anchor `seat.css:88` names `padding-right` (the Blob's horizontal bead clearance); the vertical reservation PR-01 actually names is `seat.css:89` `min-height`. Executed literally, the wave deletes the wrong axis. Every W48′ source anchor is re-resolved against HEAD before the wave opens.

The label→headline void is apportioned for the first time, and the apportionment reverses the cure order. At 1440 the readout's own reservation (`--readout-lines: 2` + `align-content: flex-end`) contributes +55.41 px of reserved-not-painted air while the Blob-derived `.title-row` `min-height` contributes exactly 0 px (73.12px minimum against an 84.97px rendered row — non-binding); at 390 the same minimum IS binding (73.12 vs 73.11) and the readout reservation is honest (−5.08 px). The measured seam is 70.42 px @1440 and 25.75 px @390 against a φG ≈ 14.87 px ceiling — 4.73× and 1.73×. Both arms fail; the desktop arm is entirely the readout's and none of the Blob's.

`--picker-header-rhythm` is retired rather than retuned: it was minted against a symptom whose cause is in another file, and after it the divergence is 2.73× with the loose arm moved from phone to desktop. The seam acquires exactly one owner — P122 `--instrument-title-gap`, consumed from the chassis.

W48′ is BORN RED: all 22 gates fail against `c654824e` today, each with a named falsifying input. Two of those gates (G-04, G-05) are specified as two-round, no-`keyup` keyboard probes because a single-round probe returns a false GREEN against a fully defective tree. Every visual gate carries a π obligation (pinned matrix, route and selector) and a DELTA obligation (the before/after scalar pair). result.dissent:
1. Any juror who carries L-13's harness-artifact finding forward is wrong on today's bytes. The report was re-run; 60 rows carry 15 distinct routes with allElements from 187 to 1741 and a total of one console error. Every conclusion drawn from the superseded uniformity — including "the picker contributes half the application's tap-target defects on all 60 captures" — must be struck. The picker's undersized targets remain a real defect on their own row (J-08); they are not a 60× artifact.

2. D's evidence gap must not be minuted as a standing record. REPORT.md and REPORT.json are on disk (mtime 14:21:43). Recording a phantom gap in the addenda would send the next seat hunting a file that exists.

3. I do not join D-02's charge that W48 sequences the PR-01 cure wrongly. The spec says in terms that "Removing only Blob height cannot close PR-01" and orders both deletions in one step. The real, and sufficient, defects are the off-by-one anchor and the un-quantified apportionment — both upheld as J-11. Precision matters here because the register is otherwise being asked to absorb a correction it does not need.

4. On severity I am harder than C on J-18 and softer than D on D-13. The debounce-cancel ownership inversion runs on every real unmount against app-shared timers — a live cross-consumer side effect, not a latent one, even though the specific dropped write is a hypothesis. Conversely the 2+1 orphan break is a consequence of the unauthored break policy, not an independent defect, and should not carry its own row into the addenda.

5. I decline to treat J-06 as out of scope because it lives in `src/`. The library's public surface is defined by what its flagship consumer could not use. Any verdict that keeps this inside "demo cleanup" leaves the 17-case switch in the slider hot path and guarantees the next consumer rewrites it.

6. I dissent from C-5's "global keyboard sink", and from my own first draft of J-04. I measured it and it is false: with the predicate primed, unmodified `z`, `Escape`, `ArrowLeft` and `a` all pass through with defaultPrevented === false and the popover unchanged. `useMagicKeys` clears `cmd` from each event's modifier state, so the sink is bounded to Cmd-modified chords — still global over every route, serious, and enough. If another juror carries the stronger framing, they are carrying an unmeasured claim.

7. I dissent from any gate written as a single-round keyboard probe. Round 1 after load never latches the lazily-created magic-keys refs, so a one-round probe of the chord returns GREEN against a tree where the defect is fully present — I produced exactly that false GREEN twice before catching it. G-04 and G-05 are therefore specified as two-round, no-`keyup` probes, deterministic across two trials. This is the single most likely way for W48′ to close green while defective, and it is a gate-soundness matter, not a stylistic one.

8. I record one enlargement against all three challengers on J-08: measuring every focusable against the 24 px floor (rather than the slider thumbs alone) returns seven undersized stops, not four — the l/a/b rail tabs sit at 23.6–23.8 px on the inline axis while the alpha tab at 24.5 px passes. Any cure scoped to "the four thumbs" leaves three failures standing.

waveSpec.title: The Gestalt — proportion, seam, zoom reflow, state matrices and the frame budget of the flagship instrument
waveSpec.scope: Stage D is NOT a new row: it is W48, superseded in place as MT-W48-PRIME (jury-2's row identity, adopted rather than competed with). Stage D composes with Stage A (library boundary), Stage B (ownership) and Stage C (the instrument), and lands WITH Stage C in one atomic close — the chassis transposition and the proportion/zoom/motion obligations are one design decision in one diff, and no intermediate state is mergeable. Stage D owns the whole as experienced: proportion, rhythm, type pair, scheme, state matrices, target geometry and the frame budget. Concretely it binds Stage C's transposition to produce: (1) InstrumentChassis at the exact golden ratio with NO filler companion — About returns to a trailing route per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 line 58, and the stage takes the full width rather than being halved by a peer document (§3 line 42: 'an absent inspector leaves no filler'); (2) ONE reserve, or none — --readout-lines, align-content:flex-end and the static line table die, the .title-row blob minimum dies, and a genuinely wrapped tuple grows BELOW into feature-local flow; (3) the seam decided as ONE quantity on BOTH sides, with the lower arm sized to seat the stage's indicator (≥ its 14.3px overhang) so the specimen is never occluded — the air released above pays for the air owed below; (4) ONE paired clamp producing label = headline/√φ through floor, fluid AND every intermediate regime, with Fira Code on the headline arm and Fraunces on the identity arm; (5) contraction RETAINED and RE-CALIBRATED, not deleted — the sufficiency threshold moves from expandedH*0.5+16 to a viewport-relative predicate keyed to the header's share of the visible card; (6) a declared frame budget enforced on a production build; (7) producer-side target seats (glass-ui Slider thumb + the rail tab), relayed to the glass-ui BH inbox per the standing fond. Consumes (design canon, ≤2 per L3): VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.2, PROPORTION-AUDIT.md.

result.addendumClause:
**MT-W48-PRIME · Stage D — the gestalt clause (normative).**

The Picker instrument is composed, not accumulated. Its outer housing is the producer
`InstrumentChassis`; `Card` is not the route chassis and no `Card` nests inside it. The stage holds
the canon protagonist share (61.8033989% golden, or 66.6666667% preview-dominant); About is a
trailing route and never Picker's companion, and an absent inspector leaves no filler — the stage
takes the full width rather than being halved by a peer document.

The specimen is bounded by **one** seam quantity decided on **both** sides. The upper arm carries no
reservation for a worst case that has not materialised and no minimum derived from an ornament's
nominal footprint: `--readout-lines`, `align-content: flex-end`, the static line table and the
`.title-row` blob minimum are deleted, and a genuinely wrapped tuple grows *below* into
feature-local flow. The lower arm is sized to **seat the stage's own indicator** — no element of the
instrument may paint over the specimen's ink at any channel value, including `v = 1`. The ratio of
the two arms lies in `[1/φ, φ]` at every reference matrix. The air released above pays for the air
owed below; these are one move.

Identity and specimen resolve from **one** paired clamp, holding `label = headline / √φ` through
floor, fluid and every intermediate regime — not only at the endpoints — with Fraunces on the
identity arm and Fira Code on the headline arm. The readout is a labelled, non-heading, non-live
`<output>`; the route's single `<h1>` is owned by the shell; the instrument has no inline editor.
The share identity — `location.hash` and `document.title` — carries the space's declared least
count and never more, by whichever path the colour was reached.

The instrument degrades honestly. At 200% and 400% zoom at least one operable channel control is in
the first settled paint, before any scroll, and the header is at most 45% of the card's visible box;
no header minimum may stand outside the zoom reflow. The action-bar command set is identical at
1440, 720@2 and 390 — the desktop/mobile layout switch is not a licence to drop commands. Under
`dir=rtl` the numeric tuple keeps model order with each unit bound to its number, and the spatial
indicator stays inside its plate. Under `forced-colors` the readout retains a non-colour visual
grammar and the protagonist retains a non-shadow differentiator from every peer plate. The dark
scheme is authored, not inherited: the ambient field darkens with the scheme, chrome uses the
restrained neutral pole, and an inert ornament never exceeds the specimen's luminance.

The instrument declares a **frame budget** and meets it on a production build: at most 20% of frames
during the primary pointer interaction exceed 16.7ms, with route TBT and GL-context count baselined
at wave open. Operable target geometry is separate from painted optics — every focusable inside the
chassis is at least 24x24 CSS px while its glyph keeps its optical rung — and that separation is
implemented in the glass-ui producer (`Slider`, rail tab), never as a demo-local override, and
relayed to the glass-ui BH inbox.

Whole-header contraction is **retained and re-calibrated, not deleted**: its sufficiency predicate
is keyed to the header's share of the visible card rather than to absolute overflow, so it serves
the phone band as well as the zoom bands it already serves.
result.dissent:
**I dissent from jury-2's MT-W48-PRIME Stage C, and from jury-1's J-15 and G-19, on one instruction: "`useHeaderCondense` deleted."**

Both siblings adopted CHALLENGE-C's C-7 verdict that the composable is unreachable dead code (jury-1 books it UPHELD_REPRODUCED and asserts its absence in G-19; jury-2 orders it deleted in Stage C and lists it on the kill-list). That verdict was measured only in the phone band. I re-ran the reachability witness myself this session (`probe-j3-gestalt-2.mjs` ARM A):

    720x450@2  overflow 223 > required 123.3  → gateOpens TRUE  → condensed TRUE  header 214.67 → 102.55  (−52%)
    360x225@4  overflow 415 > required 107.8  → gateOpens TRUE  → condensed TRUE  header 183.52 →  86.84  (−53%)
    390x844    overflow   0 · 390x600 overflow 64 · 320x568 overflow 89   all < ≈108 → gateOpens FALSE

The composable is not dead. It is the only mechanism in the component that reclaims header space at the zoom levels VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.2 and W48's own Completion clause make normative — precisely the matrices where GD-1 measures the header at 63.9% and 165.3% of the visible card. C-7's premise, "at every band where the picker is usable", excluded the zoom bands, which is where the picker is *least* usable. **Executing the deletion would regress WCAG 1.4.4 and make GD-1 strictly harder to pass, in the name of removing dead code.**

The correct action is **re-calibration, not deletion**: replace the sufficiency predicate `overflow > expandedH*0.5 + threshold` — unreachable in the 0–89px overflow band real phones produce — with a viewport-relative predicate keyed to the header's share of the visible card, which is the quantity GD-1 actually gates. The narrower defect (the mis-calibrated threshold) I uphold inside J3-4. If the executing session deletes the composable anyway, GD-1 must be re-baselined first and the loss of the 52% contraction recorded explicitly as accepted damage.

Three lesser disagreements, none of which changes any disposition:

1. **Jury-2's G7 and G8, and jury-1's equivalents, sample too few arms.** G7 asserts the type pair at 1440/390/320 and passes over the 720 regime where I measure 0.7291 (−0.0571 from 1/√φ). G8 asserts four 12x24 thumbs and passes over three rail tabs at 23.64–23.84 x 24.36, which miss the floor by 0.16–0.36px and pass a four-row assertion. GD-6 and GD-7 widen both; the widening is additive and contradicts no sibling row.
2. **Both siblings frame the display↔URL divergence as a consequence of the contenteditable** and prescribe deleting the writer. Measured (J3-6, reproduced twice), the divergence is reachable by the slider keyboard path alone, with no contenteditable in the interaction: `lab(13.6% 31.235817145191 9.621676412624 / 82.7%)`. Their cure is necessary and not sufficient; GD-8 is written to stay RED after their cure lands if the serialiser is untouched.
3. **No sibling gated the seam's lower arm.** J3-16 (new, mine) measures the spectrum thumb painting 4.38–5.19px over the specimen's ink at all three matrices, because its 14.3px overhang exceeds the 9.19px seam. A cure satisfying only `I_after ≤ min(φG, I_before − G)` leaves this present.

On everything else — the fused node, the ownership inversion, the library boundary, the chassis transposition, the parse boundary, the adoption of `MT-W48-PRIME` as the row identity rather than opening a competing wave, and **APOTHEOSIS_REQUIRED** — I concur with jurors 1 and 2 without reservation.

defects.mechanism: Error-contract ownership inversion: the library owns 'this may fail, here is why' (Result<T,E>); the demo bridge owns 'convert that to an exception'; the demo shell owns no recovery. The contract dies between hop one and hop two, and the only recovery mechanism is mounted one level too low to fire.

defects.proposedCure: Architectural, not a patch. Independently, hoist ErrorBoundary ABOVE App.vue — wrap <App/> at the createApp mount site in the boot entry — which is the only position from which a root-setup throw is catchable. Born-RED gate: navigate the URL above and assert #app innerText length > 0 with zero page errors.

One resolution path, generated from one source, for both vite and tsc; a break in the exports map then actually fails the typecheck. Separately fix vite-plugin-dts rollupTypes so dist/subpaths/css.d.ts emits no _2 shadow declarations and the local build is byte-identical to the published artifact.

defects.defect: sliderWrapperEls leaks detached DOM subtrees for the lifetime of the page. The template ref callback guards `if (el)` and so never performs the unmount delete; the map is keyed by bare channel letter, which is reused across the 17 spaces, so non-shared keys strand pointing at detached reka SliderRoot subtrees.
defects.evidence: ComponentSliders.vue:56 — `:ref="(el: any) => { if (el) sliderWrapperEls[component] = el as HTMLElement }"`. Measured live by reading the component's own setupState: initial {"gateCount":21,"mapKeys":4,"keys":["l","a","b","alpha"],"detached":0,"liveSliders":4}; after 8 space switches {"gateCount":21,"mapKeys":9,"keys":["l","a","b","alpha","r","g","c","h","w"],"detached":5,"detachedKeys":["a","b","r","g","w"],"liveSliders":4} — 9 entries for 4 live sliders, 5 hard refs to detached DOM. Two consumers iterate the poisoned map: useSliderTouchGates.ts:53 attachSliderListeners() binds FIVE listeners per entry on every space change; useSliderAnnouncements.ts:37 apply() does a querySelector + setAttribute per entry on EVERY value edit (9 DOM queries for 4 live thumbs) and computes sliderValueText for channels absent from the current space.
defects.mechanism: A manual mirror of the render tree's identity, hand-maintained by a callback that implements only half the ref contract (Vue calls it with null on unmount and the guard swallows it). The render tree already knows which channels are live; the map re-derives it and gets it wrong.
defects.reproduction: `node scratchpad/probe6.mjs` — Playwright chromium, goto http://localhost:9000/#/, then read `document.querySelector('.sliders-console').__vueParentComponent` walking up to the instance whose setupState has sliderWrapperEls; count Object.keys and those failing document.contains(). Drive 8 space switches by setting location.hash to #/?space=<s>&color=<c> for rgb, hsv, oklch, kelvin, jzazbz, ictcp, hwb, xyz with 700ms settle.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the map. The strips are a v-for over a known list — bind a single array `useTemplateRef` (Vue 3.5's array-ref form), which Vue itself keeps in exact correspondence with the rendered rows. Zero manual bookkeeping, strand-free by construction. Both downstream consumers then iterate exactly the live strips.

defects.defect: 21 glass-ui useTouchGate() instances are eagerly allocated at setup — the union of every channel key across all 17 color spaces — when at most 4 are ever live. The union-by-bare-key is also a semantic collision by construction.
defects.evidence: useSliderTouchGates.ts:31-40 — `const ALL_COMPONENTS = new Set([...Object.values(PICKER_CHANNELS).flatMap(ch => ch.map(({key}) => key)), "alpha"]); for (const comp of ALL_COMPONENTS) sliderGates[comp] = useTouchGate();`. Measured: gateCount: 21, liveSliders: 4 (same probe as L-4). 17 gates with their own refs and timer machinery are permanently idle, allocated on every picker mount including the whole mobile matrix. Collision: per picker-color.ts:52-70, `b` is simultaneously sRGB blue, HWB blackness, Lab b-axis and OKLab b-axis; `a` is both Lab and OKLab a-axis — they share one gate object.
defects.mechanism: Allocation keyed to the conceivable channel space rather than the rendered one, plus an identity (the bare letter) that is not unique across spaces. It is benign only because exactly one space renders at a time — an invariant nothing enforces.
defects.reproduction: Same probe as L-4: read setupState.sliderGates and count Object.keys → 21, against document.querySelectorAll('.channel-slider').length → 4.
defects.proposedCure: Gates belong to a rendered strip, not to a conceivable channel. Create them inside the strip abstraction (L-4's cure), keyed by the strip's identity and disposed with it. The PICKER_CHANNELS-union import then disappears from this composable entirely.

defects.defect: The component owns an unscoped global <style> that deliberately styles three sibling components it does not contain — and the mechanism does not work: its transition is deterministically overridden by the scoped style of its principal consumer. A second home for the same class exists in ExtractControls.vue.
defects.evidence: ComponentSliders.vue:238 opens `<style>` (not scoped) with a comment at :243-247 naming the intent to reach SpectrumCanvas, ExtractControls and PointerDebug. Computed style measured on /#/: {"present":true,"outlineWidth":"3px","outlineStyle":"solid","transition":"box-shadow","borderRadius":"12px","cls":"spectrum-picker … touch-gate-target"} — transitionProperty is box-shadow, NOT the outline-color declared at ComponentSliders.vue:256. Specificity: `.touch-gate-target` (0,1,0) vs SpectrumCanvas's scoped `.spectrum-picker[data-v-ad23e00d]{…transition:box-shadow…}` (0,2,0) — the scoped rule wins deterministically. CSSOM enumeration on /#/extract shows BOTH homes live: `.touch-gate-target { outline: transparent solid 3px; … transition: outline-color …; }` (ComponentSliders, unscoped) AND `.touch-gate-target[data-v-bfbc09b0] { border-radius: var(--radius-pill); }` (ExtractControls.vue:139-142, scoped).
defects.mechanism: Module-boundary inversion — a leaf SFC exporting global CSS for siblings — compounded by a cascade impossibility: an unscoped rule can never outrank the scoped rule of the component it is trying to reach, so the gate-activation fade is dead on SpectrumCanvas (the outline snaps).
defects.reproduction: `node scratchpad/probe4.mjs` — goto /#/ and /#/extract, getComputedStyle on document.querySelector('.touch-gate-target') reading outlineWidth/outlineStyle/transitionProperty/borderRadius. `node scratchpad/probe5.mjs` — walk document.styleSheets and print every cssText containing .touch-gate-target or .spectrum-picker per route.
defects.proposedCure: `.touch-gate-target` / `.touch-gate-active` are a global interaction affordance, so they belong in the global sheet: one block in demo/styles/, owned by no component. Delete the unscoped block from ComponentSliders.vue and the duplicate from ExtractControls.vue. The transition then sits at the same cascade level as everything else and actually animates. This satisfies edict 6 — the animation is MOVED, never deleted. BLOCKED: both files are glass-v8 pinned receivers.

defects.defect: controls/ reaches across into display/'s private internal file for a concept neither module owns. The borrowed function ignores half its own signature, and its docblock cites a library API that no longer exists.
defects.evidence: ComponentSliders.vue:100 — `import { readoutDecimals } from "../../display/ColorComponentDisplay/readoutReservation";`, used at :169. readoutReservation.ts is by its own 40-line docblock a typography line-packing table (DOT_CH = 0.45, SIGN_CH = 0.65, greedy line-count, fit coefficient). Its export at :62 is `export function readoutDecimals(space: string, _component: string): number { return INTEGER_LEAST_COUNT.has(space) ? 0 : 1; }` — `_component` is declared and IGNORED, yet both call sites (ComponentSliders.vue:169, ColorComponentDisplay.vue:108) pass it. Its docblock :24-25 claims derivation "from the library's own COLOR_SPACE_RANGES + COLOR_SPACE_DENORM_UNITS"; `grep -rn "COLOR_SPACE_RANGES\|DENORM_UNITS" src/` returns NOTHING — it actually reads the demo's PICKER_CHANNELS at :43.
defects.mechanism: Wrong home for a concept. 'How many decimals does a channel of space S carry' is a property of the color space, not of a readout's ch-width reservation; the ignored _component parameter is the module admitting it does not own the concept. The stale docblock naming a dead pre-4.0 API is why readoutReservation.ts:26 and valueDomain.ts also cite getColorSpaceBound.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn readoutDecimals demo/` (9 hits, 2 external call sites); `grep -rn "COLOR_SPACE_RANGES\|DENORM_UNITS" src/` (empty); read readoutReservation.ts:62.
defects.proposedCure: `leastCount(space)` moves to demo/color-session/ beside PICKER_CHANNELS — or better, into the library per L-8 where the space taxonomy already lives. readoutReservation.ts then CONSUMES it like everyone else and shrinks to the ch-packing table it claims to be. The controls/ → display/ edge is deleted, not redirected; the unused _component parameter goes with it.

defects.defect: The library owns the color-space taxonomy but publishes no channel domain metadata, so the demo re-declares all 51 range literals by hand — and one constant already has two homes in two packages with no shared source.
defects.evidence: src/subpaths/color.ts (full surface read) exports SpaceId, ChannelsBySpace, 17 constructors — and NO range/unit metadata. demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:52-70 re-derives it: 17 spaces of literal min/max/unit, tied back only by `satisfies Record<SpaceId, readonly ChannelMeta[]>`. That knowledge is what makes the slider possible: ComponentSliders.vue:131 → normalizedChannel → picker-color.ts:160-163 `(channelNumber(color,key) - meta.min) / (meta.max - meta.min)`. Live duplication: kelvin ∈ [1000,40000] is enforced by the library at src/color/model.ts:91 (`if (space === "kelvin" && channels[0] !== "none" && (channels[0] < 1000 || channels[0] > 40000))`) AND re-declared by the demo at picker-color.ts:62 (`{ key: "kelvin", min: 1000, max: 40000, unit: "K" }`).
defects.mechanism: Split ownership of one concept across a package boundary. The library validates a domain it will not publish; the consumer must re-type it to build any control. They agree today by coincidence — widen the library's kelvin guard and the demo slider silently misnormalizes with no test, no type error and no signal. The other 16 spaces have no library counterpart at all, so nothing checks them.
defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "COLOR_SPACE_RANGES\|DENORM_UNITS\|CHANNEL_RANGES" src/` → empty; `grep -n "1000\|40000" src/color/model.ts` → line 91; read picker-color.ts:52-70; read src/subpaths/color.ts in full.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition. The library gains one small export under ./color: `export type ChannelSpec = Readonly<{ key: string; min: number; max: number; unit: "" | "%" | "deg" | "K"; hue?: true; leastCount: 0 | 1 }>; export const CHANNELS: Readonly<Record<SpaceId, readonly ChannelSpec[]>>;`. It is the natural home — the library already owns SpaceId and ChannelsBySpace, and model.ts:91 already enforces one bound. PICKER_CHANNELS becomes a re-export; readoutDecimals becomes spec.leastCount (killing L-7); the kelvin bound has one home; and any REAL consumer building a color slider gets the table instead of re-typing 51 numbers.

defects.defect: demo/color-session/valueDomain.ts is a 3-line pure alias of clampPickerColor whose 46-line preamble describes a deleted architecture.
defects.evidence: valueDomain.ts:47-49 is the entire executable content: `export const clampColorToSpaceDomain = (color: PickerColor): PickerColor => clampPickerColor(color);` — two call sites, useColorPipeline.ts:51 and :67. Its docblock cites COLOR_SPACE_RANGES, getColorSpaceBound, and `src/units/color/conversions/kelvin.ts`. `ls src/` → color css easing.ts foundation quantize.ts subpaths transform value.ts vite-env.d.ts; `ls src/units` → "No such file or directory".
defects.mechanism: A tombstone module: a rename kept alive after the mechanism it named was replaced. Owner edict 2 forbids aliases outright, and the doc is load-bearing misinformation — it is the source of the same dead-API citation in readoutReservation.ts:26.
defects.reproduction: `cat demo/color-session/valueDomain.ts`; `ls src/units`; `grep -rn "clampColorToSpaceDomain" demo/ test/`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the file; call clampPickerColor directly at the two sites. Move the surviving TRUE paragraphs (the hue-wrap rule; the kelvin-is-physical rule) into clampPickerColor's own docblock where they describe live code. test/value-domain-clamp.test.ts exists and re-points to the real name.

defects.defect: componentEntries builds a [string, unknown] tuple whose second element is never read, via two casts that erase the ChannelMeta type.
defects.evidence: ComponentSliders.vue:120-125 maps PICKER_CHANNELS to `[meta.key, meta] as [string, unknown]` plus a synthetic `["alpha", {…}] as [string, unknown]`. Both consumers discard element 1: :34 `componentEntries.map(([c]) => c)` and :52 `v-for="[component] in componentEntries"`. The meta payload is never read anywhere in the file.
defects.mechanism: Dead structure defended by casts. The two `as [string, unknown]` casts exist solely to type a shape nobody consumes, and in doing so erase ChannelMeta — the one place the component could have obtained min/max/unit without the L-7 cross-feature import.
defects.reproduction: Read ComponentSliders.vue:34, :52, :120-125 — the tuple's second element has no reader in the file.
defects.proposedCure: `const componentEntries = computed<string[]>(() => [...PICKER_CHANNELS[currentColorSpace.value].map(m => m.key), "alpha"])`. Both casts and the synthetic alpha object disappear. If the meta is wanted later, keep it TYPED (ChannelMeta), never unknown. BLOCKED: pinned file.

result.axis: design (CHALLENGE-D) — visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context variant) — the explicitly declared seat model, not inherited
result.strongestDefect: D-2 — the channel drag thumb is a 12px-wide target in EVERY render matrix (12×24 desktop/narrow/fine-pointer-390/forced-colors; 12×44 coarse), failing WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8's 24×24 minimum on the inline axis even in the coarse case the mechanism exists for. The `@media (pointer: coarse) .channel-slider::before` hit extension is aimed at the wrong element and the wrong axis: it sits on the SliderRoot and grows only the block axis, so it enlarges the track-TAP zone (a press there is a value jump) and never the thumb-DRAG zone. Independently corroborated by the shipped visual matrix — REPORT.json lists all four thumbs under smallTapTargets in all four Safari matrices. The source comment at :335-344 claims the rung is "preserved by HIT-AREA EXTENSION, not row inflation"; measured, the inverse holds on both counts (desktop row 35.84px around a 24px control = +49% dead block, AND the target still fails).
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, but seven attacked-and-survived areas are recorded as positive evidence in the report's "Negative proof" section: (1) reduced motion is CORRECT — `.stagger-children` lives entirely inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` (animations.css:44) and measured under reducedMotion:"reduce" the first row child computes animation-name:"none", opacity:1, resolving directly to final geometry per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6; (2) I suspected the component's `transition: outline-color var(--duration-normal)` had lost the cascade (an early reading on .touch-gate-target returned transition-property:box-shadow) and DISPROVED it — re-measuring the four channel gates specifically returned {transitionProperty:"outline-color", transitionDuration:"0.3s"} on all four, exactly as declared; the earlier reading was the SpectrumCanvas gate at index 0, so no finding was filed; (3) aria-live="off" on the meter is correct and required by name in VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7; (4) aria-valuetext is present, unit-aware and space-disambiguated on every thumb across all nine spaces probed; (5) REPORT.json shows overflowX:0 and pageErrors:[] for route /#/ in all four Safari matrices (the one console error, "WebGL: context lost", belongs to the Blob canvas); (6) verbatimModuleSyntax is clean — the SFC imports no types, composables use `import type` and inline `type WatchSource`; (7) the 400-LoC god-module cap is honoured honestly at 395 lines with the touch-gate and announcement clusters genuinely encapsulated in composables/, not shuffled.

defects.defect: The "ONE container-scaled rhythm law" (:318-333) is a two-state step function whose clamp ceilings are structurally unreachable dead code. The comment claims it retired a hard `<lg` band switch for a rhythm that is "a smooth function of width, never two hand-tuned states". It is not: the `cqi` container (.pane-wrapper, shell.css:83) is itself capped at `--pane-max: 32rem` (foundation.css:441), so the ceilings 2.625rem/42px (needs 600px container) and 0.5rem/8px (needs 533px) can never be reached, and the shipped rhythm has exactly TWO values switching at the pane-layout breakpoint. The discontinuity survived at reduced amplitude (1.83x -> 1.12x); only its disguise changed. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.7 ("No desktop-tight/mobile-airy fork and no breakpoint pile") and PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.8 ("Real rendered relation wins over token intent").
defects.evidence: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:328-333. Measured .pane-wrapper inline-size and resolved rhythm (scratchpad/CSD-probe.mjs -> CSD-out.json): 1440 -> container 512.00, min-block-size 35.84px, row-gap 7.68px | 3440 -> container 512.00, 35.84px, 7.68px (BYTE-IDENTICAL to 1440) | 390 -> container 358.00, 7cqi=25.06 -> FLOOR 32.00px, 1.5cqi=5.37 -> FLOOR 6.00px | 320 -> container 288.00, 7cqi=20.16 -> FLOOR 32.00px, gap FLOOR 6.00px. Container cap: `--pane-max: 32rem` at demo/styles/foundation.css:441; grid clamp recorded at demo/DESIGN.md:358. Same clamp copy-duplicated at demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:216.
defects.mechanism: a fluid unit measured against a container that is itself clamped to a constant — the fluidity is nominal, the clamp arms are unexecutable, and the real breakpoint moved from a media query into the layout
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/CSD-probe.mjs against http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(92%25+88.8+20+/+82.7%25) at viewports 1440/3440/390/320; read paneWrapperWidth, rowGap, stripMinBlock
defects.proposedCure: Delete both cqi clamps. The row is not a function of the pane container (a clamped constant) but of the control it houses: `min-block-size: calc(var(--slider-track-block) + 2 * var(--console-row-air))` with the track metric fed by the producer and the air a glass-ui spacing rung. If two densities are genuinely wanted they are a named `density` rung declared once on the producer Slider/Card, not a clamp pretending to be continuous. One home for the rhythm, consumed by ConfigSliderPane instead of cloned.

defects.defect: The channel drag thumb is a 12px-wide operable target in every render matrix, failing WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (24x24 minimum) on the inline axis. The `@media (pointer: coarse) .channel-slider::before` hit-area extension addresses the wrong element and the wrong axis: it sits on the SliderRoot and grows only the block axis (`inset-inline: 0; block-size: max(100%, 2.75rem)`), so it enlarges the track-TAP zone (a press there is a value jump) and never the thumb-DRAG zone (a press there is a grab). PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.7 ("Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities") is the exact law broken — all three were conflated into one pseudo-element on the wrong box.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:345-357. Measured [role="slider"] rects (scratchpad/CSD-probe.mjs): desktop-1440 12x24 (::before content:none) | desktop-3440 12x24 | narrow-320 12x24 | mobile-390 fine-pointer 12x24 (::before content:none — no extension at all) | mobile-390 COARSE 12x44 (::before content:"", height 44px — height moved, WIDTH STAYED 12) | forced-colors-1440 12x24. Independently corroborated by the shipped matrix: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json lists all four thumbs under smallTapTargets in ALL FOUR Safari matrices, e.g. {"w":12,"h":24,"tag":"span","label":"L channel"} (safari-desktop-light /#/) and {"w":12,"h":44,"tag":"span","label":"ALPHA channel"} (safari-mobile-dark /#/). Desktop row block = 35.84px around a 24px control (+49% dead block) despite the comment at :335-344 claiming the rung is preserved "not [by] row inflation".
defects.mechanism: a consumer pseudo-element attempting to resize a node the consumer does not own — the affordance is extended on the ancestor while the target the interaction actually requires (the thumb) is untouched
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/CSD-probe.mjs; compare thumb rects across the `mobile-390` and `mobile-390-coarse` contexts. Or read REPORT.json results[].probe.a11y.smallTapTargets for route /#/ in any of the four Safari matrices.
defects.proposedCure: Thumb geometry is a producer concern. glass-ui `Slider` must expose a density/thumb rung whose coarse arm is >=24px inline (44 preferred) AT THE ROOT; the consumer then deletes `::before` outright rather than compensating around it. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8; lead the BH/BI relay packet with this row since it is the one with a shipped accessibility consequence.

defects.defect: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5's named domain-neutral axis composition ("label, unit, reserved live value, optional numeric entry ... feature waves own their domain arrangement, NOT new slider mechanics") is not adopted. The label lives in a separate sibling column (ConsoleRail) inside its own ring, bound to its row by vertical coincidence alone — no <label for>, no aria-labelledby, and a different name in the a11y tree (see D-3). There is no unit column (unit is glued into the value string) and no numeric entry. Meanwhile the consumer adds FOUR pieces of new slider mechanics in CSS. Two structural boundaries also wrap one group (console Card edge + rail ring) against PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-05.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:33-38 (rail as detached sibling column), :84-86 (unit glued into meter string), and the four consumer mechanics at :349 (::before hit extension), :384 (::after notch), :363-383 (cursor grammar), :253-274 (gate outline + inset box-shadow). Law quoted from docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §5 and PR-05 in docs/tranches/V/PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §4. Visible in frames/desktop-1440-focus.png and frames/D-oklch-ragged-track.png: the console Card edge and the rail's pill ring draw the same grouping twice.
defects.mechanism: a composition the design system already names was re-invented per-feature, so every element of it (label binding, unit, reservation, target size) became a consumer problem solved four different ad-hoc ways
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a spec-conformance reading, not a runtime failure. The downstream runtime failures it causes (D-3 name divergence, D-4 reservation breach, D-2 target size) each have their own reproduction.
defects.proposedCure: This is the gestalt cure the other findings converge on. Make the channel row `label · track · unit · value` ONE composition owned by the producer, so the label is programmatically bound to its slider, the unit has a column, the reservation is a producer concern, and the four consumer mechanics have a legitimate home. The letter rail then becomes what it should have been — a NAVIGATION affordance over an already-labelled instrument, not the instrument's only label. This is the P5 letter-rail primitive seam the file itself books at :22-24. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8.

defects.defect: Two different accessible names for the same control, produced by two code paths one directory apart. The template hand-rolls `${component.toUpperCase()} channel` while `channelLabel(space, component)` — the correct, space-disambiguated human name — already exists in the same directory and is already imported by the sibling composable. An AT reads name-then-value, producing "A channel, a axis 88.8". The component's own stated doctrine ("one voice, zero new state" :44; "ONE voice" :149) is broken in the one place a user hears it.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:63 vs demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/composables/sliderAnnouncement.ts:60-66. Measured pairs (scratchpad/CSD-probe2.mjs -> CSD-out2.json): lab aria-label='A channel' / aria-valuetext='a axis 88.8'; lab 'ALPHA channel' / 'Alpha 82.7%'; oklch 'H channel' / 'Hue 359.0deg'; hwb 'W channel' / 'Whiteness 10%' and 'B channel' / 'Blackness 10%'. The same divergence is captured in the shipped matrix: REPORT.json smallTapTargets rows carry label 'A channel', 'B channel', 'ALPHA channel'. sliderAnnouncement.ts:11-14 documents exactly why the bare key is wrong ("`b` is Blue in rgb, Blackness in hwb, and the b* axis in lab/oklab").
defects.mechanism: the same fact (a channel's human name) computed twice by two owners, so the correct implementation exists but only one consumer calls it
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/CSD-probe2.mjs; read spaces[].rows[].label vs spaces[].rows[].valuetext for any space
defects.proposedCure: `:aria-label="channelLabel(currentColorSpace, component)"`; delete `toUpperCase()`. One name function, one voice — which is the doctrine the file already claims. Not glass-blocked.

defects.defect: The meter's hand-rolled `min-width: 6ch` under-reserves the widest legal string, and the overflow is absorbed by the CONTROL rather than the readout: in oklch the hue row's track is 17.71px (5.2%) shorter than its three siblings. The instrument's rows are visibly ragged, and the pixel length of a track IS that channel's resolution, so the reflow lands in the worst possible place. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4: "Live numbers use tabular figures and reserve their widest legal representation so value changes never reflow the settled chassis."
defects.evidence: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:313 (`min-width: 6ch`). Measured 9-space sweep at 1440 (scratchpad/CSD-probe2.mjs -> CSD-out2.json): oklch hue meter renders '359.0deg' (8 chars) at 70.80px against the 53.09px reservation, and that row's track is 320.95px vs 338.66/338.66/338.64px for L/C/alpha — TRACK SPREAD 17.71px. Every other space measured spread <=0.02px (lab 0.02, lch 0.02, hsl 0.01, hsv 0.01, hwb 0.01, rgb 0.00, hex 0.00, kelvin 0.00). Visual witnesses captured by this seat: frames/D-oklch-ragged-track.png (LTR) and frames/D-rtl-meter-align.png (RTL). Aggravating: a derived per-space `ch` reservation table already exists at demo/picker/display/ColorComponentDisplay/readoutReservation.ts (header :17-19: "STATIC, derived at module scope ... no nudged constants") and this very file imports `readoutDecimals` from it at :100 while ignoring the adjacent machinery.
defects.mechanism: a nudged magic constant standing in for an existing derivation, so the format and the lock can disagree — and they do, for exactly the spaces whose unit token is two characters wide
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/CSD-probe2.mjs; compare spaces[space=oklch].rows[].track (320.95 vs 338.66) and rows[].meter (70.80 vs 53.09). Or open http://localhost:9000/#/?space=oklch&color=oklch(50%25%200.4%20359%20%2F%20100%25) at 1440.
defects.proposedCure: Derive the meter's reservation from the same per-(space, channel) table that owns the least count, so format and lock can never disagree: export `readoutCh(space, component)` beside `readoutDecimals` in readoutReservation.ts and feed `min-inline-size` from it. Delete the `6ch` constant. Not glass-blocked.

defects.defect: `hex` is an undesigned state that ships: the console renders four operable sliders with a permanently blank readout, and the screen-reader announcement degrades to a bare noun with no value. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 requires "the PERSISTENT per-channel meter"; in hex it is absent, leaving 53px x 4 rows of empty reserved column. The `sliderValueText` fallback documented as an edge guard fires for an entire first-class color space, so an AT user operating the hex console hears "Red" no matter where the thumb goes. The source declares hex out of scope at :157-158 ("its console is not this row's") — the probe falsifies that.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:157-173 and composables/sliderAnnouncement.ts:70-71. Measured at ?space=hex&color=%23ff8000 (scratchpad/CSD-probe2.mjs -> CSD-out2.json): consolePresent=true, 4 rows, meterText='' x4, aria-valuetext = 'Red'/'Green'/'Blue'/'Alpha' with NO value component. Visual witness captured by this seat: frames/D-hex-empty-meters.png — four ramps, zero numbers, empty reserved meter column at the right edge.
defects.mechanism: a state declared out of scope in a comment while the component still renders in it — the scope boundary exists only in prose, not in the render path
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/?space=hex&color=%23ff8000 and inspect .channel-meter textContent (all empty) and [role=slider] aria-valuetext ('Red','Green','Blue','Alpha'). Or node scratchpad/CSD-probe2.mjs and read spaces[space=hex].
defects.proposedCure: Stop claiming a readout the space cannot fill. hex has no per-channel model, so either the hex console reads the rgb projection — already the one voice its ramps are painted from, so this costs zero new state — or hex renders a different composition entirely (a single hex field, per PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.10's readout/editing separation). A persistent blank with reserved space around it is an omission, not a state. Not glass-blocked.

defects.defect: In forced colors the touch-gate's REST state paints a permanent 3px black ring and the ACTIVE state loses its entire visual delta. `outline: 3px solid transparent` relies on the colour being invisible, but outline-color is in the forced-colors adjustment set, so it becomes visible at rest. The active state's only two indicators are both colour-only and both erased: its outline-color color-mix is forced to the same black as rest, and its inset box-shadow is forced to `none`. Result: active is pixel-identical to rest. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 twice — "states are never color-only" and "Focus remains visibly distinct from selection in both schemes, FORCED COLORS and reduced transparency".
defects.evidence: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:253-257 (rest), :261-263 (active outline), :266-268 (active box-shadow). Measured under Playwright forcedColors:"active" at 1440 (scratchpad/CSD-probe.mjs -> CSD-out.json, key forced-colors-1440): gate outline-colors = [rgba(0,0,0,0), rgb(0,0,0), rgb(0,0,0), rgb(0,0,0), rgb(0,0,0)] — all four CHANNEL gates forced from transparent to opaque black at rest, outline-width 3px. box-shadow -> none per CSS Color Adjust 1 §3.2 forced-colors-adjust. Corroborated visually by frames/forced-colors-console.png: four identical black pill rings, no state differentiation.
defects.mechanism: encoding a state boundary in a colour channel the UA is specified to overwrite — the transparent-colour idiom inverts under forced-colors instead of degrading
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/CSD-probe.mjs; read out['forced-colors-1440'].gates[].outlineColor. Or launch Chromium with forced-colors emulation on http://localhost:9000/#/ and compare a gated vs ungated channel row.
defects.proposedCure: Rest must be `outline-style: none` (not a transparent colour), and the active state needs a non-colour channel — an outline-style/border-style switch or a producer `data-state` treatment that survives the adjustment. The durable home is the producer: the touch gate is a pointer-modality affordance, not a picker concept. Consumer patch is unblocked; the transposition is BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8.

defects.defect: The console claims the Instrument-veil material tier but reveals nothing, and pays a real 469x190 backdrop-filter compositing layer to reveal it. The source itself concedes the outcome ("read OPAQUE — only ~15% of the surviving field variation survives the blur") and books the actual cure out of the lane. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2 rules on exactly this case: "Glass earns its blur by revealing live content; OTHERWISE IT IS A NEUTRAL WELL", and its tier table assigns Specimen well = "opaque/quiet neutral stage". The console is a well wearing a veil, and the alpha override in D-8 is the symptom of tuning a material toward a tier it cannot occupy.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:25-31 (surface="veil" tier="quiet") and the self-indicting comment at :285-298. Measured on the console element in all matrices (scratchpad/CSD-probe.mjs): background-color = color(srgb 0.953656 0.920577 0.887731 / 0.443), backdrop-filter = blur(7px) saturate(1.4) brightness(1.02), rect 469.06 x 190.33 at 1440. Visually confirmed as a flat warm-cream rectangle on a pink plate in frames/desktop-1440-focus.png and frames/mobile-390-focus.png.
defects.mechanism: a material tier assigned by intent rather than by what the surface actually composites over, so the tier's cost is paid and its benefit is not delivered
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/CSD-probe.mjs; read consoleBg and consoleBackdrop at any matrix. Visual: frames/desktop-1440-focus.png.
defects.proposedCure: Pick a side — the middle is what produced the override. Either ColorPicker.vue's plate gets its clarity window (the veil becomes earned and the alpha override dies because the material finally does its job) or the console adopts `surface="opaque" tier="quiet"` and both the override and the backdrop cost are deleted. Must execute jointly with the picker-plate half as ONE wave, not two.

defects.defect: A per-instance redefinition of a glass-ui root token, scheme-forked by a `.dark` descendant selector on the element itself. This redefines the design system's quiet-glass token for one consumer element — the exact shape edict 5 forbids — and the comment names it without flinching ("a DIRECT `--glass-bg-quiet` override on the veil element"). Compounding: the `.dark` descendant fork means every future producer change to quiet-glass alpha silently skips this console in both schemes, and the substitution chain now has a consumer link in it.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:299 (`--glass-bg-quiet: color-mix(in srgb, var(--card) 42%, transparent)`) and :301-303 (`.dark .sliders-console { --glass-bg-quiet: ... 50% ... }`). Self-documented as a direct override at :291-294. Measured resolved value: background-color color(srgb 0.953656 0.920577 0.887731 / 0.443) at every matrix (scratchpad/CSD-probe.mjs).
defects.mechanism: a missing producer lever forged downstream — the consumer redefines a token it consumes, inverting the direction of the substitution chain
defects.reproduction: NONE required — the override is declarative at :299/:301-303; its resolved effect is measured as consoleBg alpha 0.443 in CSD-out.json.
defects.proposedCure: If quiet glass is wrong for instrument surfaces that is a producer rung — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2 already promises it ("denser neutral veil with NAMED ALPHA/CLARITY LEVERS"). The lever does not exist, so the consumer forged one. Land the lever in glass-ui and delete both rules. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8.

defects.defect: The entire <style> block is global but only one cluster in it has a justification. The comment legitimately justifies unscoping the touch-gate cluster (it must reach SpectrumCanvas/ExtractControls hosts outside this SFC's data-v-* scope), but the same global block then ships five names belonging to exactly one component. The cost is already realised: the rhythm clamp is duplicated verbatim into a second file, and the comment's own offer to share it was declined by copy-paste — so D-1's dead ceilings now reach two components instead of one.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:238 (`<style>` with no `scoped`), justification at :239-252 (touch-gate cluster only). Globally leaked private names: .sliders-console :283, .channel-meter :309, .channel-rows :328, .channel-strip :331, .channel-slider :346/:363/:375/:378-383/:384. Duplication witness: `min-block-size: clamp(2rem, 7cqi, 2.625rem)` appears verbatim at demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:216; the sharing offer is at ComponentSliders.vue:326-327 ("Offered to the ConfigSliderPane population (M-34) so the whole app has ONE rhythm source").
defects.mechanism: one legitimate exception used to justify an entire block, so private and shared surface area became indistinguishable and the shared piece got cloned instead of consumed
defects.reproduction: NONE required — grep -c 'clamp(2rem, 7cqi, 2.625rem)' across demo/ returns 2 (ComponentSliders.vue:332, ConfigSliderPane.vue:216).
defects.proposedCure: Split by audience, the only honest axis: a `scoped` block for the five private names, and the genuinely-shared touch-gate cluster promoted to a named utility in demo/styles/ where its three consumers can see it. Then the rhythm has one home and ConfigSliderPane consumes it instead of cloning it. Not glass-blocked.

defects.defect: `--type-mono-caption` does not exist anywhere in the tree; the meter's type role therefore falls through a masking fallback to `--type-caption`, a VIEWPORT-driven clamp, on a container-scoped instrument. Three consumers reference the phantom token with three DIFFERENT fallbacks, so one nominal role renders at different sizes across the app. Measured consequence: at a fixed 512px container the meter grows from 14.384px to 16.000px between 1440 and 3440, eating 5.97px of track from an instrument whose container moved by zero.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn -- "--type-mono-caption:" demo/ node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` returns 0 definitions. Live probe: getComputedStyle(:root).getPropertyValue('--type-mono-caption') = '' at every matrix (scratchpad/CSD-probe.mjs, tokens.typeMonoCaption='(UNDEFINED)'). Three divergent consumers: ComponentSliders.vue:310 falls back to `var(--type-caption)`; demo/shell/dock/DockStatusLamp.vue:54 and demo/palettes/browser/status/ApiOfflineChip.vue:47 both fall back to `0.6875rem`. Resolved token: `--type-caption: clamp(0.75rem, 0.71rem + 0.21vw, 1rem)` in glass-ui styles/typography/scale.css. Measured at fixed 512px container: 1440 -> font 14.384px, meter cell 53.09px, track 339.44px; 3440 -> font 16.000px, meter cell 59.06px, track 333.47px. The no-vw rule is stated at demo/styles/shell.css:79-81.
defects.mechanism: a fallback masking a token that was never minted, so three call sites silently disagree and the surviving value belongs to the wrong scaling axis
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/CSD-probe.mjs; compare out['desktop-1440'].meters[0].fontSize (14.384px) with out['desktop-3440'].meters[0].fontSize (16px) while paneWrapperWidth is 512.00 in both.
defects.proposedCure: Use the glass-ui role class VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4 names — `text-mono-small`, or `mono-caption` where the content is a caption — instead of a raw font-size var, and retire the phantom token's three fallbacks in one sweep so the role has one definition. Not glass-blocked.

defects.defect: RTL: the numeric column uses physical `text-align: right` (and physical `min-width`), so its alignment edge flips to the wrong side. The meter box mirrors to the left correctly, but the digits stay flush right — flush against the tracks, ragged against the card edge, the inverse of the LTR reading. Violates VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1 ("chrome, navigation and layout: logical inline/block direction follows the document"); §5.2's physical-axis carve-out covers scientific coordinate meaning, not the alignment of a label column.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:313-314 (`min-width: 6ch; text-align: right`). Measured at 390 with document.documentElement.dir='rtl' (scratchpad/CSD-probe2.mjs -> CSD-out2.json rtl block): rail x=310.0 w=31.7 (mirrors correctly to the right), track x=98.2 w=198.8, meter x=45.3 w=44.9, textAlign='right'. Visual witness captured by this seat: frames/D-rtl-meter-align.png. The file is otherwise logical throughout (min-block-size :332, inset-inline :352, block-size :355), making these the two physical holdouts.
defects.mechanism: physical alignment keywords in a layout role inside an otherwise logical stylesheet — correct in LTR by coincidence, inverted in RTL
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/CSD-probe2.mjs (sets dir='rtl' at 390 and reports railX/trackX/meterX/meterAlign), or open the picker at 390, run `document.documentElement.dir='rtl'` and inspect .channel-meter.
defects.proposedCure: `text-align: end`, `min-inline-size`. Not glass-blocked.

defects.defect: The meter inks the raw CSS unit token `deg` instead of the degree sign, contradicting the announcement module's own documented exemplar ("Hue 210°"). `%` already renders as a sign in the same column, so the meter is internally inconsistent about whether it speaks display notation or CSS serialization. It also costs two characters of reservation, which is the proximate trigger for D-4's ragged track.
defects.evidence: Measured meter strings (scratchpad/CSD-probe2.mjs -> CSD-out2.json): oklch '359.0deg', lch '359deg', hsl '359deg', hsv '359deg', hwb '359deg' — against '92.0%', '82.7%', '100.0%' in the same column. The promised form is documented at demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/composables/sliderAnnouncement.ts:5 ("Hue 210°"). Visible in frames/D-oklch-ragged-track.png and frames/D-rtl-meter-align.png.
defects.mechanism: a serialization artifact leaking into a display voice because unit rendering has no owner separate from the value pipeline
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/#/?space=oklch&color=oklch(50%25%200.4%20359%20%2F%20100%25) and read the third .channel-meter ('359.0deg').
defects.proposedCure: Unit rendering belongs in the same formatter that owns the least count (readoutReservation.ts), mapping deg -> °, so the display voice and the reservation arithmetic share one source. Fixing this also reclaims 2ch and removes D-4's trigger. Not glass-blocked.

defects.defect: The glass-ui boundary is crossed through 1-line re-export barrels: two import specifiers resolve to one symbol. A dual path (edict 2), and the seam that makes "is this glass-ui or a demo/ui component?" unanswerable at every call site (edict 4). It is also what let the consumer-side slider mechanics accrete — a demo/ui/ shim reads like a place where they may legitimately live.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:95-96 import Card and Slider from "../../../ui/card" and "../../../ui/slider". `cat demo/ui/slider/index.ts` -> `export { Slider } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` (the entire file). demo/ui/card contains only index.ts likewise.
defects.mechanism: an indirection barrel with no transformation — a pure alias, which is the definition of a dual path
defects.reproduction: NONE required — `cat demo/ui/slider/index.ts` is the whole proof.
defects.proposedCure: Import Card/Slider from `@mkbabb/glass-ui` directly and delete the barrels, so the design-system boundary is visible at every call site. Touches four pinned receivers — sequence AFTER the v8 property migration, never folded into it.

defects.defect: Dead payload and duplicated watchers. `componentEntries` builds [key, meta] pairs (including a hand-fabricated alpha meta literal) whose meta half is never read by any consumer; the `as [string, unknown]` cast is the tell — the type says nobody knows what this is, and nobody does. Two separate watchers on the same source do one job.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:120-125 constructs `[meta.key, meta] as [string, unknown]` plus the literal `["alpha", { key: "alpha", min: 0, max: 1, unit: "%" }]`; the only consumers destructure `[component]` at :34 and :51. Duplicated watchers at :138 and :143, both `watch(currentColorSpace, ...)`.
defects.mechanism: a data shape retained past the death of its consumer, preserved by an `unknown` cast that suppresses the type system's ability to notice
defects.reproduction: NONE required — grep the file for `componentEntries` (3 uses, all destructuring only the first tuple slot).
defects.proposedCure: `componentEntries` becomes a `string[]` of channel keys; delete the fabricated alpha meta and the `unknown` cast. Merge :138 and :143 into one watcher.

defects.defect: HYPOTHESIS — the space-change "re-key" does not re-key the element identity map. Vue invokes a function ref with null on unmount; the `if (el)` guard drops that call, so keys are only ever added, never removed. attachSliderListeners then iterates the map on every space change and attaches five listeners per entry including detached elements, and useSliderAnnouncements writes aria-valuetext onto detached thumbs. Predicted: after rgb -> lab -> hsl the map holds {r,g,b,alpha,l,a,h,s} and the detached subtrees are strongly retained for the page's lifetime. This would contradict the chassis-persistence law the file states at :20-24.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:56 (`(el: any) => { if (el) sliderWrapperEls[component] = el as HTMLElement }`); demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/composables/useSliderTouchGates.ts:53 (`for (const [component, el] of Object.entries(sliderWrapperEls.value))`); composables/useSliderAnnouncements.ts:37-44 (same iteration). Stated law at ComponentSliders.vue:20-24.
defects.mechanism: an add-only identity map behind a render that is keyed — the re-key re-mounts the rows but nothing re-keys the map that indexes them
defects.reproduction: NONE — I could not reproduce it in-session. Hash-only navigation does not re-route the picker space: an 11-space `location.hash` sweep (scratchpad/CSD-probe5.mjs) left the labels at R/G/B/ALPHA throughout. Confirming this requires driving the ColorSpaceSelector widget. LABELLED A HYPOTHESIS; not a finding until that probe runs.
defects.proposedCure: Discharge first: drive ColorSpaceSelector across >=3 spaces and assert `Object.keys(sliderWrapperEls.value).length === 4`. If confirmed, the cure is to drop the `if (el)` guard and delete the key on the null call, so the map's lifetime matches the rows'.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — assume the implementation is defective; find the bug (subject: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context variant) — declared at spawn, not inherited
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — on every touch-CAPABLE device (Windows touchscreen laptops, touch Chromebooks, Chrome touch emulation), the FIRST MOUSE click on every channel slider is silently swallowed. useSliderTouchGates.ts:57-68 installs a capture-phase pointerdown that calls e.stopPropagation() unconditionally, gated only on gate.isTouchDevice — a construction-time capability sniff ("ontouchstart" in window, glass-ui useTouchGate-B4mzQcHJ.js:20) — and never reads e.pointerType. Measured in two Playwright contexts differing ONLY by hasTouch, same 1440x900 viewport, same mouse gesture: plain desktop first click drives R 200 -> 36 (firstClickWorked true); touch-capable desktop first click 200 -> 200 (firstClickWorked false), second click 200 -> 36.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded for completeness, three hypotheses I FALSIFIED so no later seat re-files them: (1) coarse-pointer ::before overhang causing wrong-channel taps — FALSIFIED: at 390x844, gapPx 6, strip height 44, ::before blockSize 44px, and elementFromPoint at all three inter-row midpoints and at 2/6/10px above row 0 returned div.channel-rows, never a neighbouring strip; (2) the gate-active outline computing fully transparent (oklab(0 0 0 / 0)) — FALSIFIED as a transition:outline-color t=0 read artifact; the same color-mix inline on a child of the same element computed color(srgb 0.11 0.098 0.09 / 0.5), and the untransitioned .touch-gate-active .slider-track box-shadow read the same 0.5 alpha; (3) the unscoped style block leaving .touch-gate-* undefined on routes that never mount this component — FALSIFIED in dev: on /#/extract (liveTargets 0) a synthetic .touch-gate-target still computed outlineWidth 3px / outlineStyle solid / transition outline-color. Also verified NO PIN DRIFT: shasum -a 256 of the subject file is exactly a61b5ed39703af205d6ba0f4923d32daeaaf55cf9c2e21e22030a01fa82ef327, matching CARRY-LEDGER.md:67.

defects.defect: The channel-slider touch gate swallows the first pointerdown for ALL pointer types on any touch-capable device, because it gates on a device capability sniff instead of the event's own pointerType. The first mouse click on every channel slider does nothing, with no feedback.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/composables/useSliderTouchGates.ts:57-68 — `if (!gate.isTouchDevice) return; if (!gate.isActive.value) { e.stopPropagation(); gate.handleTouchStart(el, e.clientY); }` — e.pointerType is never read. gate.isTouchDevice comes from node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useTouchGate-B4mzQcHJ.js:20 `l = typeof window < "u" && "ontouchstart" in window`. MEASURED (scratchpad/probe8.mjs, two contexts, identical 1440x900 viewport and identical mouse gesture at 15% of the R track): plainDesktop {ontouchstart:false, maxTouchPoints:0} before ["200","80","40","100%"] afterClick1 ["36","80","40","100%"] firstClickWorked:true — touchCapableDesktop {ontouchstart:true, maxTouchPoints:1} before ["200","80","40","100%"] afterClick1 ["200","80","40","100%"] afterClick2 ["36","80","40","100%"] firstClickWorked:false secondClickWorked:true.
defects.mechanism: device-capability sniff used as a per-event modality test; unconditional capture-phase stopPropagation
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe8.mjs against http://localhost:9000 — launch two Chromium contexts at 1440x900, one with hasTouch:false and one with hasTouch:true, navigate to /#/?space=rgb&color=rgb(200%2080%2040), mouse.down()+mouse.up() at 15% of the first .slider-track, read the .channel-meter texts. Without touch the R meter goes 200->36 on click 1; with touch it stays 200 until click 2.
defects.proposedCure: The gate's predicate is per-EVENT, not per-DEVICE. Delete the construction-time isTouchDevice sniff from the consumer entirely and gate on `e.pointerType === "touch"` inside the handler — the exact field Pointer Events provides for this question. That also deletes the second, independent copy of the sniff this component carries (useSliderTouchGates.ts:27-28, consumed as spectrumGateIsTouchDevice at ComponentSliders.vue:203): one predicate, one place. The real transposition is upstream — glass-ui's useTouchGate should take the event, not the device, making this a producer RELAY rather than a demo-side condition.

defects.defect: A `none` component — a first-class CSS Color 4 value this repo's own parser returns — is unguarded end-to-end. In-session it throws from the component's private ramp feed and PERMANENTLY WEDGES the console (meters frozen, all subsequent colour edits and space changes silently ignored, no user-visible error). On a cold load it either replaces the picker pane with an error boundary or blanks the whole app.
defects.evidence: Unguarded readers in the subject file: ComponentSliders.vue:131 `return normalizedChannel(model.value.color, component)` and :180-183 `channelNumber(HSVCurrentColor.value, "s"|"v")`; channelNumber throws on a non-numeric channel at picker-color.ts:152-158. WARM PATH (scratchpad/probe2.mjs) captured stack: `PickerColorError: Missing oklch.h at channelNumber (demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:198:39) at demo/color-session/useSliderGradients.ts:46:18 at Array.map at ComputedRefImpl.fn (useSliderGradients.ts:45:60) at refreshComputed at job at flushPostFlushCbs`. PERMANENT WEDGE (probe3.mjs): pre ["60.0%","0.1","30.0deg","100.0%"] / duringErrs ["Missing oklch.h"] / afterOrdinaryEdit to oklch(80% 0.2 200) STILL ["60.0%","0.1","30.0deg","100.0%"] with afterErrs [] / afterSpaceChange to rgb STILL ["60.0%","0.1","30.0deg","100.0%"]. COLD PATH (probe7.mjs): rgb(255 0 0) control = 4 strips/1 console/1 spectrum; rgb(255 0 0 / none) = 0/0/0, main innerText "This panel hit an unexpected error. color_missing_alpha Try again"; rgb(none 0 0) and oklch(50% 0.1 none) = 0/0/0, `[Vue warn]: Unhandled error during execution of setup function at <App>` + `pageerror: color_missing_channel at valueOrThrow (picker-color.ts:154:8) at convertPickerColor (:162:9) at useColorPipeline (useColorPipeline.ts:57:18) at setup (App.vue:77:20)`, main innerText EMPTY.
defects.mechanism: partial function (channelNumber throws on "none") called from a render/derive path with no total-read alternative
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe3.mjs — load /#/?space=oklch&color=oklch(60%25%200.15%2030), then set location.hash to #/?space=oklch&color=oklch(50%25%200.1%20none): pageerror 'Missing oklch.h' fires and every subsequent hash-driven colour edit and space change is ignored while the meters stay frozen. node scratchpad/probe7.mjs — cold-load /#/?space=rgb&color=rgb(none%200%200) and observe 0 .channel-strip, 0 .sliders-console, 0 .spectrum-picker and an empty main.
defects.proposedCure: `none` is not an error, it is a value with a defined meaning (missing/powerless component). The gestalt cure is a TOTAL read: give channelNumber a sibling returning `number | "none"`, and let each consumer decide its own rendering — the ramp applies the powerless substitution rule, the meter inks an em-dash, the thumb parks at the space's neutral, aria-valuetext says "Hue none". Not a try/catch and not `?? 0`: a total function. The throwing accessor survives only where a number is genuinely required, and the picker's render path stops calling it.

defects.defect: In hex mode all four channel meters render EMPTY and every slider's aria-valuetext loses its value, leaving screen-reader users with only the raw 16-digit aria-valuenow — precisely the failure the U-F27/BR-4 announcement gate exists to prevent. Root cause is a duplicated computed: the component re-derives the row list locally WITHOUT the hex guard the pipeline's own copy has.
defects.evidence: MEASURED on a clean load of /#/?space=hex&color=%23ff8800 (probe3.mjs): hexMeters ["","","",""]; per-thumb (probe.mjs): R channel/valuetext "Red"/valuenow "1"/meter ""; G channel/"Green"/"0.5333333333333333"/""; B channel/"Blue"/"0"/""; ALPHA channel/"Alpha"/"1"/"". Screenshot at scratchpad/hex-console.png shows the blank meter column. MECHANISM: ComponentSliders.vue:120-125 builds componentEntries from PICKER_CHANNELS[currentColorSpace] where resolveColorSpace("hex")==="rgb" (color-model.ts:32-34), so 4 rows render; but the meter source short-circuits in hex to a single {hex:...} cell (useSliderGradients.ts:63-68), so meterText's lookup at ComponentSliders.vue:160 misses r/g/b and its alpha fallback is explicitly disabled for hex at :162 — every row returns "" at :167. The pipeline ALREADY publishes the correct guarded version of this computed at useColorPipeline.ts:117-122 (colorComponents), which the component injects around but does not use.
defects.mechanism: duplicated derivation with divergent guards — two paths to one fact, the live one is the broken one
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe3.mjs — cold-load http://localhost:9000/#/?space=hex&color=%23ff8800, read [...document.querySelectorAll('.channel-meter')].map(m=>m.textContent) => ["","","",""], and read aria-valuetext on the four [role=slider] thumbs => "Red","Green","Blue","Alpha" (no values).
defects.proposedCure: Delete the local componentEntries and consume the pipeline's colorComponents. Hex then renders no channel rows at all — the honest thing, since hex has no channels, it has a string — and the console shows the single hex cell the pipeline already models. The guard divergence is removed by removing the second guard, not by adding a third.

defects.defect: The slider-wrapper element map is never pruned. The template's function ref discards Vue's unmount (null) call and no key is ever deleted, so every channel key with no counterpart in the newly selected space keeps pointing at a DETACHED element forever — and both consumers keep iterating them, re-attaching five listeners each on every space change and writing aria-valuetext into dead nodes on every colour edit.
defects.evidence: ComponentSliders.vue:56 — `:ref="(el: any) => { if (el) sliderWrapperEls[component] = el as HTMLElement }"` (the null branch is discarded; nothing ever deletes a key). Consumers iterate the whole map: useSliderTouchGates.ts:53 (Object.entries -> 5 addEventListener each) and useSliderAnnouncements.ts:37 (querySelector + setAttribute). MEASURED PROOF OF RETENTION (probe2.mjs): hold references to the four lab wrappers, change space to rgb in-session — A_before [{L channel, "Lightness 50.0%", connected true},{A channel,"a axis 20.0",true},{B channel,"b axis 10.0",true},{ALPHA,"Alpha 100.0%",true}] -> A_afterSpaceChange [{L channel, valuetext REWRITTEN to "Lightness", connected FALSE},{A channel, REWRITTEN to "a axis", connected FALSE},{B channel,"b axis 10.0",false},{ALPHA,"Alpha 100.0%",false}]. A setAttribute onto a node with isConnected===false is only possible if the map still holds it. b and alpha were NOT rewritten because rgb re-populates those keys and overwrites the entry — the predicted key-collision behaviour, which confirms rather than contradicts the mechanism. BOUND: the union of channel keys across the 17 spaces in picker-color.ts:52-70 plus alpha is 21 (r,g,b,h,s,l,v,w,c,x,y,z,kelvin,i,ct,cp,jz,az,bz,a,alpha), so up to 20 detached reka-Slider subtrees are retained, each with 5 listener closures capturing el, gate and the whole debug object.
defects.mechanism: DOM mirrored into a hand-managed map with an add-only write path; Vue's unmount signal thrown away
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe2.mjs — on /#/?space=lab&color=lab(50%25%2020%2010) stash [...document.querySelectorAll('.touch-gate-target')] and their thumbs on globalThis, set location.hash to #/?space=rgb&color=rgb(10%2020%2030), wait, then re-read: the L and A entries report isConnected false yet their aria-valuetext has been rewritten by useSliderAnnouncements.apply().
defects.proposedCure: The map is a cache of something Vue already knows. Stop mirroring the DOM: give the v-for row its own small child component that owns its wrapper element and registers/unregisters its own touch gate in onMounted/onUnmounted, so Vue's lifecycle IS the pruning mechanism. (The patch — a delete in the ref's null branch — is strictly inferior; the per-row component also dissolves D-10 and D-11.)

defects.defect: Changing the colour space destroys keyboard focus: the focused slider thumb is unmounted by a container-level :key bump and focus falls to <body>, teleporting a keyboard user to the top of the document.
defects.evidence: MEASURED (probe.mjs): focusAcrossSpaceChange {focusedBefore: "R channel", focusedAfter: "BODY"}. MECHANISM: ComponentSliders.vue:47 `:key="animationKey"` on the .channel-rows container, bumped by the watcher at :143, remounts the entire row block; nothing restores focus. The re-key is also over-broad — alpha exists in every space and is remounted purely because the container above it is keyed, while the per-row `:key="component"` at :52 already re-keys the rows that genuinely change.
defects.mechanism: container-level remount for an animation effect, with no focus restoration
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe.mjs — on /#/?space=rgb&color=rgb(200%2080%2040) focus the first [role=slider], read document.activeElement's aria-label ("R channel"), set location.hash to #/?space=lch&color=lch(60%25%2050%2030), wait 1.8s, re-read document.activeElement => BODY.
defects.proposedCure: The chassis-persistence law the file's own comment states (lines 20-24) is right and the implementation contradicts it. Un-key the container and let the row v-for key do the re-keying, then restore focus onto the row at the same index after the patch. The stagger the container key was really buying is re-fired with an animationKey-driven CSS custom property instead of a remount — the animation is moved, never deleted (edict 6).
