defects.defect: The accessible NAME of every channel slider is the ambiguous raw channel key in shouting caps — "L channel", "A channel", "B channel", "ALPHA channel" — while the correct, space-disambiguated human names exist in a sibling module and are used only for aria-valuetext.
defects.evidence: ComponentSliders.vue:66 — the aria-label is the template literal `${component.toUpperCase()} channel`. Measured names (probe.mjs, and independently in the mega-tranche visual audit REPORT.json a11y rows for route /#/): "L channel", "A channel", "B channel", "ALPHA channel". The sibling docblock at sliderAnnouncement.ts:11-19 argues this exact case against itself — "The channel key alone is ambiguous — `b` is Blue in rgb, Blackness in hwb, and the b* axis in lab/oklab; `l` is Lightness in hsl but the L* axis in lab" — and supplies channelLabel(space, component), which ComponentSliders uses ONLY through useSliderAnnouncements for aria-valuetext, never for the name.
defects.mechanism: two voices for one fact, with the authoritative surface (the accessible name announced on focus and on every arrow key) carrying the wrong one
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe.mjs against /#/?space=lab&color=lab(92%25%2088.8%2020%20%2F%2082.70%25) — read aria-label on each .channel-strip [role=slider]; also visible verbatim in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json under results[route=/#/].probe.a11y.smallTapTargets.
defects.proposedCure: Set the aria-label from channelLabel(currentColorSpace, component) — one function, already written, already unit-tested, already imported into this directory. Drop the " channel" suffix (redundant with role=slider) and the toUpperCase (assistive tech commonly spells all-caps tokens letter by letter, so "ALPHA channel" can be read A-L-P-H-A).

defects.defect: The component's private derived state — the channel ramp gradients — lives in the shared color-session pipeline god-object rather than in the component, so its throw is not contained to the console and instead wedges the entire picker (the blast radius of D-2's warm path).
defects.evidence: Complete consumer sets by grep over demo/ excluding useSliderGradients.ts and useColorPipeline.ts: `componentsSlidersStyle` has EXACTLY ONE consumer — ComponentSliders.vue:111,194. `currentColorRanges` has EXACTLY ONE — its colocated ConsoleRail.vue:75,114. `currentColorComponentsFormatted` has two (ColorPicker.vue:49,205 and ComponentSliders.vue:110,160,234), and its hex branch exists only to serve a display component (the mechanism of D-3). The throw in D-2's warm path is at useSliderGradients.ts:46 inside a ComputedRefImpl.fn — i.e. inside the pipeline's reactive graph, which is why one bad channel freezes the whole picker rather than one component.
defects.mechanism: component-private cache hoisted into an injected god-object, coupling its failure modes to the whole session
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "componentsSlidersStyle|currentColorComponentsFormatted|currentColorRanges" demo/ --include='*.vue' --include='*.ts' | grep -v "useSliderGradients.ts|useColorPipeline.ts" — 9 hits, of which componentsSlidersStyle appears only under ComponentSliders/ and currentColorRanges only under ConsoleRail.vue.
defects.proposedCure: Move computeSliderGradients and currentColorRanges into ComponentSliders/composables/useChannelRamps.ts, deriving from the injected model. The pipeline keeps currentColorComponentsFormatted (two genuine consumers). The blast radius of a ramp bug then ends at the console — which is the point of encapsulation, and would have turned D-2's warm path from an app-wide freeze into one component rendering a fallback.

defects.defect: The coarse-pointer touch-target extension is media-gated on `pointer: coarse` — the PRIMARY input mechanism — rather than `any-pointer: coarse`, so hybrid devices (fine primary + touchscreen) get no 44px hit extension while the JS gate is armed against them.
defects.evidence: ComponentSliders.vue:345 `@media (pointer: coarse)`. Media Queries Level 4 defines `pointer` as reporting the pointing device "that is the primary input mechanism" and `any-pointer` as reporting any available input mechanism. The file's own comment at :342-344 sells the choice as a virtue — "Gated on `pointer: coarse` (the input device), never viewport width" — but the device is not what `pointer` reports; the primary device is. Measured presence of the pseudo (probe.mjs): desktop beforeH "auto"/content "none"; 390x844 coarse beforeH "44px"/content '""'.
defects.mechanism: wrong media feature for the question being asked (capability vs primacy) — the CSS gate and the JS gate disagree about which devices are touchable
defects.reproduction: NONE for the hybrid case — labelled HYPOTHESIS. Chromium's touch emulation couples the two features (probe.mjs/probe8.mjs measured pointerCoarse:true AND anyPointerCoarse:true under hasTouch:true), so the divergence could not be isolated in this harness. The spec reading is not a hypothesis; only the device-class consequence is.
defects.proposedCure: Use `@media (any-pointer: coarse)` — one word, and the CSS gate then agrees with the JS gate about which devices are touchable. Under D-1's cure both predicates become per-event and this collapses into a non-question.

defects.defect: The channel thumbs are 12 CSS px wide (12x24 desktop, 12x44 coarse), and this component supplies exactly half of route /#/'s small-tap-target count in every one of the four Safari audit matrices.
defects.evidence: MEASURED (probe.mjs): thumbW 12 / thumbH 24 at 1440x900; thumbW 12 / thumbH 44 at 390x844. INDEPENDENTLY in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json, route /#/, matrix safari-mobile-light: {"w":12,"h":44,"tag":"span","label":"L channel"},{..."A channel"},{..."B channel"},{..."ALPHA channel"}; safari-desktop-light reports the same four at 12x24. REPORT.md counts 8 smallTapTargets on /#/ in each of the four matrices — four of the eight are this component's thumbs in all four, i.e. 16 of the 60-capture tally. HONEST SCOPING: WCAG 2.5.8's spacing exception IS met — measured row pitch 43.5px (stripTop 604.33 -> 647.83), well clear of the 24px undisturbed circle, and the track itself is click-operable. So this is an ergonomics finding, not a certain SC failure.
defects.mechanism: producer primitive's thumb geometry too small for a precision instrument; the coarse-pointer cure extends height only, never width
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe.mjs — read getBoundingClientRect() on each .channel-strip [role=slider] at 1440x900 (12x24) and at 390x844 with hasTouch (12x44). Cross-check the same four rows in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json at results[route=/#/].probe.a11y.smallTapTargets.
defects.proposedCure: The thumb width is the glass-ui Slider primitive's, not the demo's — the cure is a producer RELAY, not a consumer override (edict 5 forbids per-instance overrides of the design system). Book a >=24px hit box into the same v8 packet as the track-background rename, alongside the aria-valuetext prop-through relay.

defects.defect: ConsoleRail is handed a freshly allocated array on every parent render, so it patches on every reactive tick of a drag despite a channel list that is constant within a space; and the array it is built from carries a dead payload cast to `unknown`.
defects.evidence: ComponentSliders.vue:34 `:components="componentEntries.map(([c]) => c)"` — new array identity every render pass. ConsoleRail is not cheap to patch: it recomputes restInk through a live surface probe (ConsoleRail.vue:130-140, resolveSurfaceLightnessLive) and activeInk through contrastInkFor (:147-149). The source computed's second tuple member is built and cast to unknown at ComponentSliders.vue:122-124 and never read — the only destructure is `v-for="[component] in componentEntries"` at :51, so the `as [string, unknown]` casts erase ChannelMeta for a value nothing consumes.
defects.mechanism: unstable prop identity from an inline .map() in the template plus a dead payload retained through a widening cast
defects.reproduction: NONE measured (static read of ComponentSliders.vue:34,51,120-125 and ConsoleRail.vue:103-111,130-149) — labelled HYPOTHESIS as to the patch cost; the identity instability and the dead payload are certain from the source.
defects.proposedCure: Make componentEntries a computed<string[]> of keys only — which is what both consumers actually want — so the identity is stable across renders and the cast disappears with the dead payload. Under D-3's cure it becomes the pipeline's colorComponents and this dissolves entirely.

defects.defect: sliderValue(), meterText() and sliderVars() are plain functions invoked from the template, so they re-run for every row on every render pass; sliderVars rebuilds an 11-stop gradient string per channel per pass even though the stops are already memoised upstream.
defects.evidence: ComponentSliders.vue:127 (sliderValue), :158 (meterText), :193-207 (sliderVars, whose body joins the stop list into a linear-gradient string on every call). The stops themselves are already memoised by the watcher at useSliderGradients.ts:49-61 — only the join is repeated, and only because the joined form was never memoised. Four joins x eleven stops per drag tick.
defects.mechanism: work that is a function of the colour space recomputed as a function of the frame
defects.reproduction: NONE measured — labelled HYPOTHESIS as to the magnitude; the per-render invocation is certain from the template (function calls in the render expressions at :72, :73, :85).
defects.proposedCure: One computed map component -> styleObject, rebuilt when the ramps or the thumb ink change. Under D-4's per-row-component cure each row owns its own computed and this is free.

defects.defect: Two separate watchers subscribe to the same source (currentColorSpace) to perform two assignments — two subscriptions and two scheduler entries for one event.
defects.evidence: ComponentSliders.vue:138 `watch(currentColorSpace, () => { activeComponent.value = null; });` and ComponentSliders.vue:143 `watch(currentColorSpace, () => { animationKey.value++; });`
defects.mechanism: KISS violation — one event, two subscriptions
defects.reproduction: NONE needed — static, both lines are five apart in the same file.
defects.proposedCure: Collapse to one watcher with one callback performing both assignments.

defects.defect: `aria-live="off"` on the meter span is a no-op: `off` is already the computed default for any element not inside a live region, so the attribute asserts nothing and suppresses nothing.
defects.evidence: ComponentSliders.vue:84 — `<span class="channel-meter fira-code" aria-live="off">`.
defects.mechanism: dead code in the accessibility surface, reading as a deliberate suppression the platform never required
defects.reproduction: NONE needed — static.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the attribute. If the intent was to document that the meter deliberately does not announce (because aria-valuetext carries that job), say so in a comment, not in a no-op attribute.

defects.defect: The SFC's <style> block is unscoped and is the SOLE definition site of .touch-gate-target / .touch-gate-active, which SpectrumCanvas and ExtractControls also consume — plus it exports five component-private class names into the global cascade.
defects.evidence: ComponentSliders.vue:238 opens `<style>` with no `scoped`; the comment at :244-252 justifies it for .touch-gate-*. Global leakage also covers .sliders-console (:283), .channel-meter (:309), .channel-rows (:328), .channel-strip (:331), .channel-slider (:346,:363,:375). ExtractControls.vue:135-142 re-declares .touch-gate-target SCOPED with only a border-radius — the activation outline rules exist nowhere but here. FALSIFIED AS A LIVE DEFECT (probe4.mjs): on /#/extract, which has liveTargets 0, a synthetic .touch-gate-target still computed outlineWidth "3px", outlineStyle "solid", transition "outline-color" — the dev server injects every SFC's styles.
defects.mechanism: cross-component style dependency with an implicit load-order contract
defects.reproduction: NONE for the production case — labelled HYPOTHESIS with a named test: build the gh-pages target and re-run probe4.mjs against the emitted chunks to see whether the .touch-gate-* rules survive route code-splitting on /#/extract. In dev the coupling is benign.
defects.proposedCure: Move the shared .touch-gate-* base rules to demo/styles/ where shared cascade belongs, scope the rest of the block to this SFC, and leave only the deliberately-unscoped reka-internal selectors (which the v8 hold is separately retiring).

defects.defect: The component's gates are vacuous: nothing mounts ComponentSliders.vue and nothing exercises useSliderTouchGates.ts or useSliderAnnouncements.ts, so D-1 and D-4 have zero coverage by construction, and three named mutations that would destroy the component's stated contracts keep both suites green.
defects.evidence: Complete test surface (grep -rln over test/ and e2e/ for channel-meter|channel-slider|sliders-console|ComponentSliders|useSliderTouchGates|useSliderAnnouncements): exactly two files — test/slider-announcement.test.ts and e2e/smoke/a11y-slider-operation.spec.ts. The unit suite imports only the two pure functions from sliderAnnouncement.ts. Run: `npx vitest run test/slider-announcement.test.ts` => ' ✓ test/slider-announcement.test.ts (7 tests) 2ms / Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 7 passed (7)'. The e2e (e2e/smoke/a11y-slider-operation.spec.ts) asserts only that aria-valuenow moves under Home/End/ArrowLeft — it never reads aria-valuetext, never visits hex, never reads a meter, never changes space.
defects.mechanism: gates test the pure formatter and the producer primitive, never the wiring that connects them to the component
defects.reproduction: MUTATION A: delete the entire useSliderAnnouncements({...}) call at ComponentSliders.vue:230-235 — no thumb ever receives an aria-valuetext and the whole U-F27/BR-4 contract is unimplemented; all 7 unit tests still pass (they never touch a DOM node). MUTATION B: make meterText() at ComponentSliders.vue:158 return the empty string unconditionally — every meter in all 18 spaces renders blank and every announcement degrades to the bare channel name (D-3 generalised); the e2e still passes because the sliders still move. MUTATION C: delete the pointercancel/lostpointercapture handlers at useSliderTouchGates.ts:76-86 and their registrations at :91-92 — the entire iOS Safari pointer-capture leak recovery this file exists to carry is gone; both suites pass.
defects.proposedCure: Three born-RED gates, each of which fails today: (1) a component test that mounts the console in hex and asserts every row's meter is non-empty (fails — D-3); (2) a Playwright case in a hasTouch:true DESKTOP context asserting the FIRST mouse click moves the value (fails — D-1; scratchpad/probe8.mjs is the ready-made harness); (3) a component test that switches space and asserts Object.keys(sliderWrapperEls.value) equals exactly the new space's channel set (fails — D-4).

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m]) — matches the explicit declaration this seat was spawned with; not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: L-1: a complete second implementation of this component lives at demo/palettes/browser/search/MiniColorPicker.vue, and its hand-rolled HSV→hex math disagrees with the published @mkbabb/value.js on 295/10,830 sampled colors (2.72%) because it uses Math.round where src/color/operations.ts:324 uses the CSS-spec roundHalfEven. The demo exists to be the dogfood proof of the library; one of its two spectrum pickers bypasses the library entirely and returns different colors.
result.negativeProof: Partial negatives proved, not asserted: (1) No deep-path import — `grep -rhn 'from "@mkbabb/value.js[^"]*"' demo/` returns 49 imports across exactly 5 specifiers (/color 24, /css 10, /math 6, /easing 5, /quantize 4), every one a real key in package.json#exports; zero @src/*, zero ../../src/, zero dist/ reach-through. Live dev probe confirms only /dist/subpaths/{color,css,math}.js served for the picker route. (2) verbatimModuleSyntax clean — all 8 SpectrumCanvas.vue:36-43 imports are value imports; useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:8,10 use inline `type`, :12 uses `import type`. (3) Vue 3.5 idiomatic — useTemplateRef at :56; injected App-owned ShallowRef via COLOR_MODEL_KEY removes the defineModel stale-read hazard by construction. (4) rAF is NOT ungated — scheduleSpectrumUpdate (:97-108) is a one-shot null-guarded coalescer, cancelled in stopDragging (:195-198) and onUnmounted (:217-224). (5) Animations moved not deleted — field-paint-in is scoped + PRM-gated (edict 6 permits), live-confirmed running as "field-paint-in-ad23e00d". (6) a11y mechanism correct — role="img" + reactive aria-label (right for a 2D field, not role="slider"); the visual audit's smallTapTargets rows for /#/ (8 desktop, 8 mobile) name slug buttons and channel spans, never the spectrum plate; 0 page errors, 0 horizontal overflow, 0 blank captures across all 4 Safari matrices.

defects.defect: A complete second implementation of SpectrumCanvas lives at demo/palettes/browser/search/MiniColorPicker.vue — same plate gradient, same pointer→(s,v) maths, same dot placement — and it hand-rolls HSV→RGB→hex (36 lines) instead of using the library, producing measurably different colors.
defects.evidence: Plate: useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:37-38 vs MiniColorPicker.vue:160-162 (identical two-gradient formula). Pointer maths: SpectrumCanvas.vue:117-121 (value.js clamp) vs MiniColorPicker.vue:138-139 (inline Math.max/min). Dot: useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:60-61 vs MiniColorPicker.vue:19. Hand-rolled math: MiniColorPicker.vue:85-105 (HSV→hex), :110-125 (hex→HSV). MEASURED — `node scratchpad/dup.mjs` → `samples=10830 disagreements=295 (2.72%)`, e.g. h=14 s=1 v=1 → mini '#ff3c00' vs lib '#ff3b00'; h=8 s=.5 v=1 → mini '#ff9180' vs lib '#ff9080'. Live: imported at SearchFilterBar.vue:132, rendered :66.
defects.mechanism: Duplicate ownership of a concept the library owns. src/color/operations.ts:324 quantizes with roundHalfEven (CSS Color 4 spec); MiniColorPicker.vue:103 uses Math.round (half-up). The clone did not merely repeat the library, it repeated the one spec decision the library exists to own, and got it wrong.
defects.reproduction: node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/dup.mjs — runs MiniColorPicker.vue:85-105 verbatim against hsv()+toRgba8({gamut:'clip'}) from dist/subpaths/color.js over a 361×6×5 grid.
defects.proposedCure: Delete MiniColorPicker's plate and color math; both 2D fields consume one glass-ui `useField2dPointer` primitive and one demo `plate.ts`. Interim: currentHex := pickerColorToHex(hsv(hue,sat,val,1)); the hex watcher := convertPickerColor(parsePickerColor(hex),'hsv') — 36 lines to 2, divergence zero by construction.

defects.defect: demo/color-session/picker-color.ts re-declares the library's internal SPACE_SCHEMA verbatim and hand-writes a 17-arm switch reimplementing the library's already-existing generic makeColor(). SpectrumCanvas.vue:127 (withChannel) sits directly on this duplicate.
defects.evidence: Library: src/color/model.ts:56-74 (SPACE_SCHEMA: channels/hueIndex/css per space) and :136-142 (makeColor). Demo clone: picker-color.ts:52-70 (PICKER_CHANNELS), :92-95 (CSS_PICKER_SPACES), :123-144 (buildColor, 22-line 17-arm switch). MEASURED — `node scratchpad/tbl.mjs` → `spaces compared: 17 / channel-name lists IDENTICAL: 17/17 (49 channel names duplicated verbatim) / css-serializable flag match: 17/17 / hue-channel position match: 17/17 / mismatches: []`. Neither src/color/index.ts (41 lines, read whole) nor src/subpaths/color.ts exports SPACE_SCHEMA, SPACE_IDS, makeColor, or isAnyColor.
defects.mechanism: The public export map withholds the generic surface the library already implements. Publishing only 17 named per-space factories and no generic constructor or schema forces every consumer that addresses a channel by name — or builds a color from a runtime-chosen space — to re-derive the whole table and hand-write the dispatch. The duplication is a property of the API's shape, not of the demo author.
defects.reproduction: node /private/tmp/claude-504/-Users-mkbabb-Programming-value-js/6614e90c-8bd6-434f-b017-5ad4277c6e5e/scratchpad/tbl.mjs — parses both tables out of src/color/model.ts and demo/color-session/picker-color.ts and diffs them.
defects.proposedCure: Publish the generic surface on @mkbabb/value.js/color: SPACE_SCHEMA, SPACE_IDS, makeColor, isAnyColor, plus a new src/color/channels.ts (~40 lines lifted verbatim from picker-color.ts) exporting channelRange/channelNumber/normalizedChannel/withChannel/withNormalizedChannel/withAlpha. Channel addressing over AnyColor has zero picker semantics — it belongs beside convertColor and mixColors. picker-color.ts then shrinks from 220 lines to ~35 (display strings only) and SpectrumCanvas.vue imports withChannel from the published subpath.

defects.defect: SpectrumCanvas's root-element styling is owned by a SIBLING component's unscoped <style> block: it applies .touch-gate-target / .touch-gate-active, both declared in ComponentSliders.vue. A third, conflicting declaration exists in ExtractControls.vue.
defects.evidence: Applied at SpectrumCanvas.vue:11-12. Declared at ComponentSliders.vue:253-274 (unscoped by design — its own comment at :244-246 names SpectrumCanvas as a consumer). Third site: ExtractControls.vue:140. LIVE probe against localhost:9000 — matched rules on .spectrum-picker include `{sel: '.touch-gate-target', css: 'outline: transparent solid 3px; outline-offset: 1px; transition: outline-color …'}` with computed outlineWidth '3px', outlineStyle 'solid'. foundation.css:577 records the inversion explicitly: '.touch-gate-* cluster colocated into ComponentSliders.vue's unscoped <style>'.
defects.mechanism: Wrong direction of dependency plus wrong altitude. A shared class vocabulary was pushed DOWN into a leaf SFC instead of UP into the shared stylesheet or the design system that owns the state machine. The edge is undeclared: if ComponentSliders is lazy-loaded, reordered or removed, SpectrumCanvas's touch-activation affordance vanishes with no type error, no test failure, no lint.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe.mjs — enumerates document.styleSheets rules matching .spectrum-picker and reads computed outline; the only source of the matched .touch-gate-target rule is ComponentSliders.vue's unscoped block.
defects.proposedCure: glass-ui owns useTouchGate and therefore owns the class contract. Move the .touch-gate-* rules into glass-ui's stylesheet and have useTouchGate() return the class binding (gate.classes.value) so no consumer ever spells the name. Three declaration sites collapse to zero at the consumer.

defects.defect: The component is named SpectrumCanvas and contains zero <canvas>. The name, an orphan <figure>, three dead --gamut-* tokens, and a docstring naming a deleted module are all unmaintained residue of a canvas overlay removed at a68ecdc1.
defects.evidence: LIVE: `canvasInsideSpectrum: 0` (the page's 2 canvases are goo-blob + aurora). `git show --stat a68ecdc1` deleted useGamutOverlay.ts (309 L), gamutOverlayPaint.ts (217 L), useGamutDetent.ts (115 L), SpectrumPlateCaption.vue (81 L), SpectrumDetentLabel.vue (57 L) and stripped 137 lines from the SFC; `git show a68ecdc1^:…/SpectrumCanvas.vue` shows three <canvas> elements and a caption. Residue: (a) the name + directory; (b) SpectrumCanvas.vue:3 <figure> with no figcaption; (c) spectrumLuma.ts:5-7 still cites 'useGamutOverlay' as a consumer — deleted; (d) `for t in --gamut-edge --gamut-hatch --gamut-edge-paper --gamut-hatch-paper; do grep -rn "var($t" demo/; done` → only --gamut-edge has a consumer, and it is REPURPOSED (ComponentSliders.vue:392, a slider thumb border); foundation.css:279 still reads 'The overlay canvas resolves all four'.
defects.mechanism: Nomenclature that outlived its referent — a fifth species of the legacy the owner edicts forbid, and worse than a shim: it costs on every read and nothing ever fails. It misled the audit brief for this very seat ('Canvas-based spectrum rendering… devicePixelRatio handling').
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe.mjs (canvasInsideSpectrum: 0) + `git show --stat a68ecdc1 | grep -i gamut` + the four-token grep above.
defects.proposedCure: Rename to ColorField/ + ColorField.vue — it is a 2D color field; 'canvas' was never the concept, only once the technique. <figure> → <div>. Delete --gamut-hatch, --gamut-edge-paper, --gamut-hatch-paper; rename --gamut-edge to what it now means. Fix spectrumLuma.ts's header to name its two real consumers.

defects.defect: tsconfig.demo.json#paths advertises a value.js public surface that does not exist — 3 specifiers map to nonexistent .d.ts files while 2 real published subpaths are absent. A green typecheck certifies imports that cannot ship.
defects.evidence: `node -e '…compare…'` → PUBLISHED exports: /color /css /easing /math /quantize /transform /value (7 keys, NO root '.'). tsconfig.demo paths: @mkbabb/value.js, /color, /easing, /math, /parsing, /quantize, /transform, /units. IN tsconfig NOT published: `@mkbabb/value.js @mkbabb/value.js/parsing @mkbabb/value.js/units`. PUBLISHED missing from tsconfig: `@mkbabb/value.js/value @mkbabb/value.js/css`. Targets absent: `ls dist/index.d.ts dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts dist/subpaths/units.d.ts` → all three 'No such file or directory'. tsconfig.demo.json:3-7 asserts it mirrors the published exports and :41 asserts 'the exports map is a CLOSED 8-key set' — it is a closed 7-key set and a different 7.
defects.mechanism: Two mirrors of one source of truth, one generated and one hand-maintained. vite.config.ts:28-29 generates its alias set FROM package.json#exports with the comment 'GENERATED (not hand-rolled) so the alias set can never drift from the exports map'. The tsconfig kept a hand-rolled copy and drifted five ways — the exact failure the vite comment was written to prevent, one file over. An import of `@mkbabb/value.js` bare would typecheck green against a nonexistent .d.ts and fail at runtime, because the vite alias set is generated from exports and would not alias it.
defects.reproduction: node -e "pkg=require('./package.json').exports; ts=JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('tsconfig.demo.json','utf8').replace(/^\\s*\\/\\/.*$/gm,'')).compilerOptions.paths; …set-diff…" plus `ls dist/index.d.ts dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts dist/subpaths/units.d.ts`.
defects.proposedCure: DELETE all eight @mkbabb/value.js* entries from tsconfig.demo.json#paths rather than fixing them. Proved safe and sufficient: @mkbabb/value.js/css has 10 live demo imports and NO paths entry, and `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` exits 0 — TypeScript self-name resolution already resolves bare specifiers through this package's own exports map. package.json#exports then becomes the single source of truth for both vite (already generated from it) and tsc, and the drift becomes structurally impossible.

defects.defect: Ownership cycle: usePointerDebug — a parent-level composable this component injects — hardcodes '.spectrum-picker', a class private to SpectrumCanvas.vue's scoped <style>.
defects.evidence: Down-edge: SpectrumCanvas.vue:41,52 inject POINTER_DEBUG_KEY from ../../composables/usePointerDebug. Up-edge: usePointerDebug.ts:117-122 — `document.querySelectorAll('.spectrum-picker, .slider-track, …')` and `document.querySelectorAll('.touch-gate-target, .spectrum-picker')`. The class is declared inside SpectrumCanvas.vue:230's `<style scoped>`. LIVE probe confirms the literal class survives scoping: classList contains 'spectrum-picker'.
defects.mechanism: The dependency graph has a cycle — SpectrumCanvas → usePointerDebug → SpectrumCanvas — and the up-edge works only by accident of Vue's scoping (which adds a data-v-* attribute without mangling the class name). Rename the class or restructure the element and forceReleaseAllPointers() silently stops covering the spectrum: the exact iOS pointer-capture leak recovery that composable exists for. No type error, no test, no lint — discovered only by an iOS user whose picker freezes.
defects.reproduction: grep -n 'spectrum-picker' demo/picker/composables/usePointerDebug.ts (two hits, :118 and :121) against SpectrumCanvas.vue:227-230 (`<style scoped>` … `.spectrum-picker {`).
defects.proposedCure: Invert the edge. usePointerDebug exposes registerSurface(el: HTMLElement); each component that owns a capture surface registers its own element (`onMounted(() => debug.registerSurface(spectrumRef.value!))`). The selector list is deleted, the composable knows nothing about any component, the dependency points one way.

defects.defect: useTouchGate is imported from the glass-ui ROOT BARREL one line after WatercolorDot is imported correctly from a subpath — and glass-ui publishes useTouchGate at ./dom, which the sibling ColorPicker.vue already uses.
defects.evidence: SpectrumCanvas.vue:38 `from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/watercolor-dot"` (correct) vs :39 `from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"` (barrel). Subpath exists: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/dom/index.d.ts:2 re-exports ./useTouchGate; package.json#exports['./dom'] → ./dist/dom.js (4,179 bytes). Barrel statically imports 43 internal chunks — `node -e '…extract import specifiers from dist/glass-ui.js…'` → 46 specifiers incl. ./data-table, ./dialog, ./command, ./select, ./toast, ./configurator. Correct edge proven in-tree: ColorPicker.vue:124 uses @mkbabb/glass-ui/dom; HeroBlob.vue:34-39 uses /blob /color /dom /dark. Wrong in exactly 3 places, all for the same symbol: SpectrumCanvas.vue:39, useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:12, useSliderTouchGates.ts:15.
defects.mechanism: Inconsistent import granularity for the same design system in the same file, two lines apart. Not a proven prod-bundle cost — glass-ui declares sideEffects:['*.css'] so the JS is tree-shakeable, and ColorPicker.vue:138 pulls the barrel anyway for writeClipboard — so I do not claim bytes. The defect is the edge: three imports of one symbol taking a path the codebase has already decided against.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"' demo/picker/ (3 hits) vs grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/' demo/picker/ (11 hits, incl. ColorPicker.vue:124 useIdleReady from /dom).
defects.proposedCure: `import { useTouchGate } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dom";` in all three sites, then an ESLint no-restricted-imports rule banning bare '@mkbabb/glass-ui' in demo/ — enforceable the moment L-8 lands.

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is 19 files of one-line re-export shims over the glass-ui root barrel with zero local components — a pure alias layer, and every shim forces the root-barrel edge on its consumers.
defects.evidence: `find demo/ui -type f | wc -l` → 19; `find demo/ui -type f ! -name index.ts` → none. Contents: demo/ui/popover/index.ts = `export { Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverContent } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` — one line. Same for button, slider, card, badge, avatar, checkbox, collapsible, dialog, dropdown-menu, input, label, radio-group, select, separator, skeleton, switch, tooltip; alert is 11 lines / 2 re-exports. Counter-proof in the subject: SpectrumCanvas.vue:38 imports WatercolorDot straight from @mkbabb/glass-ui/watercolor-dot with no shim. MiniColorPicker.vue:62-63 goes through ../../../ui/popover and ../../../ui/button.
defects.mechanism: Alias / dual path (owner edict 2) plus a demo-side design-system layer (owner edict 4). Two routes to the same components, one of them empty; and because all 19 shims import the root barrel, they propagate L-7 to every consumer.
defects.reproduction: for f in demo/ui/*/index.ts; do echo "$f lines=$(grep -c . $f)"; done — 18 of 19 report lines=1, all with a single @mkbabb/glass-ui reference.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entirely; rewrite each consumer to the glass-ui subpath (the subject component already demonstrates the pattern). 19 files removed, one dual path closed, and the L-7 lint becomes enforceable.

defects.defect: Two writers own touch-action on the same element: glass-ui's useTouchGate writes el.style.touchAction imperatively while useSpectrumPlateStyle writes the same inline property declaratively — and the component ALSO expresses the same boolean as CSS classes.
defects.evidence: glass-ui imperative writes, decompiled from dist/useTouchGate-B4mzQcHJ.js: `function y(e){ o.value=!0, e.style.touchAction='none', v(); }` (activate) and `function x(){ …, u &&= (u.style.touchAction='', null); }` (deactivate). Vue declarative write: useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:41-44. Same element — SpectrumCanvas.vue:135 passes event.currentTarget, which is the :style-bound div. LIVE: inline style attribute reads `background: …; --spectrum-shadow: lab(92% 88.8 20); touch-action: none;`. Third mechanism for the same state: classes at SpectrumCanvas.vue:11-12.
defects.mechanism: Shared ownership of one DOM property with no protocol. Vue's style patcher diffs against its own previous value and is blind to glass-ui's writes; glass-ui is blind to Vue's. On my trace they converge (glass-ui writes synchronously, Vue restores on the next tick) — I could NOT produce a permanent divergence and explicitly label that a hypothesis. The confirmed defect is the dual ownership itself, converging by luck of ordering.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe.mjs reads the inline style attribute and computed touchAction on .spectrum-picker; the two writer sites are useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:41-44 and the decompiled y()/x() in dist/useTouchGate-B4mzQcHJ.js.
defects.proposedCure: glass-ui owns the gate, so glass-ui owns touch-action. Give useTouchGate the inactive value it currently lacks — useTouchGate({ inactiveTouchAction: 'pan-y' }) — and delete touchAction from the style computed. One writer.

defects.defect: Two idioms for 'write a CSS color' inside one feature: the spectrum plate hand-writes an hsl() string template while its sibling composable builds every gradient stop through the library's serializer.
defects.evidence: Hand-written: useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:38 `linear-gradient(to right, #fff, hsl(${hue}deg, 100%, 50%))`. Library route, same feature: demo/color-session/useSliderGradients.ts:37 `const cssStr = serializePickerColor(step);` and :44, which resolve to value.js serializeCssColor via picker-color.ts:206-211. Third hand-written site: MiniColorPicker.vue:34.
defects.mechanism: @mkbabb/value.js/css publishes serializeCssColor and exists to own CSS color syntax. One composable in the picker dogfoods it; the other hand-writes the string. Trivial alone; as a pattern it is the same disease as L-1 and L-2 — the demo not consuming the library it exists to prove.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'hsl(\${' demo/ → 2 hits (useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:38, MiniColorPicker.vue:34); grep -n 'serializePickerColor' demo/color-session/useSliderGradients.ts → :5, :37, :44.
defects.proposedCure: Build the plate's hue endpoint through serializeCssColor (via serializePickerColor(hsl(hue,1,0.5))) so there is one idiom for CSS color emission across the feature — and one place to change when the plate moves to a wide-gamut hue ramp.

defects.defect: isTouchDevice is copied verbatim from glass-ui's internals under a comment claiming reuse, when useTouchGate already returns it on every gate the same file constructs.
defects.evidence: useSliderTouchGates.ts:25-27: `// Touch gate check — reuse the same detection as spectrum` / `const isTouchDevice = typeof window !== "undefined" && "ontouchstart" in window;`. glass-ui's own line, decompiled from dist/useTouchGate-B4mzQcHJ.js: `l = typeof window < "u" && "ontouchstart" in window` — and it is returned as `isTouchDevice` (dist/composables/dom/useTouchGate.d.ts, TouchGateReturn). The same file constructs gates at :37 whose .isTouchDevice it ignores. SpectrumCanvas.vue:138 does it right (spectrumGate.isTouchDevice).
defects.mechanism: Documented-as-shared, actually-duplicated predicate. The comment asserts reuse; the code is a copy of a design-system internal. Two sources of truth for one capability check, and if glass-ui ever refines the detection (pointer: coarse, maxTouchPoints) the demo copy silently disagrees.
defects.reproduction: grep -n 'ontouchstart' demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/composables/useSliderTouchGates.ts node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useTouchGate-B4mzQcHJ.js — the same expression in both.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the local const; read isTouchDevice off any constructed gate, as SpectrumCanvas already does.

defects.defect: The two sibling controls in demo/picker/controls/ decomposed the SAME three concerns at mirror-image seams — ComponentSliders lifted its gesture cluster and kept presentation inline; SpectrumCanvas lifted its presentation and kept ~95 lines of gesture inline. Neither concern has one home, and the plate's pure functions have zero unit coverage.
defects.evidence: ComponentSliders: gesture → composables/useSliderTouchGates.ts (133 L, takes debug as a param — testable); presentation inline. SpectrumCanvas: presentation → composables/useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts; gesture inline at SpectrumCanvas.vue:77-200 (~95 L: capture bookkeeping, rAF coalescer, gate wiring, debug). BOTH lift headers give the same reason — 'keeping the SFC under the 400-LoC cap' (useSliderTouchGates.ts:2-4, useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:2-4). Coverage: `grep -rln 'spectrumLuma|useSpectrumPlateStyle' test/ demo/test/` → nothing; only e2e specs touch the spectrum. Hard-asserted injections with no fallback at SpectrumCanvas.vue:50,52 (`inject(...)!`) vs the defensive form at ColorSpaceSelector.vue:142 (`inject(COLOR_MODEL_KEY, null)`).
defects.mechanism: The seam was chosen by line count, not by concept — which is why the same three concerns landed on opposite sides of it in two sibling directories. Consequence: spectrumLuma() (a two-line pure function) and useSpectrumPlateStyle (a pure computed factory) are trivially unit-testable but are exercised only by full-browser e2e, and the gesture cluster cannot be mounted at all outside ColorPicker.
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS (not reproduced): mounting SpectrumCanvas without providers throws `TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'model' of 'undefined'` at SpectrumCanvas.vue:45-50. I could not construct the repro without writing under test/, which this seat may not do. The decomposition asymmetry and the zero-coverage grep are confirmed.
defects.proposedCure: Split by concept, not by LoC. Gesture → glass-ui useField2dPointer (generic, shared by both spectrum pickers). Presentation → one demo plate.ts merging today's spectrumLuma.ts + useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts (they are one concept: the HSV plate's geometry and ink), as Vue-free pure functions that unit-test without a browser.

defects.defect: The accessible name announces HSV *value* as 'lightness', and the plate models a fixed sRGB/HSV field regardless of the color space the user selected.
defects.evidence: useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:27: `Color spectrum, saturation ${sPct}%, lightness ${vPct}%` — dotPos.v is HSV value, not lightness. LIVE accessible name in the captured state: `"ariaLabel": "Color spectrum, saturation 63%, lightness 100%"`. The captured route state (visual/REPORT.json, /#/) is space=lab with Lab sliders, while the plate paints hsl(H,100%,50%) + a black overlay and round-trips every drag through withChannel(HSV,…) → setCurrentColor(hsv, selectedColorSpace) at SpectrumCanvas.vue:127-129.
defects.mechanism: Same class as L-4 — a module labelled for something other than what it owns. At v=1 the plate's top row runs white→saturated-hue; announcing that as 'lightness 100%' tells a screen-reader user the color is white, which it is not. Underneath, the component is an HSV instrument named and presented as *the* spectrum for a 17-space picker.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/probe.mjs reads el.getAttribute('aria-label') live → 'Color spectrum, saturation 63%, lightness 100%' while the page title is 'lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%) — Color Picker'.
defects.proposedCure: Say 'value' in the label, and name the component for the field it actually is (ColorField, per L-4). If the plate should follow the selected space, that is a design decision to route through the D-axis seat — this seat records only that the label and the model disagree with the picker's own space.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) under demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m]) — the declared spawn tier; seat is not inherited or undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — ColorPicker's `defineAsyncComponent` split of HeroBlob is defeated: `demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphere.ts:36` imports two constants from the 103,031-byte `@mkbabb/glass-ui/blob` engine barrel instead of the 245-byte `@mkbabb/glass-ui/blob-config` subpath glass-ui 7.0.0 ships for exactly that purpose, so the whole metaball engine is fetched at 229 ms in the eager boot graph while the "async" SFC arrives at 3271 ms. The documented design intent ("Loading it async splits the whole metaball graph out of the cold-load JS") is measurably false.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Suspects that were disproven and are recorded as negative proofs in the report: the three-parallel-useDark store family is fully cured — `grep -rn "useGlobalDark\|useDark\b" demo/` returns 11 glass-ui singleton sites and zero vueuse instances; HeroBlob's single value.js import `@mkbabb/value.js/math` is a real `package.json#exports` key, correctly aliased in vite.config.ts and mapped in tsconfig.demo.json, writable verbatim by a real consumer — no deep `src/` import exists in the file; dependency direction demo→glass-ui→value.js is correct, proven by `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/color.js:3` importing `@mkbabb/value.js/color`; every producer method called (setMood/pulse/pause/resume) is in the declared `Blob.vue.d.ts` expose surface; `verbatimModuleSyntax` is clean on both type-only imports; Vue 3.5 idioms (useTemplateRef, shallowRef, onScopeDispose) are correct; decorative-a11y ownership (aria-hidden + pointer-events-none + omitted pressLabel) matches the producer's listener-free canvas contract.)

defects.defect: The async split is defeated — the 103 KB glass-ui blob engine barrel is in the eager boot graph because an eager boot composable imports two constants from it instead of from the 245-byte /blob-config subpath glass-ui 7.0.0 ships for that edge.
defects.evidence: demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphere.ts:36 `import { BLOB_CONFIG_KEY, BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/blob";` · `wc -c` → dist/blob.js 103031 B vs dist/blob-config.js 245 B (whose 2-line body re-exports BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS, BLOB_CONFIG_KEY, BLOB_HERO, LIGHTNESS_FLOOR_BRACKET, LIGHTNESS_FLOOR_DEFAULT, clampLightnessFloor) · measured request timeline: 202ms useAtmosphere.ts → 229ms @mkbabb_glass-ui_blob.js → 3271ms demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue · intent falsified at demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:150-157
defects.mechanism: barrel-import over-reach at an eager boundary: a boot module pulls a component barrel for two constants, so a downstream leaf's lazy boundary cannot hold
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/blobgraph.mjs against the live dev server at http://localhost:9000 — prints the request timeline above. Independent confirmation: aborting requests matching /blob\.js|components\/blob/ blanks first paint entirely (fcp 0, lcp 0, canvases [], exactly 1 request blocked), which is impossible if the engine were genuinely deferred.
defects.proposedCure: useAtmosphere.ts and demo/scenes/blob/BlobPane.vue import from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/blob-config`; only HeroBlob.vue (which needs the component) may import `@mkbabb/glass-ui/blob`, and it takes BLOB_CONFIG_KEY from /blob-config too so the heavy edge has exactly one owner. Add a lint rule restricting `@mkbabb/glass-ui/blob` to HeroBlob.vue + demo/scenes/blob/**.

defects.defect: The component's central invariant — |ΔL(bead body, card plate)| ≥ INK_FLOOR (0.15) — is not achieved: measured 0.0174, i.e. 11.6% of the contract. The floor is applied to palette stops while the rendered bead is the shaded output, so it guarantees nothing about the quantity it names.
defects.evidence: HeroBlob.vue:82-93 states the contract and sets INK_FLOOR=0.15; floorStops at :97-111 shifts palette-stop L only. Measured from docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-mobile-light/picker.png (1170×1992): bead-body disc mean OKLab L=0.8565 (n=593), plate annulus mean L=0.8392 (n=2016) → |ΔL|=0.0174, shortfall 0.1326. Point check: bead rgb(234,197,205) L=0.8574 vs plate rgb(239,204,200) L=0.8738 → 0.0164. Shading atoms that dominate the rendered pixel come in via `...appBlobConfig.surface` (HeroBlob.vue:170) from glass-ui presets-5myqNv59.js:39-60 (lit true, specStrength .16, rimStrength .32, iridescence .09, sssScale .1, coreGlow .06).
defects.mechanism: the guarantee is computed on a pre-shading quantity (palette stop L) that is not the quantity the user perceives (shaded body luminance) — a category error in where the invariant is enforced
defects.reproduction: python3 sRGB→OKLab sampler over the committed capture (bead disc r≤55 vs annulus 115≤d≤155 in 1152-space); or load http://localhost:9000/#/?space=lab&color=lab(92%25+88.8+20+/+82.7%25) and sample bead vs plate pixels.
defects.proposedCure: Delete floorStops and INK_FLOOR from the demo. Make the guarantee where the pixel is made: glass-ui already owns the vocabulary (clampLightnessFloor, LIGHTNESS_FLOOR_BRACKET [0.12,0.20], BlobColor.lightnessFloor, deriveBlobPalette({lightnessFloor})). Relay a `contrastAgainstL` option applied post-shading and have the demo pass resolveSurfaceLightnessLive("resting", …) as the reference.

defects.defect: The ink floor never re-derives on dark-mode or ambient change — isDark and inkAmbient are read inside floorStops but neither is a watch source, so the ramp stays floored against a plate that no longer exists.
defects.evidence: HeroBlob.vue:99 reads isDark.value and :98 reads inkAmbient?.value; the only invocations of reseedHeroStops are watch(cssColorOpaqueFrame,…) at :132 and onActivated at :246-250. No watcher on isDark or inkAmbient exists in the file.
defects.mechanism: a derived value implemented as an imperative side effect, so its reactive dependencies are invisible to the scheduler
defects.reproduction: Load /#/ in light mode, do not touch the colour, toggle the dock's dark-mode switch: --saved-bg, the resting-plate tint, isDark and inkAmbient all change; heroStops does not. The stated invariant is void until the user next moves a slider.
defects.proposedCure: Make the ramp a `computed` over (cssColorOpaqueFrame, isDark, inkAmbient, appBlobConfig.color). That also deletes reseedHeroStops, the shallowRef, the try/catch, and the entire onActivated wake-gray branch, since a computed re-evaluates on wake by construction.

defects.defect: Three homes for one concept: the closed-form lightness-separation kernel is duplicated character-for-character between HeroBlob.floorStops and useAtmosphere.guaranteeSeamOffset (differing only in one constant and the container), with a third, semantically different floor in glass-ui. Both demo copies also falsify their own 'internal spread survives' claim.
defects.evidence: HeroBlob.vue:105-110 vs demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphere.ts:~103-111 — identical `let dir = delta >= 0 ? 1 : -1; const need = FLOOR - Math.abs(delta); const headroom = dir === 1 ? 0.98 - meanL : meanL - 0.02; if (headroom < need) dir = -dir; const push = dir * (FLOOR - dir*delta);` then a per-stop `clamp(L + push, 0.02, 0.98)`. useAtmosphere.ts:67 names the copy: 'The same closed-form floor idiom the HeroBlob ink-floor uses'. Third home: glass-ui clampLightnessFloor (presets.d.ts). Stated demo law violated: demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:33-35 'sourced ENTIRELY from the library … the demo carries NO norm/denorm color math'.
defects.mechanism: copy-paste of a pure numeric kernel across module boundaries instead of extracting it to the library that owns colour algebra
defects.reproduction: Spread falsification is pure arithmetic: stops [0.10,0.30,0.50,0.70] with push=+0.30 → [0.40,0.60,0.80,0.98] — the top stop clips, spread compresses 0.60→0.58, and the achieved mean ΔL falls below the nominal floor. No runtime needed.
defects.proposedCure: One primitive, one home: `separateLightness(stops: readonly OklchStop[], referenceL: number, floor: number): OklchStop[]` in src/color/, exported from @mkbabb/value.js/color (pure, DOM-free OKLab algebra, alongside mixColors/safeAccentColor/mapColorToGamut). glass-ui already imports @mkbabb/value.js/color, so the third copy collapses too.

defects.defect: Five producer seams shipped in glass-ui 7.0.0 were not adopted at the W44 whole-adopt; HeroBlob imports two symbols and hand-rolls replacements for the rest. Worse, the `lightnessFloor` booking is undischargeable as written because the producer knob is an absolute stop floor while INK_FLOOR is a bead↔plate separation — a false carry riding the ledger.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/blob.js:1648 exports BLOB_HERO, LIGHTNESS_FLOOR_BRACKET, LIGHTNESS_FLOOR_DEFAULT, clampLightnessFloor; Blob.vue.d.ts:56-70 exposes nudge/settled/settledFrame/rendererStatus; constants.d.ts:43 'the park gate'. HeroBlob.vue:34 imports only {Blob, BLOB_CONFIG_KEY} and hand-rolls: wall-clock park :211-230 (booked at :207-210 against the 5.0.0 adopt — glass-ui is at 7.0.0), hero register :152-178 (booked PRODUCER at :148-149), INK_FLOOR/floorStops :93-111 (booked at :90-92). BLOB_HERO (presets-5myqNv59.js:73-87) vs HeroBlob.vue:160-177 diverge on 7 atoms: bodyRadius .22/.325, orbitRadius .30/.40, satelliteRadius .10/.09, eccentricity .04/.03, satelliteCount 4/3, smoothK .06/.05, fissionAmp 0/.6.
defects.mechanism: consumer-side reimplementation of producer seams outliving the adopt that was supposed to retire it; two objects named 'the hero register' with neither authoritative
defects.reproduction: grep the glass-ui 7.0.0 dist export line and Blob.vue.d.ts expose block against HeroBlob.vue's import at :34 — the shipped surface is a strict superset of what the demo consumes, and each hand-rolled block cites its own booking.
defects.proposedCure: heroConfig = computed(() => ({ ...BLOB_HERO, …only the atoms the picker genuinely overrides })); wall-clock park replaced by watch(() => blobRef.value?.settled, …); owner-ruled register deltas relayed upstream as a BLOB_HERO amendment via the standing BH/BI fond. Requires RULING-1 (re-specify or abrogate the bead↔plate floor) and RULING-2 (which register is canonical).

defects.defect: Renderer health is entirely unhandled — the hero silently vanished in the shipped visual-audit capture with a lost WebGL context, and the demo consumes none of the producer's rendererStatus contract.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json row safari-desktop-light /#/: counts.canvas=1 (every other picker capture: 2), consoleErrors=['WebGL: context lost.'] (the only console error in all 60 captures), settleMs=18905 (every other capture 3277–3606). shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png shows no bead. Producer contract: dist/composables/glass/webgpu/rendererStatus.d.ts (phase initializing|ready|error, engine, adapter, error?), exposed as a ref AND emitted by Blob. `grep -rn "rendererStatus\|renderer-status" demo/` → no output.
defects.mechanism: the component assumes the GL context survives for the page lifetime; a lost context is a normal WebGL event and is observed on this exact route, with no fallback, no placeholder, and no telemetry
defects.reproduction: The committed capture is the reproduction. Synthetically: on /#/, canvas.getContext('webgl2').getExtension('WEBGL_lose_context').loseContext().
defects.proposedCure: Wire @renderer-status on <Blob>; on phase==='error' render the settledFrame still or a plate-toned placeholder (no layout change — the footprint is already reserved by --blob-fp) and surface the row to the debug rail. This consumes a shipped seam rather than adding a mechanism.

defects.defect: tsconfig.demo.json's path map diverges from package.json#exports — 3 phantom keys, 2 missing real keys — so the demo (including HeroBlob's transitive graph) typechecks @mkbabb/value.js/css against an npm-registry tarball while Vite runs the local build, and the two .d.ts files already differ.
defects.evidence: package.json#exports has 7 subpath keys and no '.'; tsconfig.demo.json maps '@mkbabb/value.js' (root), '/parsing', '/units' — `ls dist/subpaths/` shows parsing.d.ts and units.d.ts DO NOT EXIST — and omits '/css' and '/value'. HeroBlob.vue:42 → color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:14 → color-session/ink.ts:8-11 imports parseCssColor/serializeCssColor from '@mkbabb/value.js/css'. package-lock.json resolves @mkbabb/value.js 4.0.0 from https://registry.npmjs.org/. `diff -q node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` → 'Files … differ' (10910 B vs 12490 B).
defects.mechanism: two hand-maintained descriptions of one published surface (TS paths vs the exports-derived Vite alias set) drifting apart, defeating the dist trust boundary the tsconfig header claims to establish
defects.reproduction: ls dist/subpaths/ (no parsing/units), diff the two css.d.ts files, and read tsconfig.demo.json's paths block against package.json#exports.
defects.proposedCure: Generate the tsconfig `paths` block from package.json#exports exactly as vite.config.ts already generates `valueJsSelfAlias`, or fail the typecheck when the two key sets differ. One source of truth for the published surface; both consumers derive from it.

defects.defect: The e2e fixture created specifically to end hand-duplicated blob constants has itself skewed: BEAD_RATIO 0.52 (bodyRadius 0.26) against the live bodyRadius 0.325, so the O-12 occlusion oracle probes a disc 20% smaller than the rendered bead and never tests the annulus that can actually reach the dock band.
defects.evidence: e2e/smoke/fixtures/blob-timing.ts:56-57 `/** Visible bead = 2·bodyRadius·fp (bodyRadius 0.26 — the HERO register). */ export const BEAD_RATIO = 0.52;` vs demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:163 `bodyRadius: 0.325,` and demo/picker/seat.css:10 'bodyRadius 0.325 via HeroBlob's'. Consumer: e2e/smoke/oracles/o12-blob-seat.spec.ts:113 `const r = (BEAD_RATIO / 2) * wrapper.width;` feeding probes at [cx,cy±r] and [cx±0.7r, cy−0.7r]. Fixture header declares its purpose as killing 'a three-file hand-sync waiting to skew'. The 0.26 value is the retired one pinned by tag v-blob-b0-26-ref-w40.
defects.mechanism: a constant restated in three files; two mirrors were updated, the third was not — the fixture's own stated failure mode, realized
defects.reproduction: True bead ratio is 2×0.325=0.65; the oracle uses 0.52. Every probe point lands ≥20% inside the true silhouette, so the outer annulus — the only part that can enter the chrome band — is unprobed and the oracle passes by construction, contradicting its own comment ('corners of the visible bead box').
defects.proposedCure: The fixture must not restate a component constant. Export the hero geometry once (BLOB_HERO after L-5, or a named export from a demo/picker constants module the SFC and the spec both import) and derive BEAD_RATIO from it, so the value cannot be typed twice.

defects.defect: Masking fallback on INK_AMBIENT_KEY — inject(…, null) plus `?? 0.5` — contradicting the key's own documented law and every sibling consumer, and silently substituting the exact mid-lightness the ink-on-tier design exists to abolish.
defects.evidence: HeroBlob.vue:95 `const inkAmbient = inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY, null);` and :98 `const ambient = inkAmbient?.value ?? 0.5;` vs demo/color-session/keys.ts:9-13 (the key's contract) and demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:366 `const ambient = inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY)!;` documented at :363 as 'a missing provider is a wiring defect, surfaced loudly'. The 0.5 guess is the mid-ambient referent retired at useContrastSafeColor.ts:24-31.
defects.mechanism: defensive default swallowing a wiring defect — owner edict 2 (no masking fallbacks)
defects.reproduction: Mount HeroBlob without the boot writer's provide (any standalone/test mount): the ink floor is computed against a plate lightness of 0.5 that exists nowhere in the app, with no error.
defects.proposedCure: inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY)! like every sibling. Moot once L-2's cure lands and the demo stops computing a floor at all — which is the preferred sequencing.

defects.defect: HeroBlob is the only resolveSurfaceLightnessLive consumer that skips the documented bumpProbeEpochOnMount contract, and because its first probe fires during setup it can poison the module-level shared tint cache with a pre-mount value.
defects.evidence: Contract at demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:69-79 ('it must register the mount bump from its setup, or its first (possibly detached/pre-style) probe result caches until some OTHER consumer happens to bump the epoch'). `grep -rn "bumpProbeEpochOnMount" demo/` → ConsoleRail.vue:133, useViewAccents.ts:89, useContrastSafeColor.ts:300 and :348. HeroBlob.vue:99 calls resolveSurfaceLightnessLive and never bumps. Cache: useContrastSafeColor.ts:240-251 keys liveTintCache on (darkClass, epoch) at module scope.
defects.mechanism: a shared reactive instrument whose correctness depends on a per-caller ritual — an API that can be forgotten will be forgotten
defects.reproduction: HeroBlob's floorStops runs from watch(…, {immediate:true}) at :132, i.e. during setup before mount; the resulting tint is written into the module-level liveTintCache under the then-current epoch where later readers pick it up. demo/scenes/about/markdown/composables/useMarkdownColors.ts:44 has the same omission — a family, not a one-off.
defects.proposedCure: Replace the exported resolveSurfaceLightnessLive + bumpProbeEpochOnMount pair with one composable, useSurfaceLightness(surface): ComputedRef<number>, that registers the bump itself. The ritual becomes unforgettable because it no longer exists.

defects.defect: One-way :paused binding on a component that declares v-model:paused and emits update:paused — the producer's return channel is dropped, so the demo keeps a shadow pause state the engine cannot correct, voiding the producer's 'no parallel pause path' guarantee.
defects.evidence: HeroBlob.vue:17 `:paused="blobPaused"` with no @update:paused listener anywhere in the file, while HeroBlob.vue:249, :314-315 also drive the imperative resume()/pause() half. Producer contract at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/blob/Blob.vue.d.ts:35-43 ('v-model:paused … wire its @update:paused to this v-model … The imperative pause()/resume() defineExpose handles bind the SAME renderer seam (no parallel pause path); the prop owns the default') and the declared emit "update:paused" at :69.
defects.mechanism: consumer refuses a two-way contract's return channel while also driving its imperative half — two writers, one seam, no reconciliation
defects.reproduction: Any producer-originated pause state change (a WCAG pause control wired to the Blob, or an engine self-park) emits update:paused, which HeroBlob discards; blobPaused then re-asserts the demo's stale opinion on its next write.
defects.proposedCure: v-model:paused="blobPaused". One line; it makes the demo's state a mirror of the engine's rather than a competing opinion.

defects.defect: A string-literal contract spanning the feature→boot boundary (the 'blob-emerge' animation name) whose mismatch fails silently, plus a global keyframe living outside demo/styles/ in violation of the animations edict.
defects.evidence: HeroBlob.vue:311-312 `if (e.animationName !== "blob-emerge") return;` against the keyframe defined at demo/color-picker/composables/boot/overture.css:167, which documents the hazard itself at :163-166 ('renaming … separately in HeroBlob.vue'). Placement: `grep -rl "@keyframes" demo/ | grep "\.css$"` returns exactly two files — demo/color-picker/composables/boot/overture.css and demo/styles/animations.css — so overture.css is the sole global-keyframe definer outside demo/styles/.
defects.mechanism: an untyped string as the sole coupling between two modules in different layers, with a bare `return` as the failure mode
defects.reproduction: Rename the keyframe in either file and the T.W4.5-R2 backing-store re-measure stops firing with no error, no warning and no failing test — the guard just returns.
defects.proposedCure: Move the keyframe to demo/styles/animations.css (moved, never deleted — edict 6) and export `const BLOB_EMERGE = "blob-emerge"` from one TS module that both the CSS-adjacent code and the SFC import, so the string exists exactly once.

defects.defect: On both mobile matrices the blob canvas is the only element in the picker capture that extends past the right viewport edge, an invariant nothing owns or asserts.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json, safari-mobile-light /#/ and safari-mobile-dark /#/: "bleeding": ["canvas.goo-blob-canvas"] with overflowX: 0. Definition at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/capture.mjs:107-111 — getBoundingClientRect().right > documentElement.clientWidth + 1. seat.css:2-6 legislates only the card-edge case ('only the transparent 1.6× canvas overscan crosses the card edge, clipped by .app-layout').
defects.mechanism: a 1.6× overscan canvas whose containment is specified against the card but never against the viewport, on the narrowest layout
defects.reproduction: Read the two mobile rows in REPORT.json; e2e/smoke/mobile/blob-presence-mobile.spec.ts:80 asserts canvas size against CANVAS_OVERSCAN * seatFootprintPx(paneWidth) and never checks the viewport edge, so nothing gates it.
defects.proposedCure: State the viewport-containment invariant explicitly in seat.css's law and assert it in the mobile presence spec, or clamp the overscan at the <lg rung. Currently cosmetic (the overscan is transparent) but unowned.

defects.defect: The imported component named `Blob` shadows the DOM `Blob` global inside this SFC, so InstanceType<typeof Blob> would silently degrade to the DOM file type if the import were ever renamed or removed.
defects.evidence: HeroBlob.vue:34 `import { Blob, BLOB_CONFIG_KEY } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/blob";` and :58 `useTemplateRef<InstanceType<typeof Blob>>("blobRef")`.
defects.mechanism: a producer component name colliding with a Web IDL global constructor
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis about a latent failure mode; no current defect. Removing the import today would make `typeof Blob` resolve to the DOM constructor rather than erroring cleanly.
defects.proposedCure: Producer-side naming relay (BlobOrnament would be unambiguous) via the standing BH fond. No demo action required beyond awareness.

defects.defect: The chronic gate riding this component (Q14 / CH-4) is specified on LCP, but the measured defect is TBT and eager bytes — a wave born against CH-4 as written can close GREEN without curing anything.
defects.evidence: Measured Chromium / CPU 4× / dev server / 1440×900 / n=3 medians: with HeroBlob mounted FCP 1108ms, LCP 1108ms, TBT 1663ms, longest task 857ms; with the HeroBlob module request aborted (engine still downloaded) FCP 968ms, LCP 968ms, TBT 866ms, longest 728ms → Δ LCP +140ms, Δ TBT +797ms. Second independent run: LCP median 1056ms, TBT median 1450ms. CH-4 reads 'p75 LCP ≤2.5s on the named matrix — the ~5s boot dies or V′ does not close'; the Q14 figures were LCP 5141 / TBT 5988.
defects.mechanism: a gate quantity chosen from a historical symptom rather than from the component's actual cost profile
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/blobperf.mjs (RUNS=3 CPU=4) against http://localhost:9000 — prints both arms. Caveat stated in the report: this is Chromium/dev/4×-CPU/desktop; the real-Safari signal is worse (settleMs 18905 on safari-desktop-light /#/ with the L-6 context loss), so the production Safari matrix must be re-measured before the bars are frozen.
defects.proposedCure: Re-specify the wave gates on the sick axis: HB-2 requires Δ(TBT with blob − without) ≤ 250 ms on a fixed rig (n≥5, median), and HB-1 requires no glass-ui_blob.js request before the HeroBlob module request. Keep an LCP watch, but do not let it stand as the closing gate.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue (area demo/picker)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M context) — matches the seat's explicit declaration; no inherited/undeclared seat. Seat named HEAD c654824e; working tree had advanced to e79fcd43, but HeroBlob.vue is byte-identical between them — all measurements are against e79fcd43.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the ink floor is bought by destroying 68% of the picked chroma: floorStops() (HeroBlob.vue:97-111) shifts every stop's OKLCh L AFTER deriveBlobPalette has already centred the ramp on the seed's L and gamut-mapped it, so the bead lands at the right lightness and the wrong colour. Live ramp read out of the running app: maxC 0.0890 against a seed C 0.2725 (32.7%). The producer's shipped `bodyLightness` option returns maxC 0.2725 at the SAME body lightness — 3.1× recovery. The hero ornament, whose sole purpose is to make the picked colour flesh, renders mid-mauve grey in light and near-white cream in dark; in neither scheme is it the picked colour.

defects.defect: floorStops() applies its OKLab-L push AFTER deriveBlobPalette has centred the ramp on the seed L and gamut-mapped it. The seed's L is where its chroma lives; the post-hoc shift moves the ramp off that L without re-deriving, so the ink floor is paid for with 68% of the picked chroma. The hero bead is never the picked colour.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:97-111 + :117-130. LIVE stops read from the running app (probe C3, .goo-blob-wrapper.__vueParentComponent.props.config.color.paletteStops): ["#c384a6","#c3a4ab","#c4bbbb","#c4bbb9"] → OKLCh L 0.6872/C 0.0890, L 0.7482/C 0.0375, L 0.7994/C 0.0102, L 0.7989/C 0.0106; maxC 0.0890. Seed at that moment lab(92% 88.8 20) = L 0.9583 C 0.2725 → 32.7% chroma retained. Offline byte-exact reproduction: shipped path → maxC 0.0879 (#c384a6 #c3a3ab #c4bbbb #c4bbb9); deriveBlobPalette(css,{bodyLightness:0.65}) → maxC 0.2725 (#f60bb2 #ff6198 #ff8e93 #ffb19e) at a LOWER body L (0.65 vs 0.6875). bodyLightness is shipped: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/color/index.d.ts:122-131. Corroborated by docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-dark/picker.png (near-white cream bead for a hot-pink pick).
defects.mechanism: post-hoc mutation of an already-gamut-mapped derivation instead of parameterising the derivation
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/picker-heroblob/probe-C3-stops-and-realloss.mjs (section `stops.before`), plus: node --input-type=module -e "import {cssToOklch,deriveBlobPalette,oklchStopToHex} from '@mkbabb/glass-ui/color'; const s=cssToOklch('lab(92% 88.8 20)'); const a=deriveBlobPalette('lab(92% 88.8 20)',{stopCount:4,harmony:'analogous',chromaCeiling:Math.max(0.16,s.C)}); const b=deriveBlobPalette('lab(92% 88.8 20)',{stopCount:4,harmony:'analogous',bodyLightness:0.65}); console.log(Math.max(...a.map(x=>x.C)), Math.max(...b.map(x=>x.C)))" → 0.0879 0.2725
defects.proposedCure: Delete floorStops and INK_FLOOR. Compute the target body lightness from the live plate (plateL ± ink floor) and pass it as deriveBlobPalette's shipped `bodyLightness`, with `lightnessFloor: clampLightnessFloor()` (also shipped, presets.d.ts). The ink floor becomes an INPUT to a gamut-correct derivation instead of a post-hoc mutilation of one. This single transposition also dissolves C-2 and C-13.

defects.defect: The ink floor never re-derives on a scheme flip. floorStops reads isDark.value and inkAmbient.value from inside a WATCH CALLBACK whose only tracked source is cssColorOpaqueFrame, so a dark<->light toggle (or ambient drift) cannot re-run the derive — the component keeps whichever answer it computed first.
defects.evidence: HeroBlob.vue:98-99 (reads) inside the callback of HeroBlob.vue:132 `watch(cssColorOpaqueFrame, (css) => reseedHeroStops(css), { immediate: true })`. Probe C3: "stopsUnchangedAcrossFlip": true — before and afterFlip are byte-identical ["#c384a6","#c3a4ab","#c4bbbb","#c4bbb9"]; only afterColourChange moves (["#ac5987","#d26082","#eb7378","#f3937a"]). Probe C2 measured the resting plate composited OKLab L: light 0.8079, dark 0.3511; with pickL 0.7862 the light decision is {delta -0.0217, pushes true} and the dark decision is {delta 0.4351, pushes false} — the two schemes demand different ramps. Residual |ΔL| after a dark→light flip = 0.0217, i.e. 7× below the 0.15 ink floor the F-4 cure (HeroBlob.vue:81-93) exists to guarantee.
defects.mechanism: reactive referent sampled inside a non-reactive callback — reactivity that cannot fire
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/picker-heroblob/probe-C3-stops-and-realloss.mjs and probe-C2-gl-loss-and-inkfloor.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Make heroStops a computed over (cssColorOpaqueFrame, isDark, inkAmbient) — or, after C-1's cure, let the floor be an argument to the derive and the derive be the computed. The referent must be tracked, not sampled.

defects.defect: The hero ornament's mount is transitively gated on ANOTHER canvas's WebGL success: b4 ← b2 ← auroraArrived ← !contextLost on the ATMOSPHERE canvas. A context loss before b2 latches deletes the hero blob for the whole session, and there is no context-loss handling anywhere in the blob chain — no honest terminal, no rendererStatus subscription, no recovery.
defects.evidence: Chain read-confirmed: demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphere.ts:321-324 (auroraArrived = (mode==='css' || isArmed) && !contextLost) → demo/color-picker/App.vue:296 → demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useOverture.ts:106-118 (b2 latch-once) → :152-156 (b4) → demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:94 (v-if="blobReady && ornamentOpen"). `grep -o "webglcontextlost|webglcontextrestored|context lost|isContextLost" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/blob.js` → NO OUTPUT (zero hits in the shipped producer bundle). `grep -rn "webglcontextlost" demo/` → only useAtmosphere.ts:298,301 (the sibling surface HAS the honest terminal, :283-310). Observed instance, REPORT.json /#/: safari-desktop-light settle 18905 canvas 1 consoleErrors ["WebGL: context lost."] vs the other three matrices settle ~3300 canvas 2 consoleErrors []. shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png shows NO bead. The producer renders its canvas unconditionally (blob.js: D("canvas",{class:"goo-blob-canvas"}) with no v-if), so canvas 2→1 means the whole subtree never mounted.
defects.mechanism: cross-surface mount coupling + a WebGL consumer with no loss/restore path
defects.reproduction: PARTIAL — the observed failure is the recorded Safari capture (REPORT.json /#/ safari-desktop-light + shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png). I could NOT force it in Chromium: probe-C2 (synthetic webglcontextlost @400ms), probe-C3 (WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext @400/900ms), probe-C4 (getContext patched pre-boot, loss @500/1000/3000ms) all left b2 latching normally (overture:b2@1360..1502) and the blob mounted (canvasCount 2). C4's ctxLog shows the app's first webgl2 context is created at ~126-175ms on a canvas with empty className, so the atmosphere key never matched. The source chain is confirmed by read; the Safari trigger is not yet pinned.
defects.proposedCure: Two independent moves: (a) gate b4 on paint-completion rather than the field's GPU arrival — b3Complete ∧ dockLanded already satisfies the beat DAG's stated order, so the ornament stops depending on an unrelated GPU surface; (b) give the blob the atmosphere's honest terminal by subscribing the producer's SHIPPED `rendererStatus` expose, and on a non-ok status keep the .hero-blob-anchor::before contact shadow as the seated ornament instead of nothing.

defects.defect: The blob engine mount is 100% of the picker route's measured Total Blocking Time — a single indivisible 397ms main-thread task. Separately, the standing Q14 escalation number (LCP 5141ms) does not reproduce on this matrix: LCP measures 264ms.
defects.evidence: Probe C1 (Chromium 1440x900 DPR2, warm dev server, unthrottled): fcpMs 264, lcpMs 264, cls 0.0193, longTaskCount 2, longTaskTotalMs 531, longestTaskMs 397, tbtAfterFcpMs 347, top5Tasks [{startMs:2321,durMs:397},{startMs:84,durMs:134}], overtureMarks b0@7 b1@175 b3@595 b2@1296 b4@2308. TBT 347 === 397-50 EXACTLY — the blob mount is the entire contributor. Probe C4 ctxLog independently timestamps the blob's own context: ('webgl2','goo-blob-canvas',2410,True), inside that task. Backing store healthy: blobBacking 360x360, blobCss 180.2x180.2, dpr 2, ratio 0.999 (O-12·5 floor is 0.6).
defects.mechanism: one indivisible WebGL2 context + shader-compile init task on the main thread; deferral relocates it but cannot remove it
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/picker-heroblob/probe-C1-boot.mjs
defects.proposedCure: Re-state the chronic row instead of inheriting it. The eager-boot framing is stale — the chunk IS deferred (ColorPicker.vue:157-158 defineAsyncComponent + useIdleReady) and the mount IS beat-gated past the field's arrival. The honest born-RED gate is `longestTask(blob mount) <= 150ms` OR `TBT <= 100ms on /#/`, measured with probe-C1-boot.mjs, and it is a PRODUCER row (shader precompile / armAsync chunking, the L20 eager-config/lazy-engine split), not a demo placement row. Any wave spec born-RED against '5141ms' is born against a number nobody can currently measure.

defects.defect: The shared e2e fixture's bead ratio drifted: BEAD_RATIO = 0.52 (bodyRadius 0.26) while the HERO register ships bodyRadius 0.325 (ratio 0.65). O-12's occlusion probes therefore sample a circle 20% short in radius and never touch the bead's real arc — the exact thing the oracle exists to prove.
defects.evidence: e2e/smoke/fixtures/blob-timing.ts:56-57 `/** Visible bead = 2·bodyRadius·fp (bodyRadius 0.26 — the HERO register). */ export const BEAD_RATIO = 0.52;` vs demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:163 `bodyRadius: 0.325`. test/picker-blob-config.test.ts:26 WAS updated to 0.325; the e2e fixture was not. Sole consumer e2e/smoke/oracles/o12-blob-seat.spec.ts:113 `const r = (BEAD_RATIO / 2) * wrapper.width;` = 0.26·w. At the measured seat (fp = 112.6px; probe C6 blobBox 180x180 = 1.6·fp) the probes sample r = 29.3px around a bead of true radius 36.6px — 20% short in radius, 36% short in area. Retired value named by the tag `v-blob-b0-26-ref-w40`. The fixture's own header (:2-6) advertises itself as the cure for 'a three-file hand-sync waiting to skew'.
defects.mechanism: a hand-synced constant in a fixture that claims to be the single source of truth
defects.reproduction: grep -n 'BEAD_RATIO' e2e/smoke/fixtures/blob-timing.ts e2e/smoke/oracles/o12-blob-seat.spec.ts; grep -n 'bodyRadius' demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue
defects.proposedCure: Derive BEAD_RATIO from the same authority the unit test asserts (2·bodyRadius), or better: have the oracle read the rendered bead extent rather than re-encode a config literal in a second place. A constant that must be hand-synced with a component literal is the defect, not its current value.

defects.defect: The component's only unit test is a regex over the raw .vue text. One template attribute edit deletes the entire HERO register, the ink floor, the fission arming and the quality rung while every assertion stays green. floorStops — the function with two separate defects above — has no test of any kind.
defects.evidence: test/picker-blob-config.test.ts:1-53 — readFileSync of demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue, then string assertions (bodyRadius: 0.325, orbitRadius: 0.4, satelliteRadius: 0.09, eccentricity: 0.03, aria-hidden, no @click, no writeClipboard). EXACT green-keeping mutation: change HeroBlob.vue:15 `:config="heroConfig"` to `:config="appBlobConfig"`. The heroConfig computed (:152-178) becomes dead code, its literals stay in the file, all four toMatch assertions still pass — and the blob reverts to BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS (stock warm-cream meatball, fissionAmp 0, full quality on phones). Zero tests fail. Weaker equivalents: delete floorStops + INK_FLOOR outright, set INK_FLOOR to 0, invert the dir flip, drop the onActivated re-seed.
defects.mechanism: source-text assertions standing in for behavioural assertions — a vacuous gate
defects.reproduction: Apply the diff `- :config="heroConfig"` / `+ :config="appBlobConfig"` to demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:15 and run `npx vitest run test/picker-blob-config.test.ts` — it passes.
defects.proposedCure: Retire the regex file. Mount HeroBlob in a component test with a stub Blob and assert the CONFIG OBJECT it emits (geometry tuple, surface.fissionAmp, quality at both viewport rungs, and the derived paletteStops for a known seed against known plate lightnesses in both schemes). That single test kills the vacuity and covers C-1, C-2, C-8 and C-13 by construction.

defects.defect: Oracle O-12·3 asserts the parked bead visibly answers a hover within 400ms. HeroBlob wires no hover beat and renders no pointer host, so the mechanism cannot fire — measured 0 GL draw calls across a 2s sustained sweep over the bead.

defects.defect: `chromaCeiling: Math.max(0.16, seed.C)` is inert — a cap set above the derivation's natural output. The comment asserting 'a C 0.23 pick now derives a C 0.23 ramp' is false.

defects.defect: Two masking fallbacks (edict 2: no masking fallbacks). A bare catch{} swallows every parser throw on the picker's hot path, and inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY, null) ?? 0.5 silently fabricates an ambient the app's own law says must fail loudly.

The producer's contract at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/color/index.d.ts:57-59 is explicit: 'Invalid, contextual, and non-opaque inputs throw one GlassColorError carrying the parser diagnostics… No catch-to-default recovery occurs at this boundary.' Second: HeroBlob.vue:95 `inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY, null)` + :98 `inkAmbient?.value ?? 0.5`, against demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:347 `const ambient = inject(INK_AMBIENT_KEY)!` with the docblock at :342-343 'a missing provider is a wiring defect, surfaced loudly'. defects.defect: The colour string is parsed twice on every rAF-coalesced frame: cssToOklch(css) purely to read seed.C, then deriveBlobPalette(css, …) which parses the same string again — although the API accepts the already-parsed OklchStop.
