defects.defect: One ornament is described by five different sizes and none of them is its painted mass; its canvas box escapes the card on all four sides and escapes the viewport at 390.
defects.evidence: Live measurement (scratchpad/HBD-geo.json), 1440: canvas 180.19x180.19 at (564.59,113.72,right 744.78) vs card (199,147.5,right 711) — 33.78px overhang on every side at z-index 20; layout footprint --blob-fp 112.63 (seat.css:43); padding reservation 93.12px (seat.css:88); min-height reservation 73.12px (seat.css:89); rendered painted body diameter 75.09px. At 390: canvasOverViewportRight = +17.59px — reproducing REPORT.json's "bleeding":["canvas.goo-blob-canvas"] in BOTH mobile matrices. Footprint = 112/358 = 31.3% of the card width; padding = 93.12/327.38 = 28.4% of the title row.
defects.mechanism: The producer's 1.6x canvas overscan was never reconciled with the seat's layout footprint, and the two hand-written reservations (0.76*fp padding, 0.76*fp-0.75rem min-height) were sized from the footprint rather than from the painted body. PR-03: "Blob reserves more than its painted mass".
defects.reproduction: scratchpad/HBD-probe5.mjs — evaluates getBoundingClientRect for .hero-blob-anchor, canvas.goo-blob-canvas, .pane-shell and .title-row at 1440/390/720@2x and reports canvas.right - documentElement.clientWidth.
defects.proposedCure: Collapse five numbers to one. Let the footprint token BE the painted body diameter and have the producer's overscan resolve inside it (a producer row: the overscan should not be a consumer-visible box). Then the reservation is arithmetic on the same token instead of a hand-tuned 0.76 factor, and overflow is impossible by construction rather than by an ancestor's overflow:hidden.

defects.defect: The Blob-derived vertical minimum the constitution says must not exist is still in the sheet and binds at 390 and at 200% zoom; PR-03's centre-ward displacement is unimplemented; and the constitution's own G token is not wired anywhere in the live picker.
defects.evidence: seat.css:89 min-height: calc(0.76*var(--blob-fp) - 0.75rem) -> 73.12px. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7: "no Blob-derived minimum block size enters it"; PROPORTION-AUDIT §2: "Both vertical reservations must die". Binding table (live): 1440 title-row h 84.97 (not binding); 720@2x h 73.11 = min-height 73.12 with label ink only 59.77 tall -> 13.3px of pure ornament reservation; 390 h 73.11 (binding). Label-bottom -> headline-top gap: 70.42px at 1440, 78.72px at 200% zoom, vs the §3.2 ceiling I_after <= phi*G ~= 14.87px. seat.css:47 --blob-seat: 0px and anchor.x/y == card.x/y (flush corner) vs PR-03's "one title-gap toward chassis center". A live walk of every element found --instrument-title-gap defined on ZERO nodes.
defects.mechanism: The ornament dictates the type layout instead of being seated by it; and the producer token that the law's inequality is defined against (P122's --instrument-title-gap) was never consumed, so the law has no live referent.
defects.reproduction: scratchpad/HBD-probe5.mjs (titleRowMinHeight, titleRowRect, labToNumGap at the three arms) and scratchpad/HBD-gap.mjs (walks document.querySelectorAll('*') reading --instrument-title-gap; returns []).
defects.proposedCure: Delete both seat.css reservations and let the ornament be positioned against the settled header band rather than reserving space inside it — the ornament is absolutely positioned already, so it contributes no flow height and the reservation is purely manual. Wire --instrument-title-gap from P122 so G exists, then the I_after inequality becomes measurable instead of notional. NOTE, so the wave does not over-charge: at 1440 the 70.42px void is NOT the blob's — its owner there is the readout box (122.4px tall around a 67px number), PR-01's second named cause.

defects.defect: The emerge pose and the engine arm are sequenced backwards, and the repair for that inversion uses a pause seam as a resize API and lands a 537ms long task.
defects.evidence: overture.css:167-178 animates .hero-blob-anchor from scale(0.35) AFTER HeroBlob mounts; HeroBlob.vue:297-316 onEmergeEnd fires pause();resume() to force a backing-store re-measure, conceding "resume() re-measures via idempotent resize() on the was-suspended path". defineExpose offers nudge,setMood,pulse,currentMood,pause,resume,settled,settledFrame,rendererStatus — there is no resize. Cost: at CPU 4x the blob arm shows a 537ms long task at t=3802ms; the reduced-motion arm (where the pose is no-preference-wrapped so onEmergeEnd never fires) shows no late long task at all — [154,799][1222,405][1627,55][1858,482][2353,67], all <=2.4s.
defects.mechanism: The engine arms inside a container that is actively lying about its box, so it presizes from a transformed gBCR (measured historically at dpr2: 126x126 backing for a 180.2px box) and the idle park freezes the low-res frame; the consumer then repairs the consequence instead of removing the cause.
defects.reproduction: scratchpad/HBD-probe3.mjs at CPU=4 vs scratchpad/HBD-probe4-prm.mjs at CPU=4; compare longTasks. ATTRIBUTION OF THE 537ms TASK IS A STRONGLY-SUPPORTED INFERENCE (one-arm correlation), not a direct trace — labelled as such in the report.
defects.proposedCure: Invert the order: animate an EMPTY settled seat and arm the engine at the pose's end, not before it. That single inversion deletes onEmergeEnd, the animationName filter, the park guard, the pause/resume pair and its 30-line comment; it moves GL init out of the critical band; and it is verbatim what CARRY-LEDGER W54 already asks for — "D-2 blob truthful lifecycle; arm-after-critical-paint 0px".

defects.defect: Two idle state machines race, and three consumer mechanisms self-documented as interims pending producer seams are now two major versions stale — the seams shipped.
defects.evidence: Producer glass-ui@7.0.0: constants.d.ts IDLE_SLEEP_MS = 6000 ("Idle timeout after which the blob drifts to sleepy") and REST_EPS = 0.001 ("the at-rest epsilon ... the park gate"); Blob.vue.d.ts:63-64 exposes settled and settledFrame; types.d.ts:121-129 ships BlobColor.lightnessFloor "Bounded to [0.12, 0.20] OKLab L ... default 0.15". Consumer: HeroBlob.vue:211-212 re-implements idle at 2000ms + 3300ms with two setTimeouts and a manual setMood('sleepy'), plus a cross-file constant contract into e2e/smoke/fixtures/blob-timing.ts; :93 hardcodes INK_FLOOR = 0.15. The file names both: :206-210 "the demo INTERIM; the producer settled/park-from-quiescence seam (GAP-L5, booked at the 5.0.0 adopt)"; :90-92 "The producer F9.R1 lightnessFloor knob replaces this at the W7 adopt (BOOKED)".
defects.mechanism: Interim mechanisms with no expiry check; the booked replacement conditions were met at 5.0.0 and 7.0.0 respectively and nothing swept them. Two idle machines (2000ms consumer vs 6000ms producer) now drive the same mood surface with different constants.
defects.reproduction: node -p "require('./node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json').version" -> 7.0.0; grep -n 'IDLE_SLEEP_MS\|REST_EPS' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/blob/constants.d.ts; grep -n 'settled\|lightnessFloor' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/blob/*.d.ts
defects.proposedCure: Sweep all three interims in one cut: delete BLOB_IDLE_MS/SLEEPY_POSE_MS/idleTimer/poseTimer/noteBlobActivity for the producer's settled read; delete INK_FLOOR/floorStops for lightnessFloor+bodyLightness; delete the e2e blob-timing.ts constant mirror with them. Edict 2 (no legacy, no dual paths) and edict 4 (glass-ui is the design system) both bite here, and the deletion is roughly half the file.

defects.defect: forced-colors is undesigned: every glass surface correctly flattens to the user's palette while the WebGL bead keeps full colour, becoming the single most chromatic and highest-weight object on an otherwise monochrome page.
defects.evidence: grep -rn 'forced-colors' demo/picker/ demo/color-picker/composables/boot/ -> no matches. Captured live in Chromium with forcedColors:'active' (scratchpad/HBD-forced-colors-full.png): card, dock, sliders and inputs all flatten to white with 1px black borders; the bead renders its full pink 3-D shading unchanged. NOTE: the tracked shots/forced-colors-desktop/picker.png is NOT a valid witness — WebKit ignores the flag, which is why that capture still shows full glass.
defects.mechanism: Canvas content is exempt from forced-colors by spec, so an ornament that opts into WebGL opts out of the user's palette; nothing in the seat suppresses or flattens it for users who chose a reduced-complexity, high-contrast mode.
defects.reproduction: scratchpad/HBD-fc.mjs — chromium.launch(); newContext({forcedColors:'active'}); goto /#/?space=lab&color=...; screenshot.
defects.proposedCure: @media (forced-colors: active) suppresses the ornament and its contact shadow entirely, in glass-ui at the Blob root (root-level styling, edict 5) rather than per-instance in demo seat.css. Pairs naturally with D-6's CSS-ground specimen: in forced colors the ground specimen is what remains, which is exactly correct.

defects.defect: The seat positions the ornament with physical properties in a chrome/layout role the constitution assigns to logical direction.
defects.evidence: seat.css:52-53 `top: var(--blob-seat); right: var(--blob-seat);` and seat.css:88 `padding-right: calc(0.76*var(--blob-fp) + 0.5rem)`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1: "chrome, navigation and layout — logical inline/block direction follows the document". Witness: shots/rtl-desktop/picker-postload.png — the whole scene mirrors, the bead does not, so the ornament becomes the LEADING element of the header band instead of its terminal one.
defects.mechanism: Two physical properties that currently agree; the composition survives RTL only by that coincidence. Fixing either one alone puts the identity label under the bead.
defects.reproduction: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/rtl-desktop/picker-postload.png (states.mjs applies dir=rtl post-load per MT-F022 #1).
defects.proposedCure: inset-inline-end / padding-inline-end, changed together in one edit, and re-judged as a composition: decide deliberately whether the ornament is the band's leading or terminal element in RTL rather than inheriting whichever the physical property happens to give.

defects.defect: A bare catch swallows every error class on the component's only source of colour truth, behind a comment that is factually wrong about what throws.
defects.evidence: HeroBlob.vue:118 `const seed = cssToOklch(css); // throws iff un-parseable` and :127-129 `catch { /* A transient un-parseable colour string leaves the last good ramp. */ }`. Proven false: node --input-type=module -e "const m=await import('@mkbabb/glass-ui/color'); m.cssToOklch('lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)')" -> GlassColorError: cssToOklch: color_non_opaque { code:'color_non_opaque', alpha:0.827 }.
defects.mechanism: An undiscriminating catch makes 'stale ramp' indistinguishable from 'correct ramp'; a producer regression in cssToOklch or deriveBlobPalette would degrade the hero silently and permanently with no console trace.
defects.reproduction: The node one-liner above. (The current wiring is safe — cssColorOpaque is withAlpha(color,1) at demo/color-session/useColorPipeline.ts:104 — so this is a latent trap plus a wrong comment, not a live break.)
defects.proposedCure: Discriminate: let the derivation run without a guard and let the boundary that owns colour parsing report failure through the same rendererStatus/diagnostics channel D-6 introduces. If a stale-ramp fallback is genuinely wanted, it must be an explicit, observable state, not an empty catch block.

defects.defect: Render quality is forked on a media-query breakpoint inside a seat whose own law forbids band arms and whose geometry is container-scaled.
defects.evidence: HeroBlob.vue:177 `quality: isLgViewport.value ? appBlobConfig.quality : "half"` via useBreakpoint("(min-width: 1024px)") at :71. seat.css:14 declares "ONE cqi FORMULA at every viewport (no band arms)". VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.7: "No desktop-tight/mobile-airy fork and no breakpoint pile."
defects.mechanism: Two scaling authorities in one component — the footprint is container-relative (22cqi) while the render budget is viewport-relative (min-width:1024px) — so a 512px pane on a 1440 desktop and a 358px card on a 390 phone get different quality for near-identical rendered sizes (footprint 112.63 vs 112.00).
defects.reproduction: scratchpad/HBD-geo.json: anchor.w 112.63 at 1440 and 112.00 at 390 — same painted size, different quality rung.
defects.proposedCure: Derive the quality rung from the same container measure the footprint uses (or from the producer's own DPR/fill-rate budget), so one authority scales the ornament. If a device-class signal is genuinely needed it belongs in the producer's budget resolver, not in a consumer media query.

defects.defect: heroConfig reallocates four nested objects per coalesced colour frame, inside the 12ms drag budget its own sibling comment invokes as the reason to avoid iteration.
defects.evidence: HeroBlob.vue:152-178 — the computed spreads appBlobConfig plus fresh `geometry`, `surface` and `color` objects on every heroStops write, i.e. once per rAF-coalesced colour frame during a scrub. HeroBlob.vue:84-87 invokes "the 12ms drag headroom (PI-3 — this runs in the exact rAF-coalesced fan-out drag-frame-budget measures; an iterative solve here is forbidden)".
defects.mechanism: The config object is rebuilt whole to change one array, so the producer re-reads an entirely new object graph each frame.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a hypothesis about allocation cost; no per-frame allocation measurement was taken. Structural read only.
defects.proposedCure: Falls out of D-1: once the palette policy moves to the producer via bodyLightness, heroStops disappears and the hero register becomes a static object built once, with only the seed colour flowing per frame.

defects.defect: The file is a tranche ledger wearing a component's clothes: 317 lines, ~180 of them comment, six machines, three self-declared interims whose replacements have shipped.
defects.evidence: wc -l demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue = 317. Six machines: ramp derivation (:117-132), ink floor (:93-111), config overlay (:152-178), idle/park timers (:211-230), mood bindings (:252-295), emerge re-measure (:297-316), plus the KeepAlive wake (:246-250). Cross-references to W6-4, T-49c, boot-B, §0.3, PI-3, GAP-L5, D8, WR-2, S.W3, T.W4.5 R2, BD.W-GOOBLOB-MERCURY-COLONY.
defects.mechanism: Every cure in the component's history was added beside the previous one with its provenance narrated in place; nothing was ever removed when its condition expired.
defects.reproduction: NONE — qualitative reading, offered as an observation rather than a measured defect.
defects.proposedCure: Not a god module in the edict-1 sense (it is one component), but the accumulated-interim shape is what edict 1 exists to prevent. The cures in D-1/D-2/D-3/D-9/D-10 delete roughly half the file; what should come out the other side is ~120 lines that say what the ornament is FOR rather than narrating what it has survived.
